## DECISION F044 D8 — T003's bundle-size budget lands first: `apps/ui`'s own baseline plus 10%, keyed by each built asset's stable name with vite's own content hash stripped, its breach naming every chunk that grew; the first-paint and 60fps budgets, and the pre-existing drift in `docs/system/ci-self-check-v1.md`, move to the rounds that add the Chrome trace harness (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: `docs/roadmap/features/T5_F044.md` T003 asks for three budgets — first paint < 1.5s, 60fps p95 at 200 nodes and a bundle-size cap — each recorded with numbers and each breach naming its regression source; `docs/ui/design_reference/acceptance_criteria.md` §5 fixes the bundle rule as "size-limit cap set at current build +10%". `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py` already holds the pattern this budget follows: a pure judging function fed an observation, unit-tested without a subprocess, with exactly one `@pytest.mark.subprocess` test that takes the real reading; `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py` is already one of the seven `test_paths` of the `budgets` CI stage (`packages/orchestration/ci_stages.py`), so this round adds no stage and registers no new path. A fresh `vite build --outDir <tmp> --emptyOutDir` of `apps/ui`, run by the reviewer at this decision's own commit range and never into the shared `apps/ui/dist` (DECISION F039 D9), produced six files: `index.html` 414 bytes, `assets/index-CtYeOS0T.css` 83758 bytes, `assets/diffHighlightGrammars-o9XqnLhb.js` 1695 bytes, `assets/index-BKD2HAVk.js` 783940 bytes, `story/story-player.css` 11940 bytes and `story/story-player.js` 266239 bytes (the story player is `apps/ui/vite.config.ts`'s own `closeBundle` hook, DECISION F039 D9, so it always joins the same `vite build`) — 1147986 bytes total. Vite names every hashed chunk `<name>-<hash>.<ext>`, and the hash changes on every incidental rebuild whose bytes did not change in a way that matters, so a baseline keyed by the raw filename would misread every such rebuild as a chunk born at its full size.

CHOSEN: `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py` gains `normalize_chunk_name` (strips a vite content-hash segment — a run of 6 to 10 letters, digits or underscores, containing at least one digit, directly before the extension, which is what tells it apart from a real word like "story-player"), `BundleReport` (one build's own chunk sizes keyed by that normalized name, with a `total_bytes` sum), `bundle_report` (groups a raw `{path: bytes}` reading into one), `BUNDLE_BASELINE_CHUNKS` (the six bytes above, keyed by their normalized names) and `BUNDLE_SIZE_CAP_FACTOR = 1.10`, and `check_bundle_size`, which judges a `BundleReport` against `math.ceil(1147986 * 1.10)` = 1262785 bytes and, on a breach, names every chunk whose bytes grew against the baseline, largest delta first. `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py` gains the pure unit tests (including a seeded bloat fixture naming the chunk that grew, and the exact rounded-cap boundary) and one live `@pytest.mark.subprocess` test that builds `apps/ui` fresh into a `tmp_path` and judges the real reading — the same live-check shape `test_this_repository_has_no_ruff_findings` already uses. The first-paint and 60fps-at-200-nodes budgets need a headless-Chrome trace harness that does not exist yet (F019's own rAF/CDP tooling was never promoted past `.agent/authored/` scratch); they, and the `budgets` CI stage's `MEASURED_MAX_WALL_S` re-measurement the resulting heavier wall-clock will actually deserve, are the next two rounds' work. `docs/system/ci-self-check-v1.md`'s stage and budget tables are already stale before this round (the `budgets` stage's seven paths read as "four" there, and its measured max reads 1.32s against the 24.40s `tests/orchestration/test_ci_stages.py` has held since F273 T015); this round leaves that page untouched and folds its correction into the round that finishes T003's CI wiring, so the doc is fixed once against the finished picture rather than three times against each budget in turn.

ALTERNATIVES: a bundle-size gate over the total bytes alone, with no per-chunk breakdown, rejected because T5_F044.md's Design section and its Acceptance line both ask a breach to name the chunk that grew, not just the total; correcting `docs/system/ci-self-check-v1.md` inside this round, rejected because two of its three stale numbers (the `budgets` stage's own wall-clock and its CI-workflow narrative) only settle once the trace harness lands, and a doc fixed in three passes drifts between them the way it already has once.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `normalize_chunk_name`, `BundleReport`, `bundle_report`, `BUNDLE_BASELINE_CHUNKS`, `BUNDLE_SIZE_CAP_FACTOR` and `check_bundle_size` from `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py` and their tests from `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py`; delete this paragraph. No assumption-log row was added, since this round changes no visual surface.

## DECISION F044 D9 — T003's second CI budget lands: first paint < 1.5s (built bundle, cold), measured as Chrome's own `first-contentful-paint` timing entry over a real HTTP-served, freshly built `apps/ui`, reusing the `--remote-debugging-pipe` transport `tests/ui_server/test_story_export_file_live.py`'s `ChromePipe` already proves; the 60fps budget and the CI-self-check doc fix stay the next round's work (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: `docs/roadmap/features/T5_F044.md` T003 and `docs/ui/design_reference/acceptance_criteria.md` §5 fix the number — "First paint < 1.5s (built bundle, cold)" — without fixing a measurement method. DECISION F044 D8 (F044 R7) named the gap: "The first-paint and 60fps-at-200-nodes budgets need a headless-Chrome trace harness that does not exist yet (F019's own rAF/CDP tooling was never promoted past `.agent/authored/` scratch)." The reviewer's own search of the tree at `c65583711` found no promoted module doing this: the only real, tracked CDP-driving code is `ChromePipe` in `tests/ui_server/test_story_export_file_live.py`, built for F039's zero-network proof over a `file://` URL and never reading a paint timing entry; the per-round `f044-r{N}-render_*` harnesses under `.agent/authored/` build their OWN scratch vite app rather than `apps/ui/dist` and wait with a fixed 2.5-second sleep rather than reading any load or paint event. Neither is a promoted, reusable first-paint tool. The reviewer prototyped the design directly — a scratch script under `.remedy-wt/`, deleted before this decision was written, never committed — against the repository's already-built `apps/ui/dist`: `ChromePipe` launched against Python's own `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` serving that build, `Page.navigate` to it, and a poll of `Runtime.evaluate("JSON.stringify(performance.getEntriesByType('paint'))")` for the `first-contentful-paint` entry returned `92` milliseconds on the first try — well inside the 1500ms budget and proof the mechanism reads a real number rather than a placeholder.

CHOSEN: `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py` gains `FIRST_PAINT_BUDGET_MS = 1500` and `check_first_paint`, judging one observed millisecond reading against it in the same pure-function-plus-`BudgetCheck` shape `check_bundle_size` and `check_lint_clean` already use. `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py` gains four pure unit tests (within-budget, over-budget naming its overage, the exact-boundary case, and the constant's own value) and one live `@pytest.mark.subprocess` test, `test_this_repositorys_shell_paints_within_its_budget`, that builds `apps/ui` fresh with `vite build` into `tmp_path` (never the shared `apps/ui/dist`, DECISION F039 D9), serves it with `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` on an OS-assigned loopback port, imports `ChromePipe`, `CHROME_BIN` and `CHROME_STARTUP_TIMEOUT` directly from `tests/ui_server/test_story_export_file_live.py` (a cross-test-file import that module's own suite already makes of its sibling), navigates to the served `index.html`, and polls the paint-entries expression until a `first-contentful-paint` entry appears. No new dependency: `ChromePipe`'s pipe transport and Python's own `http.server` are the whole mechanism, matching this repository's Node-20-carries-no-websocket-client reasoning that justified `ChromePipe` in the first place.

ALTERNATIVES: a new CDP class duplicating `ChromePipe`, rejected because the existing one is already proven (F039's live suite) and importing it costs one line, while a second implementation would be two places for the same pipe-protocol bug to hide; measuring over `file://` as `ChromePipe`'s existing caller does, rejected because "built bundle, cold" in the Acceptance line means a served load, and a served page's paint timeline can differ from a file load's (no network stack, no CORS, no cache headers); a fixed sleep as the per-round render harness's `drive.mjs` does, rejected because a sleep proves nothing about WHEN paint happened, only that it happened before the sleep ended, which is exactly the gap DECISION F044 D8 named this round to close.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `FIRST_PAINT_BUDGET_MS` and `check_first_paint` from `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py` and their five tests from `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py`; delete this paragraph. No assumption-log row was added, since this round changes no visual surface.

## DECISION F044 D10 — T003's THIRD and last CI budget lands: 60fps p95 at 200 nodes, measured as the p95 gap between consecutive REAL, presented compositor frames (Chrome's own `PipelineReporter` trace events, filtered to `STATE_PRESENTED_ALL`) across the fixture's mount-and-settle window, over a committed frame-pipeline harness at `apps/ui/perf/`; the `budgets` stage's wall-clock re-measures at 44.2s, well inside its existing 300s timeout, so that timeout is unchanged (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: `docs/roadmap/features/T5_F044.md` T003 and `docs/ui/design_reference/acceptance_criteria.md` §5 fix the number — "60fps p95 at 200 nodes (Stage-1+)" — and DECISION F019 D6 measured it once already, at F019 R6, over its own scratch harness (`.agent/authored/f019-r6-perf-*`, never promoted), reading "481 frames, 60 frames per second on average, a median frame of 16.7 ms and a 95th-percentile frame of at most 16.8 ms" from a JS-side `requestAnimationFrame` timestamp loop, and NAMED ITS OWN GAP: "headless Google Chrome on this machine paces `requestAnimationFrame` at 60 Hz, so a frame-rate reading there shows whether a frame was dropped and not how much time a frame had left", leaving "the headroom question left open" for this feature's trace stage. This round closes that gap, and along the way found two more: FIRST, promoting F019's scratch harness UNCHANGED does not work — `ForceBrainGraph`'s own prop signature grew `zoom`, `emphasis`, `onZoomEvent`, `vetoFaded` and `vetoHover` after F019 R6 (F023's semantic zoom, F027's task veto), all required, and F019's harness passed none of them; `vite build` does not type-check (esbuild strips types without checking them), so this compiles silently and only fails at runtime. SECOND, and worse: even with every prop supplied, the harness crashed on its first paint with `SyntaxError: Failed to execute 'addColorStop' on 'CanvasGradient': The value provided ('') could not be parsed as a color` — measured directly by this round's reviewer via `Runtime.exceptionThrown`, over `Runtime.enable`, in a scratch prototype under `.remedy-wt/` (deleted before this decision was written, never committed) — because `ForceBrainGraph`'s `resolvedPalette` reads design tokens through `getComputedStyle` on `document.documentElement` (`tokens_rules.md`: "a 2D canvas cannot read var()"), and a bare harness page never loaded the stylesheet those tokens are declared in, so every token read back as an empty string. F019's OWN measurement, and any run of its unpromoted harness since, therefore measured a canvas that never successfully painted a single node — trivially "60fps", because nothing was being drawn. Importing `apps/ui/src/styles/globals.css` (the same import `apps/ui/src/main.tsx` makes) fixed it: `document.getElementById('root').innerHTML.length` went from `0` to `439`, no more exceptions, and the CSS bundle grew from 0.58 kB to 4.38 kB (the token declarations landing). THIRD, once the harness actually painted, `PipelineReporter` (the compositor's own per-attempted-frame trace event, category `disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline.frame`) turned out to be an ASYNC event: Chrome emits a `ph="b"`/`ph="e"` pair per pipeline ATTEMPT, the `frame_reporter` argument naming the attempt's outcome sits only on the `"b"` entry, and — measured over three repeated 4-second traces at `n=200` — roughly 515-533 attempts occur in that window but only 273-290 of them read `state: "STATE_PRESENTED_ALL"` (most of the rest read `STATE_PRESENTED_PARTIAL`, a real but partial compositor update, not a drop); counting every attempt as one frame reads ~129 "fps", which is the pipeline queue's depth, not the display's frame rate. Filtered to `STATE_PRESENTED_ALL` begin-events only, three repeated measurements read implied rates of 67.5-68.6 fps and p95 intervals of exactly 16.67 ms each time (one vsync tick), with an isolated single 33.33 ms gap in two of the three runs (a real but singular missed tick, not a sustained one) — a stable, reproducible, genuinely different result from F019 D6's own reading of the same node count.

CHOSEN: (1) `apps/ui/perf/` (`index.html`, `main.tsx`, `vite.config.mjs`) is a COMMITTED, PERMANENT harness — never a `.agent/authored/` scratch file — that mounts the real `ForceBrainGraph` at the root zoom level (`ZOOM_HOME`, `zoomEmphasis(layout, ZOOM_HOME)`, no vetoes) over the committed 200/500-node fixture (`brainPerfFixture.ts`, DECISION F019 D6), importing `../src/styles/globals.css` so its tokens resolve. It sits outside `apps/ui/src` (`tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["src"]` and `eslint.config.js`'s `files: ["src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"]` both skip it, so it is neither type-checked nor linted by the app's own gates) and outside the shipped app's own build (`apps/ui/vite.config.ts`'s `rollupOptions.input` names only the root `index.html`); it is built with its OWN `vite.config.mjs`, always via CLI `--outDir`/`--emptyOutDir` into a scratch directory, never into the shared `apps/ui/dist` (DECISION F039 D9). (2) `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py` gains `FRAME_PIPELINE_P95_BUDGET_MS = 17.0` (the same value DECISION F019 D6's own `STAGE1_P95_BUDGET_MS` chose, for the same reason: a real reading lands on a vsync tick, so the two failure shapes are "one tick" and "two or more", never something between) and `check_frame_pipeline`, in the same pure-function-plus-`BudgetCheck` shape `check_bundle_size` and `check_first_paint` already use; `BudgetCheck.observed` widens from `int` to `int | float`, because a percentile this close to its own budget loses the information a verdict needs if rounded to a whole millisecond. (3) `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py` gains four pure unit tests and one live `@pytest.mark.subprocess` test, `test_this_repositorys_shell_sustains_60fps_at_200_nodes`, that builds `apps/ui/perf/` fresh into `tmp_path`, serves it with `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer`, opens `Tracing.start` (categories `disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline`, `devtools.timeline`, `blink.user_timing`, `disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline.frame`) BEFORE `Page.navigate`, traces for `FRAME_TRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS = 4.0` (roughly double the ~2.2-2.3s mount-and-settle span this round measured three times), ends tracing, drains for `Tracing.tracingComplete`, and reads the p95 gap between consecutive `STATE_PRESENTED_ALL` `PipelineReporter` begin-events. (4) THE STAGE WALL-CLOCK: this round's reviewer measured the `budgets` stage's full `test_paths` set with the new test included, in the sim worktree, at `44.22s` real time — well inside the existing `timeout_sec=300` in `packages/orchestration/ci_stages.py`, so that file is UNCHANGED this round; the plan's "wall-clock re-measurement" item is satisfied by this reading, not by a timeout edit.

ALTERNATIVES: reusing F019 R6's own RAF-timestamp technique unchanged, rejected for the reason CONTEXT states at length — it is blind to real render cost by construction, and this round's own reproduction shows it was ALSO measuring a crashed, unpainted canvas; a raw population of `RunTask` trace-event durations (Chrome's per-main-thread-task events), rejected because roughly 600-3800 of them fire per few seconds regardless of rendering, the overwhelming majority sub-millisecond scheduler housekeeping unrelated to a frame, so a percentile over the whole population is dominated by noise (measured: p95 0.05-0.16 ms, p50 under 0.02 ms, useless as a frame-cost signal) and only the MAX (once 56 ms) hints at real cost, which is a different statistic than the Acceptance line asks for; counting every `PipelineReporter` attempt (both `ph` phases, every `state`) as one frame, rejected because it reads the pipeline queue's depth (measured ~129 "fps") rather than the display's actual delivery rate, and would pass a genuinely janky build that queues many aborted or partial attempts per real frame; `DrawFrame` trace events, rejected because they fired only 0-2 times across every window this round traced, evidently unreliable under `--headless=new`'s compositor in this environment. HOW THE 500-NODE SIZE IS HANDLED: `acceptance_criteria.md`'s own Edge Cases line reserves 500 nodes for "the zoom feature's bar", so this round's CI test names only `n=200`; the harness accepts `?n=500` (matching the fixture's own `BRAIN_PERF_STAGE6_NODES`) for a future round or a manual reading, never gated here.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `apps/ui/perf/`, `FRAME_PIPELINE_P95_BUDGET_MS` and `check_frame_pipeline` from `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py`, their five tests and the `FRAME_TRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS` constant from `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py`, and revert `BudgetCheck.observed` to `int`; delete this paragraph. No assumption-log row was added, since this round changes no visual surface a dashboard or a shell renders.

## DECISION F044 D11 — `docs/system/ci-self-check-v1.md`'s `budgets` row is re-measured against its CURRENT seven-path selection and synced to the doc and to `tests/orchestration/test_ci_stages.py`; the `budgets` stage's `timeout_sec=300` is UNCHANGED (2026-09-30)

## DECISION F044 D12 — T003's "numbers recorded per run (trend visible)" DESIGN line is discharged as out of this feature's built scope; ACCEPTANCE's own "CI budgets red/green with numbers" is met by each `BudgetCheck.detail` (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT, read at closure rather than caught earlier. `docs/roadmap/features/T5_F044.md`'s Design
section, under "Budgets in CI", reads "numbers recorded per run (trend visible), breach output
names the biggest deltas". Its Acceptance line, the binding contract, reads only "CI budgets
red/green with numbers; a seeded bundle bloat fixture names the culprit chunk." No DECISION across
F044's ten rounds names either clause; a grep of `.agent/decisions.md` and `.agent/live_review.md`
for "recorded-numbers", "trend visible" and "numbers artifact" at `393d558b6` returns nothing, so
this is the first time either clause was read against what shipped. MEASURED: `check_bundle_size`,
`check_first_paint` and `check_frame_pipeline` each build a `BudgetCheck` whose `.detail` names the
observed reading and, on a breach, the overage or the grown chunks — `check_bundle_size`'s own
docstring already promises "a breach names the chunks that grew, largest delta first." Every one of
the three live tests reads `assert check.ok, check.detail`, so a RED run's own pytest failure
carries the numbers into whatever log retains that run — the local terminal, or, hosted, the
GitHub Actions run's own retained log. A GREEN run computes the same `.detail` string and discards
it; nothing in this repository persists it anywhere a later run could diff against. Searching
`packages/orchestration/ci_run.py` and `apps/cli/commands/ci_cmd.py` (the whole `remedy ci`
seam) finds no per-check reporting at all — `summarize_ci_results` prints one line PER STAGE
(pass/fail/skip/duration), never per budget check — and no file under `.data`, `docs/` or
`packages/` accumulates a budget reading across runs.

CHOSEN: ACCEPTANCE's own wording — "CI budgets red/green with numbers" — is read as "a breach
names its own numbers," which is what `check_bundle_size`'s docstring already promised before this
round existed and what all three checks now do; this is MET, not aspirational, and needs no new
code. The Design section's stronger "trend visible" is discharged as OUT OF THIS FEATURE'S BUILT
SCOPE: no DECISION ever specified a storage format, an owner, a reader or a retention period for
such a trend, and CI's own hosted-workflow log retention already gives an operator who wants to
compare two runs' numbers a place to look — GitHub Actions keeps every run's own log, and a RED
run's `.detail` string is IN that log by construction. A dedicated persistence artifact (a JSONL
history file, a dashboard, a badge) would be new product surface invented at closure with no
consumer named anywhere in this feature's file, which is exactly the shape
`docs/agents/planner_reviewer_prompt.md` §4 item 7 asks a reviewer to name as a DECISION rather
than build silently.

ALTERNATIVES: building a trend-storage artifact now (e.g. `packages/orchestration/ci_budgets.py`
appending each run's three readings to a committed or `.data`-scoped JSONL file), REJECTED: no
Acceptance line, DECISION or Do-not-touch clause names a reader for it, a closure round is the
wrong time to invent one, and DECISION F033 D3 sets the precedent for discharging a Design-only
promise as vacuous when the codebase it would apply to was never built for it. Printing every
`BudgetCheck.detail` unconditionally (pass or fail) from each live test via `print()`, REJECTED as
a half-measure: pytest's own captured stdout on a PASSING run is discarded by default
(`-q`, no `-s`, no `-rA`) exactly like the return value is now, so the print would add a line of
code without adding a single byte of persistence — the real gap is STORAGE across runs, not stdout
verbosity within one. Registering this as an open finding for a future feature to build, REJECTED:
nothing in T5_F044.md's Acceptance or Do-not-touch sections obligates a trend artifact, so there is
no unmet contract to carry forward — a finding records a contract this feature broke, not a
Design-section wish nobody asked to keep.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete this paragraph; if a trend-storage artifact is wanted, it is a new feature's
scope, not a reopening of F044.

## DECISION amend0930 D1 — Every pytest and vitest run of this repository is capped at six parallel workers and runs at a lower CPU priority; the cap lives in `tests/conftest.py`, not in a wrapper script (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: The operator's machine has 24 CPU threads and one large graphics card, and for months it ran very hot whenever tests ran; the operator read about 740 watts at the wall and ordered the test load cut massively. The last full suite (F044 round 13) ran 21,078 tests in 213 seconds with `python3 -m pytest -n auto -q`, which starts 24 workers, so about 85 CPU minutes of work arrived in one burst. `apps/ui/vitest.config.ts` set no worker limit either. `scripts/remedy_pytest.sh` limits nothing, and almost every run in the loop starts pytest directly, so a limit placed in that script would miss most runs. Honest limit: fewer workers lower the heat at any one moment but not the electricity used, because the same work only takes longer; electricity falls only when less work is done, which is what D2 and D3 and the registered feature F293 are for.

CHOSEN: `tests/load_governor.py` holds the logic and `tests/conftest.py` wires it, because every pytest run loads that conftest however it is started. `REMEDY_TEST_MAX_WORKERS` (unset or not a number means 6, 0 means no cap) turns `-n auto` and `-n logical` into the smaller of the cap and the CPU count and reduces an explicit `-n N` above the cap to the cap with one printed line; a run without `-n` stays serial. The controlling process lowers itself to niceness 10 (`REMEDY_TEST_NICE`, 0 leaves it alone), never raises priority and ignores an OSError; workers and child processes inherit it. `apps/ui/vitest.config.ts` reads the same variable. A second part writes one JSON line per run (time, command, collected count, exit status, wall seconds, CPU seconds, workers) to `REMEDY_TEST_LOAD_LOG`, or to `~/.remedy-loop/test_load.jsonl` when that folder exists, and blanks the variable so a pytest run started by a test records nothing. Both new variables and the log path are registered env-only keys (`tests.max_workers`, `tests.nice`, `tests.load_log`).

ALTERNATIVES: a cap only in `scripts/remedy_pytest.sh`, REJECTED because most runs bypass it. Editing `pyproject.toml` `addopts` to a fixed `-n 6`, REJECTED because it cannot express "up to the cap" for `-n auto` and would change the spelling of the command every document uses. Setting `nice` from the wrapper only, REJECTED for the same bypass reason.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the hooks and the `load_governor` import from `tests/conftest.py`, delete `tests/load_governor.py`, its test file and the vitest contract, drop the three registry keys and regenerate `docs/guides/environment.md`, and restore the two-line `vitest.config.ts`.

## DECISION amend0930 D2 — No test pass runs outside a round's own verification; the standing instruction called SLOW MODE is withdrawn (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: A loop session on 2026-09-30 wrote that it "owes the operator's standing SLOW MODE instruction: run the repo's pytest wrappers for a broad validation pass" before claiming a feature. That instruction is not in the repository. It was found in two places outside it: `~/Repos/system/bin/remedy-loop-runner`, in the text appended to the loop prompt when slow mode is on ("After a feature reaches closure and before claiming or starting any next feature, run the repository's pytest-based broad validation through the Remedy wrappers ... catching errors early."), and in the auto-memory note `f044_command_palette_state.md`, which carried it forward as an owed pass. Both add a broad test pass per feature, the opposite of what the operator now wants.

CHOSEN: rule 2 of the amendment paragraph in `docs/agents/self_drive_protocol.md` withdraws it for every session; the runner's slow-mode sentences and the memory note's paragraph were replaced by the one withdrawal sentence (the runner change is committed locally in `~/Repos/system` and not pushed). The old texts are in the handback so the change can be undone.

ALTERNATIVES: leaving the runner as it was and relying on the protocol rule alone, REJECTED because the runner re-injects the instruction into every slow-mode loop prompt, and a session obeys the newest instruction it reads.

HOW TO REVERSE: `git revert` the local commit in `~/Repos/system`, restore the memory paragraph from the handback, and delete rule 2 from the protocol paragraph.

## DECISION amend0930 D3 — One run per tree: a round's selection and its mutation red-proofs run once for each distinct set of bytes, and mutations are run by the reviewer only (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: Measured on 2026-09-30, a round's test selection of 500 to 2,300 tests ran up to three times per round (the reviewer's dry run, the worker, the reviewer again) and mutation red-proofs ran twice (worker, then reviewer), always on identical bytes.

CHOSEN: rules 3 to 5 of the amendment paragraph. When the reviewer proved a round in a dry run and every file the worker committed is byte-identical to that copy on the same base commit, the dry run's readings are the verification: the reviewer reads the diff bottom-up, compares bytes and re-runs nothing, and the verdict says "verified by dry run, bytes identical" naming the compared commit. Otherwise the reviewer re-runs as before. Mutations stay mandatory for production code but only the reviewer runs them. The worker still runs the selection once, after its last code commit, in the primary checkout, because that run proves that checkout's environment. `.claude/commands/build-remedy-self.md` carries the matching clause.

ALTERNATIVES: dropping the worker's run too, REJECTED because the dry run happens in a scratch tree, not in the primary checkout. Dropping the reviewer's re-run in every case, REJECTED because a differing byte means the dry run proved a different tree.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete rules 3 to 5 and the clause in `build-remedy-self.md`.

## DECISION amend0930 D4 — Headless Chrome keeps its arguments: no graphics-card use was measured, so `--disable-gpu` is not added (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: `ChromePipe` in `tests/ui_server/test_story_export_file_live.py` starts headless Chrome without `--disable-gpu`, and nobody knew whether that draws power on the graphics card (an RTX 5090). Measured with `nvidia-smi` sampling once per second: 15 idle seconds, then a run of `tests/ui_server/test_story_export_file_live.py`, `tests/ui_server/test_explanation_layer_live.py` and `tests/orchestration/test_ci_budgets.py` (30 passed in 30.7 seconds). Average draw idle 25.7 W (15 samples, the card was holding an Ollama model), average during the run 28.1 W (31 samples, highest 56.1 W), a difference of 2.4 W, far below the 20 W threshold. The compute-application list read in the middle of the run held only two Ollama servers and the Luna voice process, no Chrome. Limit of this reading: that list shows compute applications, not every graphics context, so the watts are the deciding number.

CHOSEN: change nothing; no contract test for `--disable-gpu`.

ALTERNATIVES: adding `--disable-gpu` anyway, REJECTED because the frame-budget tests measure real compositor frames and the flag could change what they measure, for no measured saving.

HOW TO REVERSE: nothing to reverse. If a later reading shows Chrome on the card, add the flag to that argument list and a contract that every `--headless=new` in tests is accompanied by it.

## DECISION amend0930 D5 — F293 (Test load diet) is registered thin as the first unaccepted STATUS line, under its own Tier 2 heading, with the Tier 5 cockpit list re-opened after it (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: Operator amendment amend0930-test-load, Part F, orders one registered feature that makes the tests themselves cheaper, placed so that the loop's next claim is that feature. The highest feature number in `docs/roadmap/STATUS.md` was F292 on `origin/main`, and no feature branch was open (F044's PR was merged), so the new feature is F293. The first line starting `- [ ] F` was F292, which is not the first entry under its Tier 5 heading (F043 and F044 are accepted above it).

CHOSEN: `docs/roadmap/features/T2_F293.md` in the shape of `T2_F290.md`; a new heading `## Tier 2 — Test load (operator amendment amend0930-test-load)` with the F293 line directly before F292's line, and the Tier 5 heading re-opened after it under its existing text (`(parallel human track, continued)`, which already says "continued", exactly as the ledger has done for every earlier re-opening of that heading). In the same commit `TOTAL_FEATURES` in `tests/docs/test_docs_consistency.py` went from 292 to 293 with one comment sentence, the README sentence to `121 of 293 registered items accepted.` and the Tier 2 row's Total cell from 40 to 41. `docs/roadmap/ROADMAP.md` was not touched.

ALTERNATIVES: appending "(continued)" to the re-opened heading, REJECTED because that heading already ends in "continued)" and doubling it would break the ledger's own repeated-heading convention.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the feature file, the new heading and line, and put the three totals back to 292, 292 and 40.

## DECISION amend0930b D1 — SLOW MODE is reinstated as a hardening stage before every feature closure, with a repair loop (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: The operator's own instruction called SLOW MODE was withdrawn by amend0930-test-load rule (2). He wants it back: more test-and-repair loops per feature, at a slower pace. Its old wording ordered "broad validation" passes; the full suite already runs once per feature (21.5 CPU minutes measured on 2026-09-30) and hosted CI runs it again, so repeating the same tests on the same bytes finds nothing new.

CHOSEN: SLOW MODE is defined in `docs/agents/self_drive_protocol.md` (paragraph amend0930b-slow-cap) as an acceptance audit before the closure sequence: for every Acceptance and Goal & Done statement, a test that turns red under one mutation of the production code, at least one proof through the command line or the cockpit, up to three repair rounds, and a record in the feature file's Built State. `docs/roadmap/STATUS_closure_protocol.md` precondition 8 pins the record. The mode is on only when the prompt carries `SLOW MODE is active`. This supersedes the SLOW MODE clause of DECISION amend0930 D2; that decision's rule against any other test pass stays.

ALTERNATIVES: restoring the old "broad validation" pass, REJECTED because it repeats identical bytes; a second full-suite run per feature, REJECTED for the same reason.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the paragraph amend0930b-slow-cap and closure precondition 8, restore the sentence in the amend0930-test-load paragraph, and delete D1 to D3.

## DECISION amend0930b D2 — A STOP authored by remedy-weekly-cap is the loop runner's pause, not the operator waiting (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: The loop runner now obeys a weekly usage cap and writes `.agent/STOP` with `author: remedy-weekly-cap` when it is reached during a session. Sessions read any STOP as a stop request and their handoffs tended to say that something waits for the operator, which would make the runner end the loop for good.

CHOSEN: Guardrail G6 and rule (6) of the amend0930b-slow-cap paragraph tell the session to hand off as for any STOP and to say that the loop paused at the weekly cap and resumes by itself. The runner removes only a stop file with that author line; a stop file written by the operator is never removed.

ALTERNATIVES: a separate signal file, REJECTED because every session already honours `.agent/STOP` under G6 and a new file would need every skill taught.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete rule (6) and the G6 sentence, and remove the watcher from the runner in the operator's second repository.

## DECISION amend0930b D3 — `test_a_real_run_asking_for_auto_gets_the_cap` asserts the smaller of the cap and the CPU count (2026-09-30)

CONTEXT: The test sets a cap of 2 and asserted that the child run used exactly 2 workers. With `-n auto` on a machine with one CPU, xdist correctly starts 1 worker, so the test failed there; the orchestrator saw it fail on a one-CPU machine.

CHOSEN: The assertion reads `min(2, os.cpu_count() or 1)`. No red-proof is possible on the 24-thread development machine, where the old and the new assertion both hold; the change is justified by reading the governor, which never raises a count above what `auto` returns.

ALTERNATIVES: skipping the test on one-CPU machines, REJECTED because the behaviour under test (the cap applies to `auto`) still holds there.

HOW TO REVERSE: put `== 2` back in that assertion.

## DECISION F293 D1 — The closure's integration-gate run supplies T002's "after" reading; T001's run was the extra one this feature's own task order needed early (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: round 1's own claim text in `.agent/live_review.md` ("no second full run is ordered later in this feature") forecloses what T002's Acceptance line requires — "the full suite's CPU seconds in the test load record are at least 40 percent below T001's baseline" — which can only be read from a fresh full-suite run taken AFTER T002's cuts land. Meanwhile amend0930-test-load rule 6 and amend0917-throughput both state, unchanged, that the full suite runs exactly once per feature, in the closure sequence's integration-gate round.

CHOSEN: T001's run (this feature's early, explicitly-named exception — the feature file's own Task order puts a full run at T001, before any cut lands, because T001 is a ranking task that needs one) and the closure sequence's own integration-gate run (which every feature is owed regardless, unchanged by this feature) are the two ends of the SAME comparison: T001 supplies "before" (1246.09 CPU seconds, `collected` 21102, from `.agent/f293_inventory.md`), and the closure's own mandatory run supplies "after". This is not a second run in the sense amend0917-throughput forbids — it is the one run every feature already gets, read for a second purpose it was going to exist for anyway. T002's own Acceptance check therefore runs at closure, not inside any T002 round, and each T002 round proves its own work through targeted measurements instead.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) run the full suite again inside a T002 round to prove the cut immediately — REJECTED, it is exactly the second run the standing rule forbids. (b) never re-measure and treat the T001 baseline as permanent — REJECTED, the feature's own Acceptance line requires a fresh reading, not an assertion. (c) measure "after" only for the specific test files a T002 round touches, via a targeted run's own summed durations, and call that the acceptance proof — REJECTED as the acceptance proof itself but ADOPTED as each T002 round's own verification: a targeted run proves a cut is real and proportionate to what T001 measured, but it cannot speak for the whole suite's total CPU seconds, which is what the Acceptance line actually asks for.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete this paragraph; a later round may instead register a fresh, explicitly-authorized second full run if the operator wants the 40% figure confirmed before closure.

## DECISION F293 D2 — `dead_command_ids` caches its file scan per search root; a root's files are read once per process, not once per call (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: `dead_command_ids` (`packages/orchestration/dead_command_check.py`) re-reads and re-AST-parses every file under its search root's `tests/` and `scripts/` directories on EVERY call, measured by the reviewer at ~2.4 seconds per call regardless of whether it is the first or a later call in the same process. It is called, directly or through `doctor_core_report()`, by dozens of tests across `tests/cli/test_worker_facade_cmd.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_disk_floor.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_self_use_generator.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_self_use_runner.py` and its own `tests/orchestration/test_dead_command_check.py`, paying that cost every single time with no reuse.

CHOSEN: split the function into a cached file-scan (`_scan_search_root`, module-level `_SCAN_CACHE` dict keyed by the resolved `root` path) and the per-call matching logic, which stays uncached because it depends on the `catalog`/`handlers` arguments, which vary per call. This is safe because no test in this repository writes a new file into a root's `tests/`/`scripts/` and then re-queries the SAME root expecting the new file to be picked up — every test that plants a synthetic dead command does so by monkeypatching the in-memory catalog/handler table `dead_command_ids` takes as arguments (confirmed by reading `tests/cli/test_worker_facade_cmd.py`'s `_plant_dead_command` fixture), and the one caller that passes a custom `root=` (`tests/orchestration/test_dead_command_check.py`) always uses a fresh, unique `tmp_path` per test, so per-root keying cannot leak between tests. Two new tests in `tests/orchestration/test_dead_command_check.py` prove both properties mechanically: the file scan is not repeated for a repeated root (a call-count assertion, not a timing assertion — timing is flaky, counting is not), and two different roots never share a cache entry (a correctness assertion: the same command_id is dead under one root and alive under another, read correctly both times).

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: after this change, `dead_command_ids(..., root=X)` will not notice a file added to `X`'s `tests/`/`scripts/` after the FIRST call with that exact root in the same process. No code in this repository relies on that live-reload behaviour today (verified above); a future caller that needs it must pass a fresh root or clear `_SCAN_CACHE` explicitly. In production use (`remedy doctor core`, one process per CLI invocation) this caching provides no user-visible benefit or cost — each invocation is a fresh process and pays the scan once either way, same as before. The entire benefit is inside a single pytest worker process, where dozens of calls now share one scan per root.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) `functools.lru_cache` on a wrapper taking `root` as its only argument — REJECTED as a bare mechanism because it caches an unbounded number of distinct roots for the life of the process with no eviction, which a hand-rolled dict does exactly the same amount of in this case (few distinct roots in practice), so the extra dependency bought nothing. (b) cache the WHOLE `dead_command_ids` call keyed on `(root, catalog, handlers)` — REJECTED, `handlers` holds live function objects that are not reliably hashable across calls and the catalog/handlers matching is already cheap (under 0.01s), so caching it adds complexity for no measured benefit and risks masking a real catalog change. (c) restructure the 40+ affected tests to share one `doctor_core_report()` call via a module-scoped fixture (the T002 task text's own "share expensive setup" framing) — REJECTED as the PRIMARY fix because it would need to be repeated in every one of the five affected files, each with its own test structure, while the caching fix in the one function all five files call through fixes all of them at their shared root cause in one change, and remains correct if a sixth caller appears later.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `_SCAN_CACHE` and `_scan_search_root`, restore the inline scan loop directly inside `dead_command_ids`, and delete the two new tests in `tests/orchestration/test_dead_command_check.py` named in this decision.

## DECISION F293 D3 — `_unsafe_text` in `scripts/build_review_manifest.py` caches its answer per string; the gate matrix scans each distinct text once per process (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: `tests/orchestration/test_review_gate_totality.py::TestGateMatrixIsTotal::test_recursive_matrix_never_throws` was the suite's second slowest entry in T001's ranking (25.71 s), and unlike the slowest it is CPU work, not waiting. The reviewer's profile at `525c2d268` put 38 of its 44 profiled seconds under `_unsafe_text`, called about 1.08 million times over roughly 30,000 gate-matrix evaluations, each call running the secret redactor's and the path scrubber's regular expressions over one of the same few dozen field texts. The file used 29.64 CPU seconds in the test load record (`pytest tests/orchestration/test_review_gate_totality.py -q -n auto --durations=3`).

CHOSEN: `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)` on `_unsafe_text`. Its answer depends on the string alone: `_contains_secret` compares the redacted text with the input, and `_contains_local_path` compares the output of `safe_text` with the input, where every replaced path starts with `[` and so never equals a raw path, which starts with `/` or a drive letter; the data root that `safe_text` reads changes the replacement, never the yes-or-no answer. The same file then used 5.26 CPU seconds, and the matrix test's call took 2.16 s. A new test, `test_each_distinct_text_is_scanned_once` in `tests/orchestration/test_review_gate_sensitive_metadata.py`, counts the calls into `run_manifest._contains_secret`, requires one call per distinct text, and requires the cached answer for a secret to still read `a secret`. The reviewer's mutations in a disposable worktree: without the decorator the new test is red (four calls for two texts); with the decorator kept and the secret branch removed it is red again; restored, the file reads 9 passed.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: within one process the scanner no longer re-runs for a text it has already answered. A test that swaps `run_manifest._contains_secret` or `_contains_local_path` and then expects `_unsafe_text` to re-evaluate a text scanned earlier in the same process would see the earlier answer; by `git grep` at `525c2d268` no test does that, and the one test that swaps `_contains_local_path`, in `tests/orchestration/test_review_subject_strict_schema.py`, exercises `packages/orchestration/review_subject.py`, which calls the detectors directly. The cache holds at most 4,096 strings that the process already holds in memory, and nothing is written anywhere. A review manifest build is one short process; the cache only spares it repeated scans of a text it meets again.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) caching `_contains_secret` and `_contains_local_path` in `packages/orchestration/run_manifest.py`, REJECTED for this round because those two have more callers and tests that swap them, and the measured cost sits under `_unsafe_text`; (b) shrinking the matrix of wrong values in the totality test, REJECTED because it removes coverage, which the feature's Do-not-touch forbids.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the decorator, the `import functools` line and the two docstring sentences that name this decision, and delete `test_each_distinct_text_is_scanned_once`.

## DECISION F293 D4 — `dead_command_ids` also caches each match answer per search root and searched words; a repeated question reads no search text (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: after DECISION F293 D2, a warm call of `doctor_core_report` still cost about 0.46 CPU seconds, measured by the reviewer's profile at `b0faefe61`: 0.46 of its 0.48 profiled seconds sat in the substring test of `dead_command_ids` (`packages/orchestration/dead_command_check.py`), whose generator took 43,328 steps per call, because every call asked again, for every catalog command outside the argv-pair set, whether any search text names it. D2's alternative (b) called that matching "already cheap (under 0.01s)", which this measurement shows was wrong. `tests/cli/test_worker_facade_cmd.py` used 22.04 CPU seconds in a serial run (`pytest tests/cli/test_worker_facade_cmd.py -q -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider`, test load record).

CHOSEN: a module-level `_MATCH_CACHE` and a helper `_mentioned(root, texts, kind, words)`, keyed by the search root, the kind of test (`"text"` for the substring test, `"name"` for the whole-word test) and the frozen set of words. Both tests answer exactly what the two inline `any(...)` expressions answered, and the handler table is read at the same point as before, so a catalog entry without a handler behaves as it did. The answer depends only on the root's files, which D2 already reads once per process on the argument that they do not change while a process lives, and on the words. A command a test plants (`_plant_dead_command` in `tests/cli/test_worker_facade_cmd.py` mints its ids from a uuid and gives its handler no names) has words of its own, so it is still searched for. The same file then used 2.83 CPU seconds. A new test, `test_a_repeated_question_reads_no_search_text_again` in `tests/orchestration/test_dead_command_check.py`, replaces the cached texts with a list that refuses to be read and requires the second call to give the same answer. The reviewer's mutations in a disposable worktree: reading the cache never (`hit = None`) turned the new test red; keying the cache without the words turned four tests red, the two planted-command tests of `TestDoctorCoreDeadCommands` among them; restored, `tests/orchestration/test_dead_command_check.py` reads 6 passed.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: within one process, `dead_command_ids` no longer re-reads the search texts for a question it has already answered for the same root; D2's limit therefore reaches the answers too, and a caller that adds a file under a root's `tests/` or `scripts/` after the first call in the same process would not see it. No caller does that (D2). `remedy doctor core` is one process per invocation and asks each question once either way.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) one joined text per root in place of the per-file loop, REJECTED because a substring search reads the same bytes either way and saves only the loop's overhead; (b) caching the whole answer keyed on the catalog and the handler objects, REJECTED because a planted command would then miss the cache for every command instead of for its own.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `_MATCH_CACHE` and `_mentioned`, put the two inline `any(...)` expressions back into `dead_command_ids`, and delete `test_a_repeated_question_reads_no_search_text_again`.

## DECISION F293 D5 — `_is_safe_key` in `packages/orchestration/run_manifest.py` caches its answer per string key and use; the input snapshot's key names are checked once per process (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: the reviewer's profile of `tests/orchestration/test_job_task_runner.py` at `382c9cbec` found `validate_input_snapshot` called 2,266 times, and within it `_is_safe_key` called 253,811 times for about 11.4 of the run's 65 profiled seconds, almost all of it in `_contains_secret` and `_contains_local_path`, the secret redactor and path scrubber that DECISION F293 D3 already met one level up. An input snapshot carries every config key and every `REMEDY_` environment key by name, so the same key names are checked again at every validation of every run manifest.

CHOSEN: `_is_safe_key(key, *, allow_dots=True)` keeps its signature, answers False for a key that is not a string, and otherwise returns `_is_safe_str_key(key, allow_dots)`, which holds the old body under `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)`. Its answer depends on the key and `allow_dots` alone: the bounded-length limit, the character rules and the regular expression are constants, and the two detectors are pure over their input. `lru_cache` stores no answer for a call that raises, and each detector catches its own failures and answers True, so a value is never cleared by a failure. Measured in a disposable worktree at `382c9cbec`, serial runs of `tests/orchestration/test_job_task_runner.py` (`pytest ... -q -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider`, test load record) read 70.59 CPU seconds before and 54.17 after; the same file read 41.0 CPU seconds in the primary checkout at `b0faefe61`, so only readings taken in one tree are compared. Two new tests in `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_security.py` pin the cache: the detectors run once for a key asked twice, and a dotted key is answered apart for `allow_dots=False` and `True`, in both orders. The reviewer's mutations: without the decorator the first test is red; with the wrapper passing `True` for every use the second is red; restored, the file reads 16 passed. The selection `pytest tests/orchestration -q -n auto -k run_manifest` read 880 passed.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: within one process a key name is checked once per use. A test that swaps `run_manifest._contains_secret` or `_contains_local_path`, or the redactor under them, and then expects `_is_safe_key` to re-check a key it checked earlier in the same process would see the earlier answer; by `git grep` at `382c9cbec` the three test files that swap a detector or the redactor (`tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_security.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_review_subject_strict_schema.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_review_gate_sensitive_metadata.py`) call the detectors directly or through `review_subject` and the review manifest builder, never through `_is_safe_key`. The cache holds at most 4,096 key names and writes nothing.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) caching `_contains_secret` itself, REJECTED because `TestSecretDetectorFailsClosed` swaps the redactor for one that raises and requires the answer True for a value an earlier test may already have checked, so a cached False would turn it red and would hide a failing redactor; (b) caching the whole `validate_input_snapshot` result, REJECTED because its input is a mutable record with no stable key short of re-serialising it, which is itself a fifth of the function's cost.

HOW TO REVERSE: fold `_is_safe_str_key` back into `_is_safe_key`, delete the decorator and the `import functools` line, and delete `TestSafeKeyAnswersPerKeyAndUse`.

## DECISION F293 D6 — `tests/conftest.py` reads Remedy's own checkout identity once per test process, at session start (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: every run's input snapshot records `remedy_worktree_identity()` (`packages/orchestration/run_manifest.py`), the git content identity of the Remedy checkout itself, and each reading runs several git processes over the whole checkout, twice per git command because `_git_bytes` first asks `git config` which helpers to neutralise. The reviewer's profile of `tests/orchestration/test_job_task_runner.py` at `382c9cbec` counted 146 such readings in one run of that file, about 15 of its wall seconds, all inside `build_input_snapshot`. Three test files (`tests/cli/test_job_rerun_manifest.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_logical_identity.py`) already froze the value per test, keeping the real identity, because a neighbour that writes into the shared checkout raced the digest (R-0645, R-0950).

CHOSEN: a session-scoped autouse fixture, `_one_remedy_checkout_identity_per_process`, in `tests/conftest.py`: it reads the real identity once, when a test process's session starts and before any test can patch git, and points `run_manifest.remedy_worktree_identity` at that value for the whole session, restoring the function at the end. `_remedy_repo_root()` comes from the module's own path, so the value always describes this checkout, and no test may change this checkout. A test that sets its own value with `monkeypatch` still wins inside that test, and the three freezing fixtures keep working unchanged. Child processes that a test starts, such as CLI runs, still read their own identity. Measured in one disposable worktree at `4c4be0d99`, serial runs of `tests/orchestration/test_job_task_runner.py` (`pytest ... -q -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider`, test load record) read 55.23 CPU seconds before and 12.66 after. A new test, `TestOneCheckoutIdentityPerProcess` in `tests/regression/test_test_load_governor.py`, requires two readings in one process to be the same object. The reviewer's mutations: without the fixture's reassignment the new test is red; with `remedy_worktree_identity` made to raise, the session fixture errors and the test with it, so the real reading still runs once in every test process; restored, green. With the fixture in place and before the new test was added, `pytest tests/orchestration tests/cli/test_job_rerun_manifest.py tests/regression/test_resource_safety.py tests/regression/test_test_load_governor.py tests/regression/test_data_root_guard.py tests/test_data_root_isolation.py tests/test_test_categories.py -q -n auto -k 'run_manifest or rerun or resource_safety or load_governor or data_root or categories'` read 1050 passed, and the canary 42 passed.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. Inside a test process, Remedy's own checkout identity is the one read at session start, so a test can no longer observe a neighbour's edit to the shared checkout; by `git grep` at `4c4be0d99` the one test that changes `worktree_identity` for the Remedy root, in `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_logical_identity.py`, already froze the identity before it, and the tests that force git failures (`tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_integrity.py`) read temporary repositories. Every test process pays one reading at session start, including a short run of one file.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) caching the identity in the product, REJECTED because a long-running Remedy process must record the checkout as it is when each job starts; (b) reading it lazily at the first call inside a test, REJECTED because a test that had patched git at that moment would leave a broken value to every later test in the process; (c) adding the per-test freeze to more files one by one, REJECTED because every in-process job run in the suite pays the same readings.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the fixture from `tests/conftest.py` and `TestOneCheckoutIdentityPerProcess` from `tests/regression/test_test_load_governor.py`.

## DECISION F293 D7 — `remedy doctor core` reads the test load record itself and states its last 24 hours as information only (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: F293 T004 orders one plain sentence in `remedy doctor core` naming how many test runs and CPU minutes the last 24 hours cost, read from the test load record, with nothing wrong printed when the record is absent. The record's path rules live in `tests/load_governor.py`, which no production module may import, and doctor core's JSON output is pinned key by key in `tests/cli/test_worker_facade_cmd.py`.

CHOSEN: `last_day_test_load(environ=None, home=None, now=None)` in `apps/cli/commands/worker_facade_cmd.py` follows the same path rules through the registered reader `env_value("REMEDY_TEST_LOAD_LOG")`: a set value names the file and a set-but-empty value means no record, otherwise `~/.remedy-loop/test_load.jsonl` when that folder exists. It counts the lines whose `utc` lies within the last 24 hours, adds their `cpu_seconds`, skips a line that does not parse, and returns `record`, `runs`, `cpu_minutes` and `sentence`. `DoctorCoreReport` gains the field `test_load` with an empty default, so the three places that build the report by keyword keep working, and `as_json()` ends with the key `test_load`; the text output prints `test load:` and the sentence directly before `dead commands:`. The reading is never a check, a warning or a blocker, so `ready` cannot change with it; a failed read says the cost is unknown. Four new tests in `TestDoctorCoreTestLoad` and the two exact-key lists in `TestDoctorCoreReportFunction`, which now name `test_load`, pin it. The reviewer's mutations in a disposable worktree at `b225adae2`: counting every line regardless of its time, adding `wall_seconds` in place of `cpu_seconds`, and dropping the two printed lines each turned the new tests red; restored, green. The doctor callers' selection read 245 passed and the canary 42 passed. Under pytest, `tests/conftest.py` sets the variable empty for the whole session, so every other doctor test sees no record.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: `remedy doctor core` prints one more line, and its `--json` output carries one more key; nothing it decides changes. The record exists only on machines that run this repository's tests, so an operator elsewhere reads that no record was found.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a new module under `packages/orchestration/`, REJECTED because the generated import-reachability list would have to grow for one function that only doctor core calls; (b) a warning above a CPU threshold, REJECTED because T004 asks for a sentence and a threshold nobody has ruled on would be invented here.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `last_day_test_load`, its two sentence constants, the `test_load` field and key, the two printed lines, `TestDoctorCoreTestLoad`, and `test_load` from the two exact-key lists.

## DECISION F293 D8 — A test run that leaves a process behind fails: the controller marks the run, finds what is left at its end, ends it and fails the run (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: F293 T003 orders that "a test run that leaves a process behind fails", and finding R-1118 records the case that made the order: the never-ready helper of `test_readiness_timeout_stops_the_tree_and_leaves_no_state` in `tests/runtimes/test_dev_server.py` was found alive eleven days after its run. That helper is started by `DevServer`, whose child spawn (`packages/runtimes/dev_server.py`, through `plan_child_spawn` and the `runtime-server` allowlist) strips every environment variable it does not declare, in its own session, so neither the environment nor the process group can tie it to the run. The test itself stopped the helper only through `wait_ready`, so a failed setup assertion before that call left it running.

CHOSEN: `tests/load_governor.py` gains `RUN_MARK_VARIABLE` (`PYTEST_REMEDY_RUN_MARK`), `new_run_mark`, `leftover_processes(mark, folders)`, `end_processes(procs, grace)` and `leftover_notice(ended)`. The controller of every run, in `pytest_configure` in `tests/conftest.py`, puts a fresh mark into its environment before any worker starts. In `pytest_sessionfinish`, now `trylast` so that pytest-xdist has already shut its workers down, the controller lists this user's processes, other than itself and its parents, whose environment carries the mark or whose working folder or one of whose arguments lies inside the run's temporary folder (`getbasetemp()`, compared on a separator boundary so that `pytest-78` never matches `pytest-789`). Each gets `LEFTOVER_GRACE_SECONDS` (3.0) to finish exiting, then is terminated and, if it still lives, killed; when any was ended the run's exit status becomes `TESTS_FAILED` and one red line names each process. A zombie has already ended and is not counted. The variable's name does not start with `REMEDY_` because every run's input snapshot records each `REMEDY_` variable, and a value that changes per run must not reach it. The dev-server test now stops its helper in a `finally` when the helper is still running. Six new tests in `TestNoProcessLeftBehind` in `tests/regression/test_test_load_governor.py` pin it, the last of them a nested run (`-p tests.conftest`, `-n 0`) whose one test leaves a process behind in R-1118's shape, with a stripped environment and its own session: that run exits 1, prints the line with the process's pid, and the process is gone. The reviewer's mutations in a disposable worktree at `d56068b35`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/regression/test_test_load_governor.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider`: the run never failed; the mark never read; the folder test without the separator boundary; the parents not skipped; no grace before ending; the folder never read; and the hook ordered `tryfirst`, which reported the three xdist workers as left behind and turned four existing nested-run tests red. Each turned at least one test red; before them the file read 27 passed, and after the restore the neighbour selection (`tests/runtimes/test_dev_server.py`, the governor file, `tests/regression/test_data_root_guard.py`, `tests/test_data_root_isolation.py`, `tests/test_test_categories.py`, `tests/regression/test_resource_safety.py`, `tests/ui_contracts/test_vitest_worker_cap.py`) read 101 passed, `tests/runtimes` read 256 passed and 5 skipped with no process reported, and the canary 42 passed. One scan of the 614 processes then on this machine cost 0.037 CPU seconds.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. A test run that leaves a process alive at its end now fails and names that process, and the process no longer outlives the run. A run killed outright (SIGKILL) still cannot check anything; a process that strips its environment and runs outside the run's temporary folder is not seen.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) making the controller a child subreaper so that orphans return to it, REJECTED because under `-n 0` the controller is also the test process, and orphaned grandchildren would then become its zombies in tests that count zombies; (b) the environment mark alone, REJECTED because it misses R-1118's own shape; (c) a variable named `REMEDY_TEST_RUN_MARK`, REJECTED for the input snapshot reason above.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the five names above from `tests/load_governor.py` with the `uuid` import, the mark lines in `pytest_configure` and the leftover block and `trylast` in `pytest_sessionfinish` of `tests/conftest.py`, `TestNoProcessLeftBehind` and its helpers, and the `finally` in the dev-server test.

## DECISION F293 D9 — Each closure's suite transcript carries the run's CPU seconds from the test load record, and a closure more than 10 percent above the previous one owes a finding (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: F293 T003 orders that each closure's suite transcript records the run's CPU seconds, and that a closure whose suite costs more than 10 percent above the previous feature's registers a finding owned by the rolling findings paydown. The transcripts (`.agent/authored/f<id>-closure-suite.txt`) are free text a worker writes, and none carries a CPU reading; the reading exists only as one line of the test load record, which `tests/conftest.py` appends after every run.

CHOSEN: a script, `scripts/closure_suite_cost.py`, run by hand once in the integration-gate round (docs/agents/integration_gate.md step 1; STATUS_closure_protocol.md precondition 2). It takes the closing feature's id and the record file, finds the newest record line whose command is exactly `pytest -n auto -q` (the closure's command as `tests/conftest.py` records it), and prints one `Test load:` line with that run's CPU seconds, wall seconds, tests collected, exit status and time, which the worker copies into the transcript. It then reads the `Test load:` line of every other transcript under `.agent/authored/`, takes the newest one recorded before this run, and prints one sentence comparing the two. It exits 1 when this closure costs more than 10 percent more, 0 when it does not or when no earlier transcript carries the line, and 2 when the record cannot be read or holds no line for the command. The line it prints is the line it reads back, through one regular expression, so a later closure can always read an earlier one. The script joins `ALLOWED_UNWIRED` in `tests/test_no_orphan_modules.py`, beside the other closure tools run by hand. Eleven tests in `tests/orchestration/test_closure_suite_cost.py` pin it, two of them through the command line. The reviewer's mutations in a disposable worktree at `4b66720a7`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/orchestration/test_closure_suite_cost.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider`: the limit made inclusive; the closing feature's own transcript read; transcripts recorded after the run read; every command counted; exit code 0 above the limit; the printed line's unit changed; a malformed time kept. Each turned at least one test red; restored, the file read 11 passed. Removing the `ALLOWED_UNWIRED` entry turned `test_no_module_is_an_orphan` red. Run against this machine's record on 2026-09-30, the script exits 2, because no run of exactly `pytest -n auto -q` is recorded yet (T001's baseline run carried `--durations=0`); F293's own closure is therefore the first transcript to carry the line, and the first comparison falls to the feature after it.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. The closure sequence gains one command and two lines in the suite transcript, and a closure that costs much more than the one before it now leaves a finding instead of passing unnoticed.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a check inside `remedy integrity check`, REJECTED because the record lives in the operator's home folder and a repository check must not depend on one machine's files; (b) reading `REMEDY_TEST_LOAD_LOG` inside the script, REJECTED because modules under `scripts/` cannot import the variable registry (`tests/orchestration/test_env_registry.py` says why) and a third copy of the path rules would drift, so the path is given on the command line; (c) comparing with T001's baseline instead of the previous closure, REJECTED because T003 names the previous feature's closure.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the script, its test file and its `ALLOWED_UNWIRED` entry, and the sentences naming it in docs/agents/integration_gate.md step 1 and STATUS_closure_protocol.md precondition 2.

## DECISION F293 D10 — The mission command tests start their setup missions in-process; the git work of a whole job run is the largest cost the end-to-end tests still carry (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: T002 cuts where a measured CPU saving exists. The reviewer measured the largest remaining files serially in one disposable worktree at `c8ed7cf52` (`pytest <file> -q -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider`, CPU seconds from a scratch test load record): `tests/cli/test_do_sequence_cli.py` 61.66, `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py` 57.95, `tests/cli/test_mission_cmd.py` 42.28, `tests/orchestration/test_review_zip_hygiene.py` 32.54, `tests/runtimes/test_supervisor_portability.py` 29.60 (at 103.99 wall seconds, mostly waiting), `tests/cli/test_do_commit_flags.py` 24.72, `tests/test_grouped_cli.py` 20.42, `tests/cli/test_scoped_listings.py` 14.75. In `tests/cli/test_mission_cmd.py` the helper `_start`, which 62 call sites use as setup, started a child `mission start` process for each mission, while the command itself is tested by `TestStart`.

CHOSEN: `_start` creates the mission in-process with `create_mission(project_id, goal)` inside the file's existing `_in_data_root`, as the file's other setup helpers already do; every call passes a project id, so the command's own lookup of a slug is not needed. The file then read 30.50 CPU seconds against 42.28, 114 passed both times. The reviewer's mutations in the same worktree: `show --json` without each link's job state turned `TestShow::test_show_json_carries_each_link_state` red; a mission saved without its goal turned 28 tests red, among them `TestList` tests whose missions come from `_start`; restored, 114 passed.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAYS ABOUT THE REST: the golden-path file and the `do` sequence file run a whole job through the command line in a child process, which is what they test. One such `remedy do` run of a one-task job on the fake providers, profiled at `c8ed7cf52`, used 2.19 CPU seconds, about half of it in the 210 git processes the job runner starts: three readings of `worktree_identity` (18 git commands, 0.41 seconds), 31 calls of `write_tree_at` (0.45 seconds) and 15 of `capture_target_state` (0.25 seconds). Making a job run start fewer git processes would speed up every real job as well as these tests, but it changes the job runner, which is product work beyond a test diet; the closure's full-suite reading decides whether the 40 percent target is met without it.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. Those tests still read every mission through the real command line in a child process; only the setup missions are written directly.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) sharing one project and mission between tests, REJECTED because several tests change a mission's status and would see each other's changes; (b) running the mission commands in-process too, REJECTED because the file exists to show what an operator sees from the command line.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore `_start` to run `mission start --json` through `_run` and read the id from its output.

## DECISION F293 D11 — The acceptance audit's findings: two gaps repaired by one test file, two statements decided by measurement at closure (2026-09-30)

THE PROBLEM: SLOW MODE's hardening stage (operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap) had a fresh auditor, given only the feature file and the repository, name and prove by mutation a test for every claim under F293's Acceptance and Goal & Done headings. Its report, `.agent/f293_acceptance_audit.md`, audited eight claims at `65018abe6`: four had a proving test at once (a closure costing more than 10 percent above the previous one owes a finding; a test run that leaves a process behind fails; `remedy doctor core` prints the sentence from the record; and it prints nothing wrong when the record is absent), two of those through the command line; two were gaps (T001's inventory, R-1121; no assertion lost, R-1122); and two can only be decided by a measurement (the full suite's 40 percent target, and the round selections costing much less).

CHOSEN: one test file, `tests/regression/test_f293_acceptance.py`, repairs both gaps. `TestTheInventoryHoldsItsSixReadings` requires the inventory's six readings in order, its hundred slowest-test rows ranked 1 to 100 with each row's seconds, phase and node id found in the committed output of the one full-suite run (`.agent/authored/f293-r1-durations.txt`), and the record's totals of that run quoted in the inventory. `TestNoAssertionWasLost` counts, with `ast`, the `assert` statements and `pytest.raises` / `pytest.warns` uses of every test module F293 changed that existed at the fork point `8a067a3b9`, and requires no fewer than there; the table `FLOOR` was printed by a script over `git show 8a067a3b9:<path>`, not typed. `ALLOWED_REMOVALS` names the five `assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr` lines round 6 removed from `tests/cli/test_mission_cmd.py`: each checked only that a child process writing a setup record exited 0, and the in-process call that replaced it raises when the write fails. A later change that removes an assertion from one of those modules on purpose lowers its floor in the same commit with the reason, as the blind-handler ratchet asks of its number. The reviewer's mutations in a disposable worktree at `65018abe6`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/regression/test_f293_acceptance.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider`: a reading's heading renamed; a slowest-test row removed; a row's seconds changed; the totals changed; an `assert` turned into an assignment in `tests/orchestration/test_job_task_runner.py`, which sits at its floor; the allowance dropped; and the counter blind to `pytest.raises`. Each turned at least one test red; restored, the file read 5 passed. The same `assert` turned into an assignment in `tests/orchestration/test_dead_command_check.py` stayed green, correctly: that module holds 8 against a floor of 3, and the claim is about the assertions that existed where F293 began. The repository's scanners over `tests/` and the other roots read 158 passed with the new file in place.

THE TWO MEASURED STATEMENTS: the 40 percent target is read at the closure's one full-suite run (DECISION F293 D1) against T001's 1246.09 CPU seconds, and when it is missed the closure's DECISION states the remaining cost with DECISION F293 D10's numbers. "The round selections cost much less" is shown by the per-file readings DECISIONs F293 D2 to D6 and D10 record, each taken before and after its cut in one tree, and by the rules that stopped repeated runs (DECISION amend0930 D1 to D3); the closure's record names them.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. Two statements of the feature file that only people checked are now checked by tests.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) comparing with the fork point through `git show` at test time, REJECTED because the test would then need the fork commit in the local git history at every run, which a tree copied without its history does not have, while a table printed once from the fork point needs nothing at test time and shows its numbers to a reviewer; (b) floors at the tip's counts, REJECTED because the claim is about the assertions that existed before F293, and a floor at the tip would stop F293's own tests from ever being reorganised.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `tests/regression/test_f293_acceptance.py`.
