## DECISION F293 D14 — The closure's self-use item SU-040 lands: the task-progress probe of `remedy dev status` catches the four errors it can meet, and two tests pin it through the command line (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: F293's closure consumes one self-use item (docs/roadmap/STATUS_closure_protocol.md precondition 6). The queue held none, and the generator's tier 4 supplied `SU-040`: the handler at line 100 of `apps/cli/commands/dev.py`, around the task-progress probe of `remedy dev status`, caught every exception under an excused `# noqa: BLE001` mark. Round 18 ran the item to its approval gate (job `2e0772c99fcd47fc`, the `self_use` role on `claude-cli`, 2 provider calls, $0.69, reviewer verdict pass, no run defect) and never applied it; the job's change, saved in `.agent/selfuse_f293/job_diff.txt`, narrows the handler to `(ImportError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError)` and lowers `MAX_EXCUSED` in `tests/test_ble001_ratchet.py` from 288 to 287. No test covered the handler.

CHOSEN: the job's two-line change lands as the job wrote it, before the closure's one full suite, so that suite runs on the tree that ships. The four types are the ones the probe can meet: an import that no longer resolves, a missing `version` key, a changed call signature and a missing attribute. Two new tests in `TestDevStatusCommandSchema` of `tests/regression/test_named_bugs.py` drive `remedy dev status --json` through `apps.cli.main.main`: for each of the four errors, the command still answers `ok` with `task_progress_ok` false and `ui_contract_ok` true, so the other checks are still reported; and a `RuntimeError` from the probe is no longer read as a failed check, so the command exits 1 with the error's name in its JSON envelope. The reviewer's mutations in a disposable worktree at `8977a0a98`, each run with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` as `python3 -m pytest tests/regression/test_named_bugs.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider -k DevStatus`: the handler widened back to `Exception`; each of the four types dropped in turn; and `RuntimeError` added to the tuple. Each turned one test red; restored, 13 passed.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: `remedy dev status` still reports a broken task-progress probe as a failed check when the probe fails in one of the four expected ways. A defect of any other kind now stops the command with its own name, where before it was hidden as a failed check.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) adding `ValueError` to the tuple, REJECTED because `JobPlan` is a dataclass and the probe parses nothing, so no path raises it; (b) narrowing the sibling handler at line 90 in the same change, REJECTED because the item names one mark, and that one belongs to `SU-039`, whose empty run is finding R-1117, owned by the rolling paydown.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore the handler's `except Exception:` line with its `# noqa: BLE001` mark, set `MAX_EXCUSED` back to 288, and delete the two tests named above.

## DECISION F293 D15 — F293 closes at a 24.5 percent cut; the rest of T002 moves to F294, registered directly after it (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: F293's Goal & Done asks for the full suite's CPU seconds at least 40 percent below T001's baseline, OR a dated DECISION showing with numbers that what remains cannot be made cheaper without weakening a test. The closure's one full suite, re-run in round 21 on the tree that ships, used 940.64 CPU seconds for 21,145 collected tests (`.agent/authored/f293-closure-suite.txt`), 24.5 percent below T001's 1,246.09; the target is at most 747.65, so about 193 CPU seconds are missing. The second branch does not hold either: what remains can still be made cheaper. DECISION F293 D10 measured the largest known part, the git work of a whole job run (one `remedy do` of a one-task job used 2.19 CPU seconds, about half of it in 210 git processes), which is product work in the job runner rather than a change to the tests. F293 stands at session 6 and round 22, below the soft limit of 7 sessions and 25 rounds.

CHOSEN: split and close, the standing default of operator amendment amend0905-throughput, taken here one session before the limit because the remaining work is a different kind of work. F293 closes at the scope it reached: T001, T003 and T004 complete, T002 complete for the cuts of DECISIONs F293 D2 to D6 and D10. The rest of T002 is registered as F294, "Test load diet, part two" (`docs/roadmap/features/T2_F294.md`), placed directly after F293 under the same Tier 2 heading (amend0906-split-placement), so Rule A5 proposes it next. Its file names F293 as its parent, starts from the round 21 reading, carries T002 and its Acceptance line word for word, and names the job runner's git work and the three files that run whole jobs through the command line as the first things to measure. The registration lands in one commit with the `TOTAL_FEATURES` pin (294), the README's overall count (121 of 294) and its Tier 2 row (39 of 42). F293's Built State states the reading and the split. Because this changes the order of work and closes a feature short of its number, it is written to the operator questions file as a reversible ruling (amend0911-feedback rule C, kind B; amend0917-throughput rule 5).

THE NUMBERS BEHIND THE CUT: T001's run, 1,246.09 CPU seconds and 355.02 wall seconds for 21,102 collected tests; the closure run, 940.64 CPU seconds and 276.83 wall seconds for 21,145. The cuts, each measured before and after in one tree: the dead-command scan and its answers cached per root (D2, D4; `tests/cli/test_worker_facade_cmd.py` 22.04 to 2.83 CPU seconds serially), the review manifest's metadata scan cached per text (D3; the gate-matrix file 29.64 to 5.26), the run manifest's key check cached per key and use (D5; the job runner file 70.59 to 54.17 in one worktree), Remedy's own checkout identity read once per test process (D6; the same file 55.23 to 12.66), and the mission tests' setup written in-process (D10; 42.28 to 30.50). Two provider-override tests no longer start a paid model process (R-1119), and one retry test no longer sleeps through a 30-second backoff.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) more test-only cuts in F293 before closing, REJECTED because the files T001 ranked highest that are left either wait rather than compute (the supervisor and runtime lifecycle files, which the CPU reading barely counts) or run whole jobs, which is what they test, so the cuts left are a few CPU seconds each and every attempt to prove them at whole-suite scale costs another full run of about 940 CPU seconds; (b) ruling that nothing more can be cut, REJECTED because D10's numbers show that the job runner's git work can be cut; (c) waiting for the operator, REJECTED because operator questions never stall a feature (amend0917-throughput rule 5).

HOW TO REVERSE: delete F294's STATUS line and `docs/roadmap/features/T2_F294.md`, set `TOTAL_FEATURES` back to 293 with its comment, the README's overall count back to 293 and its Tier 2 row back to 41, and re-open F293 (`[~]`) with T002 as its remaining slice.

## DECISION F294 D1 — One `worktree_identity` reading discovers the repository's configured helpers once, and F294 cuts the job runner's git work first (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: F294 must take the full suite from F293's closure reading, 940.64 CPU seconds, to at most 747.65. DECISION F293 D10 named the largest known cost: the git processes a whole job run starts. The reviewer re-counted them at `020bc9a16` with an in-process one-task `remedy do` on the fake providers, the shape of `tests/cli/test_do_sequence_cli.py`, counting every git process by its subcommand: 210 per run. 18 of them were `git config --name-only --get-regexp` discoveries of the repository's configured helpers (the F7 rule that a reading never runs a repository's clean, smudge, process, diff or fsmonitor command): `worktree_identity` runs six git commands per reading, the job run takes three readings, and `_git_bytes` discovered the helpers again before each command, though nothing between two commands of one reading changes them.

CHOSEN: `worktree_identity` opens a scope for its reading, the context variable `_READING_HELPER_ARGS` in `packages/orchestration/run_manifest.py`, and `_helper_neutralizing_args` answers a directory's second and later commands from it. The scope is a fresh dictionary per reading and per thread, and it ends with the reading, so the next reading always discovers afresh. Only a discovery that ended with git's own answer is remembered, exit 0 (helpers listed) or exit 1 (nothing configured); a discovery that raised or failed otherwise is retried by the next command, as before. The reading's body moved unchanged into `_read_worktree_identity`, and `_git_bytes` keeps its signature, which two tests in `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_integrity.py` replace with a lambda of that shape. One run then starts 195 git processes, 3 of them discoveries, read twice in each tree; its CPU seconds, 1.40 and 1.23 at the base against 1.37 and 1.21 after, move less than they vary between two runs, so this cut is counted in processes. Four new tests in `TestOneHelperDiscoveryPerReading` of the same test file pin it: a reading discovers once and runs six commands; with a clean filter configured every one of the six carries its neutralization; a reading after the filter was configured discovers afresh and neutralizes it; and a discovery that times out is retried by the next command. The reviewer's mutations in the dry tree on `020bc9a16`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest <the new class> tests/cli/test_job_rerun_workspace_security.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, against a control of 17 passed: no scope opened (3 failed); one memo shared by every reading (2 failed, one of them the existing canary `test_a_filter_process_never_runs`); a reuse that drops the discovered helpers (6 failed, four of them existing canaries); a failed discovery remembered (1 failed); and git's exit 1 not remembered (2 failed). The file was restored byte for byte after each.

THE ORDER OF F294: the job runner's git work first, one kind of repeated reading per round, each measured before and after in one tree by the reviewer's count; then the three files that run whole jobs through the command line are measured and cut from the top of what remains; then the amend0930b-slow-cap hardening stage; then closure, whose one full suite gives the "after" reading.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing a user sees. A job run starts 15 fewer git processes, and every git command of a reading is still run with every configured helper neutralized.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) one discovery per directory for the whole process, REJECTED because a repository can gain a helper between two readings, and the later reading would then run it, which the existing canary turned red under that mutation; (b) a new keyword argument on `_git_bytes` carrying the discovered helpers, REJECTED because two existing tests replace `_git_bytes` with a lambda of its present signature; (c) a module-level dictionary set and cleared by `worktree_identity`, REJECTED because two threads reading at once would share it.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore `worktree_identity` and `_helper_neutralizing_args` from `020bc9a16`, delete `_READING_HELPER_ARGS`, `_read_worktree_identity` and the `contextvars` import, and delete `TestOneHelperDiscoveryPerReading`, `_recording_git`, `_split` and `_DISCOVERY` from `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_integrity.py`.

## DECISION F294 D2 — Every test's data root comes from one parent per test process, made once, so no test lists the base temporary directory to number its root (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: `tests/conftest.py::_isolated_data_root` (finding R-0803) gave every test a fresh data root with `tmp_path_factory.mktemp("remedy-data")`. pytest numbers such a directory by listing the whole base temporary directory of the test process and taking the highest number with that prefix plus one, so each of the roughly 3,500 tests an xdist worker runs in the full suite listed every root made before it, and every `tmp_path` a test asked for listed them too. The reviewer measured pytest's own `make_numbered_dir` in a scratch directory, one worker's share of the suite simulated as 3,500 tests each making one numbered root and every second test one numbered `tmp_path` directory: 5.93 CPU seconds. The same with the roots made inside one parent, made once, by a counter: 0.63 CPU seconds. Over the six workers of the full suite that is about 30 CPU seconds of the about 193 that F294 still has to cut.

CHOSEN: a session-scoped fixture `_data_root_allocator` in `tests/conftest.py` makes one numbered `remedy-data` parent per test process with `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` and returns a function that makes the next root inside it, `<parent>/<n>`, a new directory made with mode `0o700`, the mode `mktemp` uses. `_isolated_data_root` asks for that fixture instead of `tmp_path_factory` and sets `REMEDY_DATA_DIR` to the next root; everything else it does is unchanged, including leaving alone a value a module- or class-scoped fixture already set. Each test still gets its own new, empty directory under the base temporary directory, and every child process still inherits it. A new test in `tests/test_data_root_isolation.py`, `test_every_root_is_a_new_directory_under_one_parent`, takes the test's own root and two more from the allocator and requires three different directories with one parent, all empty. The reviewer's mutations in the dry tree on `e6312ed80`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/test_data_root_isolation.py tests/regression/test_data_root_guard.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, against a control of 9 passed: one directory reused for every root, and roots no longer taken from the allocator's parent, each turned the new test red; no directory made turned it and `test_each_test_gets_a_fresh_empty_root` red. The file was restored byte for byte after each. A selection of the suite large enough to show the saving would itself cost hundreds of CPU seconds, so the saving is read at the closure's one full suite.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product and nothing a test can rely on: each test's data root is a new empty directory as before, now named `remedy-data<k>/<n>` instead of `remedy-data<n>` under the same base directory.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) one data root shared by every test of a process, REJECTED because R-0803's guard and many tests rely on a fresh empty root; (b) `tempfile.mkdtemp` under the base directory, REJECTED because its random names make a root harder to find from a failing test's output, while the counter needs no listing either.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `_data_root_allocator`, give `_isolated_data_root` its `tmp_path_factory` argument back and set the variable to `str(tmp_path_factory.mktemp("remedy-data"))`, and delete `test_every_root_is_a_new_directory_under_one_parent`.

## DECISION F294 D3 — A reading runs `git submodule status` only when the index holds a submodule (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: one in-process one-task `remedy do`, profiled at `4d92d0e4f`, spends 0.71 CPU seconds in its own Python and 1.13 in the processes it starts, almost all of them git. The reviewer measured each git command a reading runs, 40 times in a one-file repository on this machine's git 2.34.1: every one costs 2.0 to 3.7 milliseconds of CPU except `git submodule status`, 58.5, because on this version it is a shell script. `worktree_identity` runs it once per reading, and a job run takes two readings with Remedy's own checkout frozen as the suite freezes it (DECISION F293 D6), three without. On Remedy's own checkout of 8,226 files it costs 64.0 milliseconds against 8.0 for `git ls-files --stage -z`.

CHOSEN: `_submodule_status` in `packages/orchestration/run_manifest.py` lists the index with `git ls-files --stage -z` through `_git_bytes`, so every configured helper stays neutralized, and runs `git submodule status` only when that listing holds a gitlink (an entry of mode 160000) or when the listing itself failed; otherwise it answers as the command does with no gitlink, success and no output. The reviewer read git 2.34.1's answers in a scratch repository: with no gitlink the command prints nothing and exits 0, even when `.gitmodules` is malformed; with a gitlink and no mapping it exits 128; with a real submodule it prints its line. So the identity's digest, its `dirty` flag and its problems are the same either way, and a reading still runs six git commands. Four new tests in `TestSubmoduleStatusOnlyWithASubmodule` of `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_integrity.py` pin it, each against the reading as it was where that matters: without a submodule, and with a malformed `.gitmodules`, the command never runs and the identity equals the old reading's; with a real submodule it runs once and the identity equals the old reading's, `dirty` included; a gitlink without a mapping still makes the identity incomplete with a `submodules:` problem; and a failed index listing falls back to the command. The reviewer's mutations in the dry tree on `4d92d0e4f`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest <the new class> <the class of DECISION F294 D1> -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, against a control of 8 passed: the probe always skipping (3 failed), never skipping (4 failed), a failed listing read as no submodule (1 failed), and the wrong mode (4 failed). The file was restored byte for byte after each. Measured with Remedy's identity frozen, three alternating runs each of one one-task `remedy do` in two fresh worktrees: the processes the run starts used 0.913 CPU seconds on average at the base and 0.850 after.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing a user sees. A reading of a repository without submodules no longer starts the submodule script, which makes every job run, and every reading of Remedy's own checkout, cheaper.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) asking `.gitmodules` instead of the index, REJECTED because the command lists the index, and a gitlink without a mapping, which makes the identity incomplete today, would then be skipped; (b) dropping submodules from the identity, REJECTED because a submodule's state is part of what a reading promises to cover.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `_submodule_status`, call `_git_bytes(repo_path, ["submodule", "status"])` in its place again, and delete `TestSubmoduleStatusOnlyWithASubmodule`, `_always_submodule_status` and `_ran_submodule_status` from `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_integrity.py`.

## DECISION F294 D4 — The golden-path tests run `init`, `do` and `status` in the test process; the file's other commands stay child processes (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py` is the canary every round runs and one of the costliest files of the full suite. Its three helpers `_init_project`, `_run_do` and `_run_status`, which most of its 42 tests use as setup and as the command under test, each started `python -m apps.cli.grouped` as a child process. A child starts a fresh interpreter, imports the command line again and reads Remedy's own checkout identity again, which the test process has already read once (DECISION F293 D6). The reviewer measured `init` and `do` of one order in a scratch repository, three times each: 1.77 CPU seconds as two child processes, 1.38 in-process with the imports warm. DECISION F293 D10 had read the child process as what this file tests; the file's own words, "Tests for the golden-path CLI", and its assertions, on output, exit codes and the records a run leaves, are about the commands, and the module entry point is still proven by the commands this decision leaves as children.

CHOSEN: the three helpers call `_in_process`, a new helper in the same file, which runs `apps.cli.grouped.main` in the test process the way `subprocess.run` ran the child: with the child's environment (the whole of `os.environ` is replaced by the helper's `env` and restored afterwards), the repository as working directory, an empty stdin, stdout and stderr captured as text, and the child's exit code: 0 when `main` returns, the code of a `SystemExit`, 1 with the message on stderr for a `SystemExit` that carries text, and 1 with the traceback on stderr for an exception nothing caught. It returns a `subprocess.CompletedProcess`, so no test body changed and no assertion was touched. The commands the tests run inline, `job show`, `job stop`, `decision list`, `do run`, `--help` and every printed `Next:` line, still run as child processes. `tests/cli/test_do_sequence_cli.py` already runs `do` in-process 46 times through the same `main`. The reviewer's mutations in the dry tree on `46b9d303f`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/cli/test_golden_path.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, against a control of 42 passed: an empty order exiting 3 in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` (2 failed); the stop line of `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py` reworded (1 failed); the helper reporting every exit code as 0 (2 failed); and the helper ignoring the child's environment (17 failed). Each file was restored byte for byte. The file run serially read 52.51 CPU seconds in the primary checkout at `46b9d303f` and 40.08 in the dry tree; the dry tree is a fresh worktree whose remaining child processes read a checkout with a cold index, so the saving of at least 12.4 CPU seconds per run is a floor.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. The golden-path tests check the same output, exit codes and records with the same assertions, and they finish sooner.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) running every command of the file in-process, REJECTED because the file would then no longer start the command line as a program at all; (b) one shared `init` and `do` per module, REJECTED because pytest-xdist here sends single tests to whichever worker is free, so a module-scoped run is repeated on most workers, and several tests need a project with no job or a corrupted record.

HOW TO REVERSE: give `_init_project`, `_run_do` and `_run_status` back their `subprocess.run([*_CLI, ...], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, cwd=str(repo), env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)` bodies and delete `_in_process`.

## DECISION F294 D5 — The in-process command line moves to `tests/cli/in_process_cli.py`, and the scoped-listing tests run their setup through it (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: `tests/cli/test_scoped_listings.py` read 20.98 CPU seconds for 20 tests, run serially in the primary checkout at `46b9d303f`. Its setup helpers started a child process for every `init` (eleven calls in the file), every `do` that creates a job to list (ten) and every `project current` that names the slug a test expects (five), while the subject of its command-line tests is the listings, `job list`, `status` and `stats failures`, read as the program prints them. DECISION F294 D4 had written the helper that runs the command line in the test process inside `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py`; a second file needing it would have copied it.

CHOSEN: two commits. First the helper moves unchanged into the new module `tests/cli/in_process_cli.py` as `run_cli_in_process(args, cwd, env)`, beside `CLI_CHILD_ARGV`, the child command it stands in for, as `tests/cli/runtime_helpers.py` already holds shared helpers for this directory; `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py` imports it and its three helpers call it, and no test body changes. Then `_init_project`, `_create_job` and `_get_project_slug` of `tests/cli/test_scoped_listings.py` call it, keeping their own assertions, while `_run_cli`, which every listing a test asserts on goes through, still starts the child process; no test body changes there either. The reviewer's mutations in the dry tree on `129437ee4`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/cli/test_golden_path.py tests/cli/test_scoped_listings.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, against a control of 62 passed: a job planned by `do` without its project in `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py` turned `test_full_isolation_and_flags` red; the shared helper reporting every exit code as 0 turned the two empty-order golden-path tests red; and the shared helper ignoring the child's environment turned 22 tests red. Each file was restored byte for byte. The scoped-listing file run serially read 16.54 CPU seconds in the dry tree against 20.98 in the primary checkout; the dry tree's remaining child processes read a checkout with a cold index, so the saving of at least 4.4 CPU seconds per run is a floor.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. The scoped-listing tests check the same listings, printed by the same program, with the same assertions.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) importing the helper from `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py`, REJECTED because a test module is not a library, and a later change to that file would then reach another; (b) running the listings in-process too, REJECTED because the listings as the program prints them are what that file tests.

HOW TO REVERSE: give the three helpers of `tests/cli/test_scoped_listings.py` back their child-process bodies from `129437ee4`, move `run_cli_in_process` back into `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py` as `_in_process`, and delete `tests/cli/in_process_cli.py`.

## DECISION F294 D6 — Where the suite's CPU still goes after F294's cuts, and why the building rounds end here (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: F294 must take the full suite to at most 747.65 CPU seconds from F293's closure reading of 940.64. Its rounds 1 to 5 landed five cuts, each measured before and after in one tree: one discovery of a repository's configured helpers per identity reading (DECISION F294 D1, 210 to 195 git processes per one-task `remedy do`); every test's data root from one parent per test process (D2, about 30 CPU seconds of a full suite by the simulation that decision records); `git submodule status` only when the index holds a submodule (D3, the processes a one-task run starts from 0.913 to 0.850 CPU seconds); the golden-path tests' `init`, `do` and `status` in the test process (D4, 52.51 to at most 40.08 CPU seconds per run of the file); and the scoped-listing tests' setup in the test process (D5, 20.98 to at most 16.54). Read file by file they come to roughly 47 CPU seconds of a full suite plus a few hundredths of a second per job run, well short of the about 193 still needed. Only the closure's one full suite gives their real sum.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, so the next session starts from numbers: each file run alone and serially with `python3 -B -m pytest <file> -q -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider`, CPU of the whole process tree. In the primary checkout at `129437ee4`: `tests/cli/test_plan_approval.py` 7.07 (31 tests), `tests/cli/test_config_cmd.py` 3.61 (19), `tests/cli/test_scoped_listings.py` 20.98 (20), `tests/test_grouped_cli.py` 20.35 (302), `tests/test_command_discovery.py` 5.68 (98). At `720fc70b2`: `tests/orchestration/test_job_apply_commit.py` 47.43 (59 tests), `tests/orchestration/test_persisted_call_ownership.py` 19.37 (25), `tests/orchestration/test_job_evidence.py` 9.60 (94), `tests/orchestration/test_disk_floor.py` 5.15 (31), `tests/orchestration/test_job_stop_integration.py` 3.27 (26), `tests/orchestration/test_exec_guard.py` 2.85 (47, 17.08 seconds of wall time, most of it waiting), `tests/orchestration/test_mission_e2e.py` 1.96 (24), `tests/orchestration/test_run_manifest_cross_episode_concurrency.py` 1.54 (12, 31.14 seconds of wall time, waiting). A research agent read, in a worktree at `020bc9a16`, `tests/cli/test_do_sequence_cli.py` 61.41, `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py` 63.05 and `tests/cli/test_do_commit_flags.py` 34.00. One in-process one-task `remedy do` on the fake providers at `720fc70b2`, with Remedy's own identity frozen as the suite freezes it, used 0.68 CPU seconds in its own Python and 0.82 in the processes it started: 188 git processes, one `uname -p`, and one `python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests -q`, the definition-of-done gate checking the target's tests. Its git work is 31 tree snapshots (`write_tree_at`, three processes each), 15 of them from `capture_target_state`, which the job runner calls at every safe point to absorb a human change (DECISION F263 D-E), 14 times for one task.

WHAT THE NUMBERS SAY: the costliest files left each run a real job in every test and then change what the job left, by applying it, committing it or tampering with its records, so no two tests can share one run; and pytest-xdist here sends single tests to whichever worker is free, so a run shared by a module would be repeated on most workers anyway. Inside a job run, what remains is the job runner's own work: the absorbs at every safe point and the definition-of-done gate's test run. Making either cheaper changes what every job run does for the operator, the detection of a human edit and the gate that releases a job, which is product behaviour and not a test diet. The smaller repeated readings left, such as the ten `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` calls of `repo_root`, from five modules, that the research count at `020bc9a16` found in one run, would save about 30 milliseconds per job run at a risk out of proportion to it.

CHOSEN: F294's building rounds end at round 5. The next session runs the amend0930b-slow-cap hardening stage on F294's Acceptance and Goal & Done, then the closure sequence, whose one full suite gives the "after" reading. If that reading misses 747.65, the closure decides between the two routes DECISION F293 D15 weighed, a ruling with the numbers or a split, and writes the trade-off to the operator questions file, because what remains can only be cut by changing what a job run does.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing. This decision records measurements and the order of the next rounds.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) fewer absorbs per task, REJECTED inside a test diet because it delays the detection of an operator's edit in every real job to save CPU in the tests; (b) copying one finished job's records into each test of the apply-commit and call-ownership files, REJECTED because the records carry the absolute paths of the repository and the data root they were written for; (c) caching `repo_root` per path, REJECTED for the reason above.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete this decision and the Built State section of `docs/roadmap/features/T2_F294.md`, and put a building round back at the head of `.agent/plan.md`'s Next Steps.

## DECISION F294 D7 — The acceptance audit's findings: two gaps repaired by tests, the 40 percent target and its DECISION alternative decided at closure (2026-10-01)

## DECISION F294 D8 — The repeat audit: the allocator test forbids any directory listing, and a digest change in the review table is the review record (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: the hardening stage's repeat audit (operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap), run by a fresh auditor at `01c05e027` from the feature file and the repository alone, re-audited the two statements that had gaps; its report is `.agent/f294_acceptance_reaudit1.md`. It confirmed both of round 7's repairs under its own mutations and reported one miss for each. (1) For "without losing a single assertion": an assertion that existed at the fork point, weakened to a tautology in the same commit that writes the weakened unit's new digest into `REVIEWED_CHANGES`, passes both checks. (2) For the data root: an allocator that calls pytest's own `make_numbered_dir` on the base temporary directory, instead of `tmp_path_factory.mktemp`, lists that whole directory again and passes `test_a_root_is_made_without_numbering_the_base_directory`, which patched only `mktemp`.

CHOSEN: (1) is not a gap. `REVIEWED_CHANGES` is the review record: a unit may differ from the fork point only by a digest a reviewer read and wrote down with its round and reason, exactly as DECISION F293 D12 built it for F293. A commit that weakens an assertion and adds its digest shows both in one diff, which is the place a review sees it; no test can stop the author of a test from editing it, and a check against `.agent/live_review.md` would only move the same trust into a second file. R-1126 is therefore resolved. (2) is repaired: the test now replaces `os.scandir`, `os.listdir` and `pathlib.Path.iterdir` with a function that raises, only while it asks the allocator for two roots, so any way of numbering a root by listing a directory fails it: `mktemp` and `make_numbered_dir` reach `os.scandir` through pytest's `find_prefixed`, and on the operator's Python 3.10 `Path.iterdir` does not go through `os.listdir`, so both are named. The reviewer's mutations of the allocator in the dry worktree `.remedy-wt/f294-r8-dry` at `01c05e027`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest <the new test> <test_every_root_is_a_new_directory_under_one_parent> -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider`: a `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` call per root; the auditor's `make_numbered_dir` under the base temporary directory; `make_numbered_dir` under the allocator's own parent; numbering by the length of `parent.iterdir()`; and numbering by the length of `os.listdir(parent)`. Each turned the new test red while the shape test stayed green, which is why the shape test alone could not guard D2. Restored, the two acceptance files read 7 passed. R-1127 stays open until the next repeat audit has tried the repaired test.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. One test now catches every way of making a data root that lists a directory, not just one.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) asserting that each root's parent is not the base temporary directory, REJECTED because numbering inside the allocator's own parent would still list a directory that grows with every test of the process; (b) counting directory listings during a whole test, REJECTED because the test body and pytest's own fixtures list directories for reasons of their own.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore round 7's body of `test_a_root_is_made_without_numbering_the_base_directory`, which patched only `tmp_path_factory.mktemp`.

## DECISION F294 D9 — The second repeat audit: allocating a data root may make one directory, and neither list one nor start a process (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: the hardening stage's second repeat audit (operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap), run by a fresh auditor at `cb959bda3` from the feature file and the repository alone, tried six mutations of `tests/conftest.py` against the data-root statement; its report is `.agent/f294_acceptance_reaudit2.md`. Five turned a test red: numbering by `Path.iterdir`, by `os.listdir` and by `os.scandir`, a parent made by `tempfile.mkdtemp` outside pytest, and `_isolated_data_root` making its own root instead of asking the allocator. One stayed green: an allocator that numbers each root by counting the output of a child `ls -1` process over its parent, because round 8's test replaced only Python's own listing functions. The reviewer found a second escape while checking the repair: on the operator's Python 3.10, `Path.glob` and `Path.rglob` reach `os.scandir` through an accessor bound when `pathlib` is imported, so the patch of `os.scandir` does not reach them.

CHOSEN: `test_a_root_is_made_without_numbering_the_base_directory` now states the allocator's whole contract after its one parent: allocating a root makes one directory, lists none and starts no process. While it asks for two roots it replaces with a function that raises `os.scandir`, `os.listdir`, `Path.iterdir`, `Path.glob`, `Path.rglob`, `subprocess.Popen` (under `subprocess.run`, `check_output` and `os.popen`), `os.system`, `os.fork` (under the `os.spawn*` family) and `os.posix_spawn` / `os.posix_spawnp`. The reviewer's mutations of the allocator in the dry worktree `.remedy-wt/f294-r9-dry` at `cb959bda3`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest <the test> -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider`: the auditor's `ls -1` through `subprocess.run`; `ls -1` through `os.popen`; `ls -1` through `os.system` into a file; counting `parent.glob("*")`; counting `parent.rglob("*")`; `make_numbered_dir` under the base temporary directory; and counting `os.scandir(parent)`. Each turned the test red with `AssertionError: allocating a root listed a directory or started a process`; restored, the two acceptance files read 7 passed. This is the hardening stage's third and last repair round; R-1127 stays open until the next repeat audit has tried the test.

WHERE THE GUARD STOPS, STATED ONCE: the test guards every route Python itself offers for listing a directory or starting a program. A listing made through a foreign-function call into the C library is outside what a test can replace, and an allocator written that way would be a deliberate evasion that a reviewer reads in the diff, not a regression.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. One test now names the allocator's whole contract.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a timing check that allocation stays fast as the base temporary directory grows, REJECTED because a timing assertion is flaky under the worker cap and the lowered CPU priority; (b) refusing every system call by a seccomp filter in a child process, REJECTED as a test far heavier than the one line it guards.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore round 8's body of `test_a_root_is_made_without_numbering_the_base_directory`.

## DECISION F294 D10 — The hardening stage ends after its three repair rounds; R-1127 stays open, narrowed to a name bound before the test runs (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: the hardening stage's third repeat audit (operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap), run by a fresh auditor at `8ceb35ef8` from the feature file and the repository alone, tried six mutations of the data-root allocator; its report is `.agent/f294_acceptance_reaudit3.md`. Four turned the test red: `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` per root, `ls -1 | wc -l` through `subprocess.run(shell=True)`, `os.walk`, and `glob.glob`. Two stayed green. The auditor counted one: an alias of `os.scandir` taken when `tests/conftest.py` is imported, used later to list the parent, because the test replaces the attribute `os.scandir` and a name bound before that keeps the original function. The other, a call of the C library's `system` through `ctypes`, the auditor did not count, as DECISION F294 D9 also rules.

CHOSEN: rule (3) of operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap allows three repair rounds, and rounds 7, 8 and 9 were those three, so the stage ends here. R-1127 stays OPEN, owned by F294 until its closure, whose bookkeeping commit hands it to the next findings paydown, F290, as amend0911-feedback rule A orders; F294 closes PASS_WITH_RISKS naming it. What remains of R-1127, stated in place of its registration's repair sentence: `test_a_root_is_made_without_numbering_the_base_directory` refuses every directory listing and every started process that the allocator looks up when it runs, and it cannot see a listing function the allocator's module bound to a name of its own before the test ran. A repair would check the allocator from outside the test process, for example by recording the directories a child pytest run lists while it allocates roots. The Built State of `docs/roadmap/features/T2_F294.md` records the stage in plain words.

THE STAGE IN NUMBERS: the first audit took eight claims; four had a proving test at once, one is measured only by the closure's full suite, and three were reported as gaps. One of those three, the DECISION alternative, is decided by the closure's own record (DECISION F294 D7). Of the other two, R-1126 is resolved (rounds 7 and 8) and R-1127 is narrowed by three repairs and remains.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product and nothing in a test. The feature's record says what its hardening stage proved and what it did not.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a fourth repair round binding the patch earlier, REJECTED because rule (3) caps the stage at three repair rounds, and an alias bound at import time escapes any patch the test can apply at run time; (b) ruling the alias outside what a developer would write, REJECTED because `from os import scandir` is ordinary Python, and the finding is the honest record of what the test cannot see.

HOW TO REVERSE: a later feature that checks the allocator from outside the test process resolves R-1127 and edits the Built State's sentence that names it.

## DECISION F294 D11 — The closure's self-use item SU-041 lands: the autocoder probe of `remedy dev status` catches the two errors it can meet, and two tests pin it through the command line (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: F294's closure consumes one self-use item (docs/roadmap/STATUS_closure_protocol.md precondition 6). The queue held none, and the generator's tier 4 supplied `SU-041`: the handler at line 119 of `apps/cli/commands/dev.py`, around the autocoder probe of `remedy dev status`, caught `(ImportError, Exception)`, that is every exception, under an excused `# noqa: BLE001` mark. Round 11 ran the item to its approval gate (job `36d6e3a3d6cb403c`, the `self_use` role on `claude-cli`, 4 provider calls, $0.93, reviewer verdict pass, no run defect) and never applied it; the job's change, saved in `.agent/selfuse_f294/job_diff.txt`, narrows the handler to `(ImportError, TypeError)` and lowers `MAX_EXCUSED` in `tests/test_ble001_ratchet.py` from 287 to 286. No test covered the handler.

CHOSEN: the job's two-line change lands as the job wrote it, before the closure's one full suite, so that suite runs on the tree that ships. The two types are the ones the probe can meet: an import that no longer resolves, and a changed constructor of `FileOp` or `StructuredPatch`, which are frozen dataclasses without validation. Two new tests in `TestDevStatusCommandSchema` of `tests/regression/test_named_bugs.py`, beside F293's two for `SU-040`, drive `remedy dev status --json` through `apps.cli.main.main` with `StructuredPatch` replaced: for each of the two errors, the command still answers `ok` with `autocoder_fake_e2e_ok` false and `task_progress_ok` true, so the other checks are still reported; and a `RuntimeError` from the probe is no longer read as a failed check, so the command exits 1 with the error's name in its JSON envelope. The reviewer's mutations in the dry worktree `.remedy-wt/f294-r12-dry` at `0739ede19`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/regression/test_named_bugs.py tests/test_ble001_ratchet.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider -k "DevStatus or ratchet or excused or marks"`: the handler widened back to `(ImportError, Exception)` with its mark (the defect test and the ratchet red); `ImportError` dropped; `TypeError` dropped; `RuntimeError` added; the failed check reading as true (both parameters red); and `MAX_EXCUSED` left at 287 (the ratchet red). Each turned at least one test red; restored, 19 passed.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: `remedy dev status` still reports a broken autocoder probe as a failed check when the probe fails in one of the two expected ways. A defect of any other kind now stops the command with its own name, where before it was hidden as a failed check.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) keeping only `ImportError`, REJECTED because a renamed or removed field of either dataclass raises `TypeError` at the probe's own call, which is the failure the check exists to report; (b) adding `ValueError`, REJECTED because neither dataclass validates its fields, so no path raises it.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore the handler's `except (ImportError, Exception):` line with its `# noqa: BLE001` mark, set `MAX_EXCUSED` back to 287, and delete the two tests named above.

## DECISION F294 D12 — F294 closes on its Acceptance's second branch: 865.36 CPU seconds, and what remains cannot be cut in the tests without weakening them (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: F294's Goal & Done and its Acceptance ask for the full suite's CPU seconds at most 747.65, 40 percent below F293's T001 baseline of 1,246.09, OR that the ranking shows what remains cannot be made cheaper without weakening a test, with a dated DECISION saying so with the numbers. The closure's one full suite (round 13, `.agent/authored/f294-closure-suite.txt`) used 865.36 CPU seconds for 21,160 collected tests, exit 0: 8.0 percent below F293's closure reading of 940.64 and 30.55 percent below the baseline. The first branch is missed by 117.71 CPU seconds. F294 stands at session 2 and round 13, below its soft limit.

THE NUMBERS FOR THE SECOND BRANCH: DECISION F294 D6 ranked what remains. The costliest test files left are `tests/cli/test_golden_path.py` (52.51 CPU seconds before round 4, at most 40.08 after), `tests/cli/test_do_sequence_cli.py` 61.41, `tests/orchestration/test_job_apply_commit.py` 47.43, `tests/cli/test_do_commit_flags.py` 34.00 and `tests/orchestration/test_persisted_call_ownership.py` 19.37, each read alone and serially. Each runs a real job in every test and then changes what that job left, by applying it, committing it or tampering with its records, so no two tests can share one run, and pytest-xdist here hands single tests to whichever worker is free. Inside one job run, after F294's cuts, the cost is the job runner's own work: 188 git processes for a one-task run, 15 of its 31 tree snapshots taken by the absorb of a human change at every safe point (14 times for one task, DECISION F263 D-E), and one run of the target's own tests by the definition-of-done gate. Making these tests cheaper in the tests themselves means replacing that work with fakes: skipping the absorbs or the gate, or sharing one job between tests that each change it. Each of those stops the test from checking what a real job does, which is weakening the test. Making the job runner itself do less at every safe point is a change to the product that delays the detection of an operator's edit in every real job, which a test diet does not decide.

CHOSEN: the second branch holds, and F294 closes on it with this decision as its record. T002 is complete for the cuts of DECISIONs F294 D1 to D5, each measured before and after in one tree and each kept with its red-proof. F294 closes PASS_WITH_RISKS, naming R-1127, which its closure hands to the next findings paydown, F290. No follow-up feature is registered: the remaining cost is the price of tests that run real jobs, and a cheaper job run is a product question. Because this closes a target the operator set short of its number, it is written to the operator questions file as a reversible ruling (amend0911-feedback rule C, kind B; amend0917-throughput rule 5), with the trade-off: fewer absorbs per task or a cheaper done-gate in every real job, for about 118 CPU seconds per full test run.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: nothing in the product. The full test run now costs about 865 processor seconds instead of 941, and the 40 percent target is closed by a ruling, not by the number.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a third test-diet feature, REJECTED because D6's ranking leaves no test-side cut of that size that keeps every test checking a real job, so it would mint the same remainder again; (b) a product feature that absorbs human changes less often, REJECTED on the session's own authority because it changes what every real job does for the operator, and offered to the operator instead; (c) holding the closure until the operator answers, REJECTED because operator questions never stall a feature (amend0917-throughput rule 5).

HOW TO REVERSE: the operator asks for the job-run change; a new feature registered after F294 takes it, and this decision's CHOSEN paragraph is superseded by that feature's closure.

THE PROBLEM: operator amendment amend0827-process-diet rule 4 orders exactly one consolidation pass of the pre-emission checklist in `docs/agents/planner_reviewer_prompt.md` §3 per feature, inside its closure sequence, and the list may come out of it the same length or shorter.
