## DECISION F292 D1 — F292's plan read is one builder in `plan_editing`, served by `remedy job plan-show --json` and by a dashboard `plan` section, and the feature is built in five rounds (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, measured by the reviewer at `2d138e90f` with a research agent's map read back against the sources: `remedy job plan-show --json`, `_cmd_plan_show` in `apps/cli/commands/job_plan_cmd.py`, builds the plan read inline, and nothing else serves it: no route and no dashboard section carries the plan's version, its approval or a planned task's dependencies. The write door already accepts the six plan edits of DECISION F015 D3, each naming `expected_version`, and `patch.approve-hunks` with an optional `task_run`, an `approved` list of hunk ids and a `rejected` list of `{id, reason}`. The diff envelope already carries each hunk's id, but `DiffView` offers no hunk control and no route serves a recorded hunk decision. The palette lists its seven form entries disabled with `PALETTE_FORM_REASON` (DECISION F044 D5).

CHOSEN: (1) THE PLAN READ is `plan_view(job)` in `packages/orchestration/plan_editing.py`. It answers None for a job with no stored plan with tasks. Otherwise it answers the version, the approval as stored, `editable`, and `not_editable_because` from `edit_window_refusal` (None while the plan is editable), and every planned task in plan order with `PLAN_VIEW_TASK_FIELDS` (id, title, goal, depends_on, est_tokens_band, files_hint, acceptance) plus the first mapped task entry's id, status and spec version, which read `""`, `""` and 1 when no entry maps the task. `_cmd_plan_show` prints from it, and its JSON and its text are unchanged. The dashboard's new `plan` section, `_build_plan_section` in `packages/orchestration/ui_server.py`, is that same answer with `available` True and `error` empty, so the plan view's version, approval and tasks equal `plan-show --json` by construction. A job with no plan reads `available` False, version 0 and no tasks, and a malformed stored version is reported as `error`, never raised. (2) THE ORDER, one building round each: the plan read, this round; the plan view in the cockpit, read only, meaning the section's type and normalizer, a `plan-view` region that shows the version, the approval, the edit window and each task's dependencies and acceptance, and its render check; the six edits in that view, each sent with the version shown, a version conflict and a refusal told in plain words, and the view read again after each accepted edit; the diff view's hunk controls, whose read of the recorded decisions is ruled in that round's own DECISION, because a decision replaces the whole record for its diff and the controls must therefore start from what is recorded; and the palette's seven form entries turned into surface entries, with an end-to-end run. Then the amend0930b-slow-cap hardening stage, then the closure sequence. (3) R-1128, found at this claim's Open PR Gate, is owned by F290 under amend0929-context-hygiene and is not repaired here.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a route of its own for the plan instead of a dashboard section, REJECTED because the dashboard is the read the cockpit already holds for a job and `task_specs`, built from the same stored plan, is served there, while a second read would need its own refresh rule; (b) serving `not_editable_because` as `""` while the plan is editable, REJECTED because `plan-show --json` emits null there and the acceptance asks the two to be equal; (c) building the read in `ui_server.py` and leaving the command line's copy in place, REJECTED because two copies can drift, which is the very risk the acceptance line names.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore `_cmd_plan_show` and `_task_entry_for_planned_id` in `apps/cli/commands/job_plan_cmd.py` from `2d138e90f`; delete `plan_view` and `PLAN_VIEW_TASK_FIELDS` from `plan_editing.py`, `_build_plan_section`, `_empty_plan_section` and the `plan` key from `ui_server.py`, and `tests/ui_server/test_dashboard_plan.py`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D2 — The plan view is a read-only sheet opened from the right panel's Plan button; its rules live in one pure module and it reads the dashboard's `plan` section (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, read by the reviewer at `d55f29be6`: the dashboard now serves the `plan` section (DECISION F292 D1 (1)), but the client's `RemedyDashboard` has no field for it and no screen shows a plan. Whole-job surfaces in the cockpit (Lessons, Tour, Story, Results, Terms) are sheets the shell mounts as siblings after `</main>`, which `tests/ui_contracts/test_main_layout_guard.py` holds to four children, each opened by a quiet button in the right panel. The cockpit re-reads the dashboard every five seconds (`RemedyApp.tsx`).

CHOSEN: (1) THE DATA. `RemedyDashboard` gains a required `plan: RemedyPlan`, with `RemedyPlanTask` for each planned task; `normalizePlan` in `apps/ui/src/api/remedyApi.ts` reads the section on the dashboard path and gives the failure path the no-plan shape. The server's `null` approval and `null` reason read `""`, a version that is not a whole number of at least 1 reads 0, and a section that is not `available` is never editable and lists no task. `tests/ui_contracts/test_plan_view_contract.py` holds the keys the decoder reads equal to the keys `_build_plan_section` writes, for the section and for each task. (2) THE RULES live in `apps/ui/src/api/planView.ts`, which reaches no fetch, clock, storage or DOM: which body to show (the section's read failed, no stored plan, or the plan); the approval in plain words (`pending` reads "waiting for approval", and an approval the table does not know is shown as stored); the headline "Version <n> · <approval>"; the edit window in one sentence carrying the server's reason; what a task waits for, in the plan's own order; and the task entry that runs it, or that none does. A failed read shows one quiet sentence and never the raw error text (ux_spec.md §17). (3) THE VIEW is `apps/ui/src/components/plan/PlanView.tsx`, `data-ui="plan-view"`: a right-anchored glass sheet on `--remedy-z-overlay` with the learning overlay's surface, a dialog named Plan that Escape and a Close plan button close, showing the headline, the edit window as a pill that is tinted when open and says so in words, and each planned task as a tile with its id, title, size band, goal, dependencies, entry, and its acceptance criteria numbered from 0, the index the plan edits address. It does not show the task entry's own id or the files hint, which a person does not act on here. (4) THE ENTRY is a quiet Plan button, `data-ui="plan-button"`, first of the right panel's buttons below the tasks card; the shell owns whether the view is open and hands it `dashboard.plan`, so the view is as fresh as the dashboard poll. The six edits of the next round add their own re-read after an accepted edit, as D1 (2) orders.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a card inside the right panel, REJECTED because a plan with several tasks and criteria needs the height of a sheet and the right panel's cards are summaries; (b) a fetch of its own in the view, REJECTED because the dashboard already carries the section and a second read would need its own refresh rule; (c) showing the server's error text, REJECTED because it is a program's message, not a sentence for a person.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `apps/ui/src/components/plan/`, `apps/ui/src/api/planView.ts` and `planView.test.ts`, `tests/ui_contracts/test_plan_view_contract.py`, `RemedyPlan`, `RemedyPlanTask` and the `plan` field from `types.ts`, `normalizePlan`, `normalizePlanTask` and their two call sites from `remedyApi.ts` with their tests in `remedyApi.test.ts`, the Plan button from `RightLivePanel.tsx`, and the plan view's state, import and mount from `RemedyShell.tsx`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D3 — The plan view's edits send through one module against the version shown, an accepted edit reads the dashboard again at once, and the six edits land over three rounds: edit and delete now, then the criteria and the order, then merge and split (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, read by the reviewer at `224f67eda`: the write door accepts the six plan edits of DECISION F015 D3, each with `expected_version`; `plan_edit_refusal` answers a stale version as 409 with `current_version` alone, a plan that fails revalidation as 409 with `detail` and `current_version`, a closed plan as 409 with `detail`, and an edit the plan cannot take as 400 on field `args` with `detail`; an accepted edit answers the plan's new version. The cockpit reads the dashboard every five seconds and nothing can ask it to read sooner. DECISION F292 D1 (2) gave the six edits one round.

CHOSEN: (1) THE SEND is `apps/ui/src/api/planEditSend.ts`: the six command ids in the door's spelling and order, one builder per edit carrying the backend's own argument object, one request builder that adds the version the view shows as `expected_version`, the one flow `sendPlanEdit`, and the wording: an accepted edit says "Saved as version <n>.", a refusal that carries `detail` says "Not saved: <detail>." whatever else it carries, a 409 with only `current_version` says the plan changed since it was opened, and every other status is worded as the pause door words it. The module composes `taskEditSend.ts` and `pauseSend.ts` for the headers, the nonce, the submit and the shared statuses. (2) THE RE-READ: `RemedyApp.tsx` holds a reload count that re-runs its dashboard read at once and restarts the five-second timer; the shell passes `onReload` to the plan view, which calls it after an accepted edit. Until the dashboard serves the version the edit landed as, the view's edit controls are disabled with the reason, because an edit sent against the version still shown would only be refused as stale. (3) THE RULES of the controls live in `apps/ui/src/api/planEditView.ts`: when the controls may be used and why not; the edit form's draft, what is wrong with it, and only the fields it changed, trimmed; the four size bands of the planner's `TokenBand`; and the question a delete asks first, naming the tasks that wait for the task and what they will wait for instead, as `plan_delete_task` rewires them. (4) THIS ROUND'S CONTROLS, shown only while the plan is open for editing: each task's Edit, which opens `PlanTaskEditForm` with its title, goal and size, and Delete, which asks first; the outcome of each send is one sentence in the view's status line. (5) THE ORDER, amending D1 (2): the criteria editor and the order of the tasks in the next round, merge and split in the round after, then the hunk controls and the palette's surfaces as D1 orders. Each of those rounds adds its controls over the same send module. (6) R-1129, found while writing (1), is owned by F290: the runtime task edit's own wording reads `current_version` before `detail` and so hides a revalidation refusal's reason.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) all six edits in one round, REJECTED under SLOW MODE because merge and split each need a selection of tasks or of criteria that is a control of its own, and one round with all six would be the largest of the feature; (b) waiting for the five-second read after an accepted edit, REJECTED because the controls would sit disabled for up to five seconds after every edit; (c) a fetch of the plan inside the view after an edit, REJECTED because the dashboard is the view's one source and a second read would show two versions at once.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `apps/ui/src/api/planEditSend.ts`, `planEditView.ts`, their tests and `apps/ui/src/components/plan/PlanTaskEditForm.tsx`; restore `PlanView.tsx`, `PlanView.module.css`, `planViewMarkup.test.ts` and `tests/ui_contracts/test_plan_view_contract.py` from `224f67eda`; remove the reload count and `onReload` from `RemedyApp.tsx` and `RemedyShell.tsx`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D4 — The plan view edits criteria in place and moves a task one place at a time, and refuses before sending what the planner would refuse: an empty criterion, a task with no criterion, and a task before one it waits for (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, read by the reviewer at `bf875dc91`: `plan_edit_acceptance` in `packages/orchestration/plan_editing.py` takes `op` of add, edit or remove, an `index` (left out, an add goes at the end) and a `text`; the planner's schema refuses an empty criterion and a task with no criterion, which arrive as `invalid_plan`. `plan_reorder` takes the whole new order, and `revalidate` refuses an order that puts a task before one it waits for, "a job runs its tasks in plan order". DECISION F292 D3 (5) gave this round the criteria and the order.

CHOSEN: (1) THE CRITERIA are `apps/ui/src/components/plan/PlanCriteria.tsx`, which renders a task's criteria under their index as before and, while the plan is open for editing, gives each criterion Change and Remove and the task an Add a criterion button. Change opens a one-line form on that criterion's own line, prefilled; Add opens an empty one after the list; Save sends `planEditAcceptanceEdit` with the trimmed text — an edit at the criterion's index, an add with no index — and Remove sends a remove at its index at once, because an add puts it back. The plan view owns which form is open, one across the whole plan. (2) THE MOVES are Move up and Move down beside each task's Edit and Delete, sending the whole new order through `planReorderEdit`. (3) THE RULES, in `apps/ui/src/api/planEditView.ts`: `planCriterionProblem` refuses an empty criterion; `planCriterionRemoveBlocked` disables Remove on a task's only criterion, with the reason; `planMove` answers the new order or the reason a move cannot be made — the task is already at that end, the task it would pass is one it waits for, or one that waits for it. Each refusal is the planner's own rule stated before the send, so a person is told at the button rather than after a refused edit; the backend still refuses whatever reaches it. (4) The criterion buttons are a smaller ghost so a row of criteria reads as text first, and a criterion row aligns its buttons on the text's baseline.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) dragging a task to any place, REJECTED because it is a pointer-only control with no keyboard path in this cockpit and a one-place move reaches every order the plan-order rule allows; (b) asking before a criterion is removed, REJECTED because the removal is undone by adding the criterion back, unlike a deleted task whose dependants are rewired; (c) leaving the refusals to the backend alone, REJECTED because a disabled button with its reason costs nothing and saves a round trip that can only fail.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `apps/ui/src/components/plan/PlanCriteria.tsx`, `planCriterionProblem`, `planCriterionRemoveBlocked` and `planMove` with their tests; restore `PlanView.tsx`, `PlanView.module.css`, `planViewMarkup.test.ts`, `planEditView.ts`, `planEditView.test.ts` and `tests/ui_contracts/test_plan_view_contract.py` from `bf875dc91`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D5 — Merge and split are forms on the task that say what the edit will do before it is sent; with them the plan view offers all six plan edits (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, read by the reviewer at `c53dad57f`: `plan_merge_tasks` in `packages/orchestration/plan_editing.py` takes two or more task ids, joins them through `task_granularity._merge_group` at the first one's place in plan order and under its id — every criterion of each, the waits of all, the titles joined — and rewires every other task that waited for one of them to wait for the first. `plan_split_task` takes a task id and a partition of its criterion indexes into at least two non-empty groups; `_split_task` makes one task per group, run one after the other, the first waiting for what the task waited for, and every task that waited for the task waits for the last part. The plan's own checks still apply after either, so a merge that would make a task wait for itself, or put a task before one it waits for, is refused as `invalid_plan` with a reason.

CHOSEN: (1) MERGE is `apps/ui/src/components/plan/PlanMergeForm.tsx`, opened by a task's Merge button: the plan's other tasks as checkboxes under "Merge <id> with", and, once one is chosen, one sentence saying what will happen — which tasks become which one, with how many criteria, and which tasks will wait for it instead. Merge tasks sends `planMergeTasksEdit` with the chosen tasks and this one in plan order. (2) SPLIT is `apps/ui/src/components/plan/PlanSplitForm.tsx`, opened by a task's Split button: each criterion with the part it goes into, opening with the last criterion in part 2, and one sentence saying how many tasks will run one after the other and which tasks will wait for the last part. Split task sends `planSplitTaskEdit` with one group per part that holds a criterion, in part order. (3) THE RULES, in `apps/ui/src/api/planEditView.ts`: Merge is disabled with a reason on a plan of one task, and Split on a task with one criterion; a merge with nothing chosen and a split into one part are answered in the form and never sent; the sentences describe the planner's own rewiring and do not restate the planner's id scheme for split parts, which the view shows once the dashboard is read again. (4) With this round every one of the six edits of DECISION F015 D3 is offered in the plan view; the next round is the diff view's hunk controls.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) naming the split parts' ids in the preview, REJECTED because it would copy `_child_ids` and its collision rule into the browser, a second copy that can drift; (b) a merge from a multi-select across the whole task list, REJECTED because starting from one task keeps the first of the merge, whose id the result takes, obvious to the person; (c) refusing in the browser a merge the planner would refuse for a cycle or an order, REJECTED because that check is a graph walk the planner already owns, and its refusal reaches the person with its reason.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `apps/ui/src/components/plan/PlanMergeForm.tsx`, `PlanSplitForm.tsx` and the merge and split rules with their tests; restore `PlanView.tsx`, `PlanView.module.css`, `planViewMarkup.test.ts`, `planEditView.ts`, `planEditView.test.ts` and `tests/ui_contracts/test_plan_view_contract.py` from `c53dad57f`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D6 — The hunk controls start from the decision recorded for the attempt the diff shows, served by a read route of its own, and every refusal the door would hide is stated before the send; the controls themselves land next round, beside the diff rather than inside its rows (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, read by the reviewer at `8e77c28e9` with a research agent's map read back against the sources: `patch.approve-hunks` records one decision per attempt under `job.metadata["hunk_decisions"]["<task>:<attempt>"]` (`_dispatch_approve_hunks`, keyed by the diff's task id or `DIFF_SCOPE_JOB` and its `source`), and a second decision on the same attempt REPLACES the first whole, so a hunk a send leaves out goes back to pending. No route serves a recorded decision to the browser. The door refuses an empty decision, an unknown hunk, a rejection without a reason and a cut-short diff, and answers every refusal with the one fixed sentence "hunk decision was refused", withholding its reason under DECISIONS F009 D18 and D22. The diff view's rows are a fixed 20 pixels high for its virtual scrolling, and `tests/ui_contracts/test_diff_view_render.py` pins how `DiffView.tsx` renders them.

CHOSEN: (1) THE READ is `recorded_hunk_decision(metadata, *, task_id, attempt)` in `packages/orchestration/hunk_decision_record.py`, total and keyed by that module's own `_attempt_key`, answering `{attempt_key, decided_at, hunks}` with each row's `id`, `state` and `reason`; `ui_server.py` serves it for the attempt the diff shows, at `/api/jobs/<id>/hunk-decisions` for the job's own diff and `/api/jobs/<id>/task-runs/<tid>/hunk-decisions` for a task run's, keyed exactly as the door keys the decision it records. A diff with no `source` has no attempt and answers no key and no row. `tests/ui_server/test_command_channel.py` walks the new structural route. (2) THE CLIENT reads it through `readHunkDecisions` in `apps/ui/src/api/hunkDecisions.ts` and `loadHunkDecisions` in `remedyApi.ts`, which reads a failed read as nothing recorded. (3) THE RULES, in `apps/ui/src/api/hunkDecisionView.ts`: a person starts from the record, hunk by hunk, or pending; a recorded hunk the diff no longer shows is left out; a hunk the server sent no id for, an absent diff and a cut-short diff cannot be decided, with the reason; a send records every decidable hunk's state in the diff's order, refuses to record nothing and refuses a rejection without a reason; and the tally counts approved, rejected and pending. (4) THE SEND is `apps/ui/src/api/hunkDecisionSend.ts`: an accepted decision says its three counts, read off the door's answer; the door's one refusal says plainly that the server refused the decision for this change and how to try again, and invents no reason; every other status is worded as the pause door words it. (5) THE CONTROLS land in the next round as a panel of their own inside the diff panel, beside the diff view: one row per hunk with its header, Approve, Reject with a reason, and the tally, because a reason field cannot live in a 20-pixel row and the diff view's rendering is pinned by its own guards. Clicking a hunk's row is not required to scroll the diff. The palette's surfaces and the end-to-end run follow, then the hardening stage.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) adding the decisions to the diff envelope, REJECTED because the feature file forbids touching the diff view's reading of the envelope and the envelope is pinned by its own tests; (b) controls that send only the hunks touched in one sitting, REJECTED because the record is replaced whole and the untouched hunks would silently return to pending; (c) wording the door's refusal with a guessed reason, REJECTED because the door withholds the reason on purpose and a guessed reason is the kind of claim this cockpit must not make; (d) the controls inside the diff's own rows, REJECTED for the row height and the guards above.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `recorded_hunk_decision`, `_hunk_decisions_for_view`, `_build_hunk_decisions_json`, `_build_task_run_hunk_decisions_json`, the `hunk-decisions` handler and the structural route, the walk's added path, `tests/ui_server/test_hunk_decisions_route.py`, `apps/ui/src/api/hunkDecisions.ts`, `hunkDecisionView.ts`, `hunkDecisionSend.ts` with their tests, `loadHunkDecisions` with its tests and import, and `tests/ui_contracts/test_hunk_decision_contract.py`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D7 — The hunk decisions are a panel after the diff view inside the diff panel, one row per hunk with Approve, Reject with a reason and Undecided, starting from the record and reading it again after each recorded decision (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, read by the reviewer at `7a0b07d96`: DECISION F292 D6 landed the read of the recorded decision, the rules and the send, and placed the controls beside the diff view rather than inside its rows. The diff panel in `RemedyShell.tsx` is a bare landmark after the shell, holding the file sidebar and the diff view, opened from a task's detail popover, the guided tour and the chat; its own layout was left to a later ruling at F037 and is unchanged here, so the panel opens below the cockpit and the popover that opened it stays above it.

CHOSEN: (1) THE PANEL is `apps/ui/src/components/diff/HunkDecisionPanel.tsx`, `data-ui="hunk-decisions"`, mounted in the diff panel directly after `DiffView` and handed the envelope and the send target; it adds nothing to `DiffView.tsx` or `DiffView.module.css`. (2) THE READ: it reads the decision recorded for the attempt the envelope shows through `loadHunkDecisions`, drops a read that arrives after the diff moved on, starts every decidable hunk from that record, and reads it again after each decision the door records. While the read is in flight it says so and keeps Record disabled with that reason. (3) EACH HUNK is a row with its file and its `@@` header in the mono face and three pill choices, Approve, Reject and Undecided, the chosen one pressed and tinted with a border and weight; Reject opens a reason field; a hunk the server sent no id for says it cannot be decided here. A diff that is absent or cut short shows the reason instead of any row. (4) RECORD is disabled with the reason while nothing has changed since the record, while the record is being read and while a decision is in flight; otherwise it sends the whole decision through `sendHunkDecision`, after the rules refuse a decision that decides nothing or a rejection without a reason, and the outcome is said in the panel's status line with the tally above the rows. (5) THE NEXT ROUND turns the palette's seven form entries into surface entries opening the plan view and this panel, with an end-to-end run; then the hardening stage.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) radio inputs instead of pressed pills, REJECTED because the cockpit's other mode switches (the learning overlay's) are pressed pills and the same look keeps one control language; (b) laying the diff panel out as a sheet in this round, REJECTED because that is the layout ruling F037 deferred and it changes every opener of the diff, which is beyond this feature's file; (c) sending each choice as it is made, REJECTED because every send replaces the record whole and a half-made set of choices would be recorded as final.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `apps/ui/src/components/diff/HunkDecisionPanel.tsx`, its stylesheet and `hunkDecisionPanelMarkup.test.ts`; remove its import and mount from `RemedyShell.tsx` and the two panel tests from `tests/ui_contracts/test_hunk_decision_contract.py`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D8 — The palette's seven form entries open surfaces: the six plan edits the plan view, the hunk approval the job diff's hunk decisions; both stay open on an ended job; and one end-to-end test drives both through the real server (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION, read by the reviewer at `630b56070`: `apps/ui/src/api/paletteCommands.ts` lists the six plan edits and `patch.approve-hunks` as "form" entries that `paletteCommandState.ts` always disables with "The palette cannot ask for this command's arguments yet." (DECISION F044 D5); the feature file's Acceptance asks that the palette list no form entry disabled. `handleOpenSurface` in `RemedyShell.tsx` opens the add-task sheet and the task edit form itself and otherwise scrolls to a card already on the page; the plan view and the diff panel are mounted only while open. The palette refuses every entry on an ended job, while the write door records a hunk decision whatever the job's state, and a finished job's change is the one whose hunks a person decides.

CHOSEN: (1) THE ENTRIES: the six plan edits become surface entries opening `plan-view`, and `patch.approve-hunks` one opening `hunk-decisions`, each still asking nothing; `PaletteFlow` loses "form", and `PALETTE_FORM_REASON` and its check are deleted, so no entry of the palette is a form any more. (2) THE OPENING: `handleOpenSurface` opens the plan view's sheet for `plan-view`, and for `hunk-decisions` opens the diff panel on the job's own diff, whose panel holds the hunk decisions; a task run's diff stays reachable from the task's popover. (3) THE RULE: the token check still comes first, and the ended-job refusal now skips the two surfaces `plan-view` and `hunk-decisions`, because both are views that say for themselves what can still be done. (4) THE END-TO-END RUN is `tests/ui_server/test_plan_view_live.py`: the real UI server, started in the test's process over a cockpit built into the test's own temporary folder, with the server's bundle lookup pointed at that build; headless Chrome finds the six plan edits in the palette enabled, opens the plan view from "Edit a planned task", edits a task's title and reads the stored plan at version 2 with the new title while the view shows "Version 2", then opens the job's hunk decisions from "Approve or reject the hunks of a change", records one approval and one rejection with a reason, and finds on disk exactly the record `record_hunk_decision_from_view` writes for that decision. It cannot tell an immediate re-read from the cockpit's five-second poll, which also shows version 2 within its wait, so the immediate re-read stays proven by the round 3 render and the contract test that pins its wiring. (5) The next step is the amend0930b-slow-cap hardening stage, then the closure sequence.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a task argument on the hunk entry to open a task run's diff, REJECTED because the palette's task step offers only tasks and the job's own diff is the change a person reviews as a whole; (b) keeping "form" as a flow with no entries, REJECTED because a flow nothing uses is a branch nothing tests; (c) a mocked door in the end-to-end test, REJECTED because the round's purpose is to prove the cockpit and the real door agree.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore `paletteCommands.ts`, `paletteCommandState.ts`, their tests and `handleOpenSurface` in `RemedyShell.tsx` from `630b56070`; delete `tests/ui_server/test_plan_view_live.py` and the palette test added to `tests/ui_contracts/test_plan_view_contract.py`; delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F292 D9 — The hardening stage audited nine statements, found a proving test for every one and no gap; F292 goes to its closure sequence with nothing to repair (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION: operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap rule 2 orders, in SLOW MODE, one hardening stage after a feature's last building round and before its closure sequence. F292's last building round, round 8, was reviewed PASS at `5c68dfd9a`. The reviewer delegated the acceptance audit to a fresh worker given only `docs/roadmap/features/T5_F292.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the amendment's paragraph and the repository, and no block, handoff or verdict.

THE AUDIT, committed as `.agent/f292_acceptance_audit.md`: nine statements, the five DONE clauses of Goal & Done and the four Acceptance lines. Each was matched to a test, and each test turned red under one mutation of the production code in the disposable worktree `.remedy-wt/f292-audit-wt` at `5c68dfd9a` and green again when the code was restored. Two of the proofs reach the feature as a person does: claims 6 and 7 through the real command line, `remedy job plan-show --json` and a stale `--plan-version`, and claim 4 through `tests/ui_server/test_plan_view_live.py`, headless Chrome against the real UI server, where a dead reason field for a rejected hunk stopped the run. The auditor removed its worktree; `git worktree list` read twelve lines afterwards and the primary checkout stayed clean.

THE REVIEWER'S CHECK: the reviewer re-ran the user-path proof, claim 4, in its own dry tree, which equals `5c68dfd9a` byte for byte: the mutation read `1 failed`, the byte-identical restore `1 passed`. The reviewer reads claim 2, which the auditor proved through the door's own command list, as also pinned on the cockpit's side by the plan view's markup tests, whose mutations rounds 3 to 5 ran.

CHOSEN: no gap was found, so no finding is registered and no repair round is owed (rule 3). The feature file's Built State gains its hardening paragraph (rule 4), and the closure sequence comes next, starting with the integration gate's one full suite (rule 5).

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a repeat audit by a second auditor, REJECTED because rule 3 repeats the audit only for statements that had gaps; (b) holding the closure for the diff panel's layout, REJECTED because that layout is F037's deferred ruling and no statement of this feature's file asks for it.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `.agent/f292_acceptance_audit.md`, the Built State section of `docs/roadmap/features/T5_F292.md` and its banner line's change, and this paragraph; a later audit then runs again.

## DECISION F293 D16 — the operator answers Q2: shaken by the 210 git programs per job but decides by delegation; the already-registered job runner change stays the one cleanup item (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT: Operator question Q2 in `.agent/operator_questions.md`, written at F293 round 22 on 2026-10-01, reported that the test-load cut reached about a quarter against the 40 percent target, that the largest remaining cost is not in the tests but in the job runner starting about 210 small git programs during every test that runs a whole job, and that fixing the job runner is a product change which also makes real jobs faster. The reviewer closed the finished work at the quarter it reached and registered the job runner change as a new roadmap item, placed directly after it. The operator's answer arrived via remedy-answer, quoted in full: "Holy shit, 210 sounds like a lot. Do we need a cleanup? Decide by yourself please"

CHOSEN: deciding by delegation, as the operator asked: the already-registered job runner item is the one cleanup the 210-git-program cost needs, and no second, separate cleanup item is registered beside it. The split stands — F293 closes at the quarter it reached, and the job runner change is built next, directly after it. The Q2 entry is deleted, and `.agent/operator_questions.md` reads EMPTY once Q3 is also recorded.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a second, separate cleanup item for the 210 git-program cost outside the already-registered job runner change, REJECTED because the registered item already is that cleanup, and a second one would duplicate its scope; (b) reopening F293 or F294 now to chase the remaining 40 percent target, REJECTED because the operator's concern names the subprocess count specifically, which the job runner item already addresses as a product change, not a test change.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete this paragraph and write the question again; a later session then re-decides whether a second cleanup item is needed.

## DECISION F292 D10 — The closure's self-use item SU-042 changed nothing, so no change of it is landed; it is consumed by F292 at the STATUS flip, and its defect is a recurrence of R-1117 (2026-10-01)

THE SITUATION: closure precondition 6 (`docs/roadmap/STATUS_closure_protocol.md`) has every closure run exactly one self-use item to its approval gate. F292's round 11 generated `SU-042`, "Narrow the excused handler at apps/cli/commands/dev.py:126", and ran it as job `ee28dd2e1c254f05`. The job ended `completed` and its one task passed review, but the job's branch changes no file, and `describe_self_use_run_defects` returned one string, "a task passed review but no path outside .agent/ changed".

CHOSEN: no change of `SU-042` is landed on this branch. The precondition asks for the item to be run, its defects registered and its `consumed_by` set; it does not ask for its change to land, and here there is no change. F293 and F294 landed their items because Remedy's own job had written a correct change, which a person then only had to accept; a repair written by the reviewer instead would not be Remedy used on Remedy. This follows F044's closure, whose item `SU-039` changed nothing in the same way and was consumed without a landing.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) the reviewer writes the narrowed handler and lands it, REJECTED for the reason above and because the change is outside F292's scope; (b) running the item again, REJECTED because the precondition asks for one run, a second run costs money again, and R-1117 is the record of this behaviour; (c) a new finding id, REJECTED by checklist item 30, because R-1117 describes the same defect.

HOW TO REVERSE: set `SU-042`'s `consumed_by` back to empty in `scripts/self_use_queue.json` and delete this paragraph; the next closure then runs `SU-042` again as its own item.

## DECISION F200 D1 — `remedy serve` is one supervisor per data root: it answers the cockpit's own write door on a unix socket, the command line sends the door's commands to it while it runs, and it runs the jobs it is handed as child processes and runs them again after a restart; the scheduler, the cockpit thread and the notify and audit-export workers are not built, because what they would host was retired or never existed (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F200.md` was written before F261 retired the job queue. Measured at `959b88a85` by the reviewer's two research helpers and re-read by the reviewer. (a) THE QUEUE. DECISION F261 D14 deleted `packages/orchestration/job_queue.py`, the `queue` group and the executor binding that let an idle run take its project's next queued goal, naming "none for the unattended pickup" as the heir; DECISION F261 D22 deleted `job enqueue`, `job pause`, `job cancel`, `job resume-queue` and `worker run`, naming "none for the queue itself". F048's STATUS line still reads `[x]`, because an accepted line is never touched, and F049, parallelism, is `[ ]` and unbuilt. The feature file's sentence "the queue (F048) already claims atomically" is therefore false, and its scheduler has nothing to consume. (b) THE WRITE DOOR. F009's door is `_RemedyHandler._handle_command_submission` in `packages/orchestration/ui_server.py`, reached by `POST /api/jobs/<id>/commands`. It reads a JSON envelope of `command`, `client_nonce` and optional `args`, checks the bearer token, the `X-Remedy-CSRF` header, the job, the payload, `UI_EXPOSED_COMMANDS` in `apps/cli/command_catalog.py` (21 ids), the nonce and the rate limit, and records every effect with `COMMAND_EFFECT_SOURCE`, which reads `"ui"`, and with the token's fingerprint as the actor. Each of the 21 ids is also a command line command with the same id, and the command line handlers call the package functions directly, never the door. (c) THE COCKPIT. `remedy ui start <job>` runs one foreground server per job, bound to 127.0.0.1, built by `start_ui_server` as a subclass of `_RemedyHandler` with its state bound on the class. (d) No notify worker and no audit-export worker exists. (e) RUNS. `remedy job run` runs `pingpong_job.run_job` in the foreground, writes `running` into the job's `job.json`, and for a git target holds an exclusive lock at `<data root>/projects/<project>/locks/<job>.lock` for the whole run; a SIGKILL leaves the record reading `running` and frees the lock. `tests/orchestration/test_resume_kill.py` is F047's kill-and-resume proof.

CHOSEN. (1) THE SUPERVISOR. `remedy serve start` runs one supervisor per data root in the foreground, which is how a systemd unit or a container runs it; `remedy serve status` reports it and `remedy serve stop` stops it. Its files live in a new durable data-root class `serve`, whose paths `packages/orchestration/serve_paths.py` computes: the socket `serve.sock`, the process id file `serve.pid`, the token file `serve.token` and the run registry `runs/`. A data root too deep for a unix socket path is refused with the setting to change. (2) ONE WRITE DOOR. The supervisor listens on that unix socket and answers it with the cockpit's own request handler, so the socket carries the F009 envelope on the same route through the same checks, and no second write protocol exists. An effect that arrives over the socket is recorded with source `cli` and the command line's actor, so the record on disk is the same whichever way the command was given. The socket file and the token file are readable by their owner only. A localhost HTTP client channel is not built: the socket is the one client channel, and the cockpit's own server stays `remedy ui start`. (3) CLIENT DETECTION. When the socket of the resolved data root answers, the command line is a client: a command the door carries is sent as an envelope, and the command line prints the answer exactly as its direct handler prints it, with the same exit code. When no socket answers, every command runs direct exactly as today, and direct mode stays fully supported. A command the door does not carry runs direct in both modes; this is the one place the amended feature departs from "in daemon mode ONLY the daemon writes job state", because a door clause for every other write command is the headless API's work (F253), not this feature's. (4) RUNS. The socket also accepts `job.run`, which the cockpit's browser door does not: `remedy job run` in client mode hands the job to the supervisor, which runs it as a child process running `remedy job run` in direct mode and records it in its run registry. Different jobs run side by side; a second `job.run` for a job the supervisor is already running is refused. Nothing is kept for later: a run that cannot start is refused, so no queue comes back. (5) RESTART. When the supervisor starts, every job in its run registry whose child is gone and whose record still reads `running` is run again the same way, and a kill test with SIGKILL proves the result against F047's (each task executed once, every task green). (6) NOT BUILT, each with its reason: the scheduler loop and its parallelism, because the queue was retired with no heir and F049 is unbuilt; a cockpit thread inside the supervisor, because one cockpit for the whole host is F201's remote access; the notify and audit-export workers, because neither exists to be hosted. The feature file's "the suite runs twice: direct + client" is read as one test module that runs every forwarded command in both modes, because operator amendments amend0917-throughput and amend0930-test-load allow one full suite per feature. (7) THE ORDER. This claim lands `serve_paths` and the `serve` class. Then: the supervisor with its three commands and the socket answered by the cockpit's handler; client detection with `job.stop`, `job.pause` and `job.unpause` forwarded and the both-modes test module; the door's other commands the command line shares; `job run` through the supervisor; the restart and its kill test; the systemd unit `scripts/serve/remedy-serve.service`, the container entrypoint `scripts/serve/container-entrypoint.sh` and the built-state page; then the amend0930b-slow-cap hardening stage and the closure. The feature file gains an Amendment section stating the amended design, slicing and acceptance; its earlier sections stay as written.

ALTERNATIVES. Rebuilding a queue inside F200 was rejected: it reverses DECISIONs F261 D14 and D22, which retired the queue on purpose. A localhost HTTP channel with a token was rejected for this feature: owner-only file permissions are the access control a local client needs, and a second listening port belongs to F201. Giving the door a clause for every write command was rejected for this feature, as in (3). Placing F200 behind F290 was rejected: Rule A5 takes the first open line, and the amended feature is buildable now.

CONSEQUENCE. `remedy serve` becomes a command group; while a supervisor runs, the door's commands and `job run` go through it and every other command runs as before. Operator question Q4 states this ruling in plain words; the ruling is executed and stands until the operator overturns it (amend0917-throughput rule 5). HOW TO REVERSE: delete this section and the feature file's Amendment section, and revert the rounds that land it.

## DECISION F200 D2 — the supervisor answers its socket with a subclass of the cockpit's handler whose `effect_source` reads `cli`, and `serve` is an advanced command group; R-1131's repair lands with them (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. DECISION F200 D1 (2) records an effect that arrives over the socket with source `cli`. Measured at `b5817560e`: the door's `_dispatch_job_stop`, `_dispatch_job_pause` and `_dispatch_job_unpause` in `packages/orchestration/ui_server.py` pass the module constant `COMMAND_EFFECT_SOURCE`, which reads `"ui"`, and `pause_control.unpause_job_command` takes a `source` and records it nowhere. `start_ui_server` binds the handler's state by subclassing `_RemedyHandler` with `type(...)`. `VISIBLE_GROUP_ORDER` in `apps/cli/command_catalog.py` fixes the default help's visible groups by DECISION amend0905-vocab D4, and `tests/cli/test_cli_ux.py` pins `len(GROUPS) == 33`. R-1131 records the two guards round 1 left red.

CHOSEN. (1) `_RemedyHandler` gains the class attribute `effect_source`, defaulting to `COMMAND_EFFECT_SOURCE`, and the three clauses pass `self.effect_source`, so the cockpit's own server is unchanged. `serve_daemon.socket_handler_class` subclasses the handler the way `start_ui_server` does, with `effect_source` `"cli"`, no preview worker and no page. Only the stop and the pause record their source, so only those two are proved over the socket; the unpause clause reads the attribute too, so the three clauses stay alike. The actor the door records for the other commands, and its steering channel, stay the cockpit's until the round that forwards those commands, which states its own reading of each. (2) `serve` is an advanced group, `user_facing=False` like `data`, so the visible order D4 rules is untouched; the pin becomes 34 and `serve` joins the test's internal set. (3) A supervisor counts as running exactly when its socket accepts a connection, and `remedy serve stop` sends SIGTERM to the process the process id file names only when the socket answers. (4) `serve_daemon.post_command` sends one envelope with the token read from the token file, for the command line's client mode to use in the next round. (5) R-1131's repair is the import chain this round creates; round 2's selection names every `tests/test_*.py` file and `tests/cli/test_advertised_commands.py`.

ALTERNATIVES. A public handler factory in `ui_server` was rejected for this round as more change in the door's module than one attribute; a visible `serve` group was rejected because it reopens D4's ruled order.

CONSEQUENCE. `remedy serve start`, `remedy serve status` and `remedy serve stop` exist; nothing changes for a user who never starts the supervisor. HOW TO REVERSE: revert round 2's code commits and delete this section.

## DECISION F200 D3 — the command line's client mode sends only the effect: `job stop`, `job pause` and `job unpause` keep their own job resolution, refusals and printing, and hand the one write to the supervisor; a read decides the refusals the door would hide, and a source the command names travels with it (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. DECISION F200 D1 (3) makes the command line a client while a supervisor answers, with the same output and exit code as direct mode. Measured at `7d925b647`: `_cmd_job_stop` in `apps/cli/commands/job_stop_cmd.py` resolves the job id, refuses an unknown, already stopped or completed job, calls `safe_points.request_stop` and prints the whole stop request; the door's `job.stop` answers with the request id alone. `_cmd_job_pause` and `_cmd_job_unpause` in `apps/cli/commands/job_pause_cmd.py` print from the result of `pause_control.pause_job_command` and `unpause_job_command`, whose `refused` result names the state or the task, while the door answers every such refusal 409 with the one message `COMMAND_PAUSE_STATE_MESSAGE`. All three commands take `--source`, defaulting to `cli`; the socket handler of DECISION F200 D2 records `cli` whatever the client sends.

CHOSEN. (1) ONE SEAM PER COMMAND. Each of the three handlers runs everything before its effect as today, and at the effect asks `apps/cli/serve_client.supervisor_answers`; when it holds, `forward_effect` sends the effect as one envelope with a fresh hexadecimal nonce and returns the door's body without its `command` key, so the printing below the seam is the same code in both modes. `job stop` reads the request the door wrote back from disk by its id, pending or already consumed, because it prints the whole request. (2) REFUSALS A READ DECIDES. `pause_control.pause_command_refusal` is the refusal both pause commands begin with, a terminal job state or a task the plan does not hold, extracted unchanged; in client mode the command line calls it before it sends anything, so a refusal prints its reason in both modes and never reaches the door. A refusal the door still answers, a race this read cannot see, is reported under the command's own error token with the door's message, and a supervisor that stops answering mid-request is `serve_unreachable`; neither falls back to writing direct, because the supervisor may already have applied the effect. (3) THE NAMED SOURCE. The socket handler sets `client_names_source`, so a non-empty `args.source` is recorded as given, as `--source` is when the command runs direct; the cockpit's own handler leaves it unset and records `ui` whatever a browser sends. (4) `REMEDY_SERVE_DIRECT`, set to any non-empty value, forces direct mode, so a run the supervisor starts never sends a command back to it. (5) `tests/cli/test_serve_client_parity.py` is the both-modes module of the amended acceptance: every scenario runs through the real argv dispatcher on a data root with no supervisor and on one whose supervisor answers, and output, exit code and the job's control files are compared after the ids and timestamps that differ by construction are replaced; the door's audit file tells the two modes apart.

ALTERNATIVES. A single switch in `apps/cli/grouped.py` that sends a whole command and prints the door's answer was rejected: the door answers with less than the command prints, so every command would need a second printer. Widening the door's 409 body was rejected because the cockpit's door hides refusal detail on purpose.

CONSEQUENCE. With a supervisor running, `job stop`, `job pause` and `job unpause` write through it and print exactly what they print without one; with none, nothing changes. HOW TO REVERSE: revert round 3's code commits and delete this section.

## DECISION F200 D4 — client mode stays with the commands that start, stop, pause and unpause a job, and the other door commands run direct in both modes; the supervisor's socket accepts `job.run`, which the supervisor runs as a child process it records in its run registry (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. DECISION F200 D1 (3) planned to forward every door command the command line shares. Measured at `bb22ee016` by the reviewer's research helper over `job.veto-task`, `job.steer`, `chat.send` and `job.edit-task`, and re-read by the reviewer: each would need its refusal checks extracted for a read before forwarding, a door override for the actor or the steering channel it records, and a read-back of the record the door wrote, because the door's bodies carry less than the commands print; and some answers cannot be made the same at all without widening the cockpit door's bodies, which F009 keeps short on purpose — a steering write failure, a lock timeout, an edit's refusal code. Those commands write control and evidence records that a running job reads at its safe points, under their own locks, so writing them direct is already safe while a supervisor runs. `remedy job run` runs `pingpong_job.run_job` in the foreground.

CHOSEN. (1) Client mode covers `job.stop`, `job.pause`, `job.unpause` and, from the next round, `job.run`. Every other command runs direct in both modes, as the commands the door does not carry already do; a door clause for each is left to the headless API (F253). (2) The cockpit's handler gains `_dispatch_extra_command`, which answers None, and the door calls it after its own clauses and before its 501 guard. The supervisor's socket handler, now a class of its own built by `serve_daemon.socket_handler_class`, accepts `job.run` when it holds a launcher and answers it through that hook, with the door's own audit line, nonce publication and accepted event. (3) `RunLauncher` in `packages/orchestration/serve_runs.py` starts a run as `remedy job run <job>` through the supervisor's interpreter, in a session of its own, with `REMEDY_SERVE_DIRECT` set and the supervisor's data root, its output going to `runs/<job>.out` and `runs/<job>.err`, and records it in `runs/<job>.json`, again with its exit code when it ends. A second `job.run` of a job whose run has not ended is answered 409 with the code `job_already_running`, and nothing waits. (4) A run outlives the supervisor that started it; the restart round decides what a new supervisor does with it.

ALTERNATIVES. Forwarding the four researched commands as D1 planned was rejected for the cost above and for the answers that cannot be made the same. Answering `job.run` through a new clause inside the cockpit door's own chain was rejected: the hook keeps the cockpit's door free of a command its page never sends.

CONSEQUENCE. While a supervisor runs, only those four commands go through it; the feature file's Amendment and operator question Q4 now say so. HOW TO REVERSE: revert round 4's code commits, delete this section and the paragraph it adds to the feature file, and restore Q4's earlier text.

## DECISION F200 D5 — `remedy job run <job>` naming the job alone, with `--json` at most, hands the job to the serve supervisor and follows the run's output to its end; any other option, or a job the data root does not hold, runs direct; every ending the exit-code table has no code for exits 1 (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. DECISION F200 D4 makes `job.run` one of the four client-mode commands, and its round 4 lets the supervisor's socket start a run as a child process running `remedy job run <job>` with its output in `runs/<job>.out` and `runs/<job>.err`. Measured at `17a8cbafc`: `_cmd_job_run` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` takes twenty-four options besides `--json`, most persisted on the job for its next run, checks them, refuses a job `job_resume_refusal` names, and then runs `run_job` in the foreground, printing its report; it has no confirmation prompt. `CLI_EXIT_CODES` in `apps/cli/exit_codes.py` names 0 to 4 and no code for an interrupted command (DECISION F283 D12), and `tests/cli/test_exit_codes.py` reads every handler's exit sites statically.

CHOSEN. (1) WHEN. Client mode applies to `job run` when no option but `--json` is given and the job exists on this data root; then, after every check the command makes today, it sends `job.run` with `args.json` and follows the run. With any other option, or a job the data root does not hold, it runs direct, so its output is the one it always printed; carrying the options through the door would mean writing the command line again on the supervisor's side. (2) THE RUN. The launcher adds `--json` to the run's command when `args.json` is true, and puts the directory holding this code first on the run's `PYTHONPATH`, so that `-m apps.cli.main` runs the supervisor's own code wherever the supervisor was started. (3) FOLLOWING. `serve_client.follow_run` prints the two files as they grow, standard output to standard output and standard error to standard error, until the run's record names this run's process and an exit code, and the command then exits with that code, which is what the same command run direct exits with. Every other ending exits 1, the table's `failed`: Ctrl-C, which stops following, leaves the run going and says how to stop it; a run a signal ended; and a run whose process is gone and whose end was not recorded within five seconds. `tests/cli/test_exit_codes.py` names the one site whose code it cannot read, with that reason. (4) PROOF. `tests/cli/test_serve_client_parity.py` runs a plain `job run` and a `job run --json` of a fake-provider job in both modes and compares output and exit code after the ids, paths, timestamps and durations each mode mints are replaced.

ALTERNATIVES. Passing every option through the envelope was rejected: the door would carry a second copy of `job run`'s argument parsing. A new exit code 130 for Ctrl-C was rejected because it would change F283's ruled table for one command.

CONSEQUENCE. With a supervisor running, `remedy job run <job>` prints what it always printed and the run survives a closed terminal. HOW TO REVERSE: revert round 5's code commits, delete this section and the feature file's D5 paragraph.

## DECISION F200 D6 — the operator answers Q4: decides by delegation; the smaller daemon design DECISIONs F200 D1-D5 already built is confirmed and stands (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT: Operator question Q4 in `.agent/operator_questions.md`, written at F200 round 1 on 2026-10-01, reported that the daemon-mode item's old plan relied on three things since removed or never built — the job queue, running several jobs from one such queue, and the two helpers for notifications and audit export — and that the item was rewritten to one supervisor per data root, answered over the cockpit's own write door on a private unix socket, carrying only the four commands that start, stop, pause and resume a job in client mode, restarting its own registered jobs after a restart, and shipping a systemd unit and a container entrypoint, with the queue, queue-based parallelism, the two helpers and serving the cockpit page from the service left out. The operator's answer arrived via remedy-answer, quoted in full: "Bitte unbedingt selbst entscheiden ob das sinn macht und was es genau tut. Du bist der main orchestrator mit dem besten überblick über das projekt!" ("Please be sure to decide for yourself whether this makes sense and exactly what it does — you are the main orchestrator with the best overview of the project.")

CHOSEN: deciding by delegation, as the operator asked. Rounds 1 through 5 have already built exactly what Q4 described: DECISIONs F200 D1-D5 confine the supervisor to a private unix socket answered by the cockpit's own door, forward only `job.stop`, `job.pause`, `job.unpause` and `job.run` in client mode, and leave the scheduler, queue-based parallelism and the notify/audit-export workers unbuilt because what they would host was retired by DECISIONs F261 D14/D22 or never existed — the same reasoning Q4's own text gives. The design makes sense: it unblocks F201 (remote access), which needs a running supervisor, without reviving a queue the operator had removed on purpose, and the one dropped promise — every other write command still writing direct instead of through the door — costs no record, because those records are already written to be safe mid-run, as DECISION F200 D4 established. No change to the design is ordered; the smaller service stands as built. The Q4 entry is deleted, and `.agent/operator_questions.md` reads EMPTY.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) rebuilding the waiting line so the daemon matches the feature file's original, unamended plan, REJECTED because it reverses DECISIONs F261 D14 and D22, which retired the queue on purpose, for the same reason DECISION F200 D1 already rejected it; (b) widening the door to carry every write command now rather than leaving that to the headless API (F253), REJECTED for the cost and the less-exact error messages DECISION F200 D4 already weighed; (c) holding F200 open pending a second written confirmation from the operator, REJECTED because the operator explicitly delegated the call and asked for a decision now, not another question.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete this paragraph and write the question again; a later session then re-decides whether the smaller daemon design should be reopened or the queue reinstated.

## DECISION F200 D7 — on every start the serve supervisor settles each run its registry still holds open: a run whose process still runs that job is adopted, a job whose own record still reads `running` is run again, and any other run is recorded as ended without a code (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. The amended acceptance of `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F200.md` asks that killing the supervisor and its runs with SIGKILL and starting it again runs every registered job that still reads `running` again, to the end F047's kill test proves. Measured at `70c984073`: `RunLauncher` in `packages/orchestration/serve_runs.py` writes `runs/<job id>.json` when a run starts and again with its exit code when it ends, so a record with no exit code is a run whose end no supervisor saw; each run is started in its own session, so it outlives a supervisor that dies; `remedy job run` on a job whose record reads `running` continues it from its task boundary (`run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`); and `load_job_plan` raises on a record of the wrong shape while `load_job_plan_safe` never raises.

CHOSEN. (1) WHEN. `run_supervisor` calls `RunLauncher.resume_registered` once, after it has bound its socket and written its process id file and before it serves any request, so no `job.run` can race the settling. (2) ADOPTED. A record whose process is still alive and still that job's run is adopted: on Linux the process's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` must hold the job id as one whole argument and its state must not be a zombie, so a process id the system has since given to another program is not mistaken for the run; where `/proc` does not exist, a live process id is enough. The launcher refuses a second `job.run` of an adopted job with `job_already_running`, as it does for its own children, and a watcher records the run's end once the process is gone, with no exit code, because the new supervisor is not its parent. (3) RUN AGAIN. Otherwise, when the job's own record, read with `load_job_plan_safe` through the supervisor's data root, reads `running`, the job is started again as a fresh run with fresh logs; a start that fails with an operating-system error leaves the record as it was, for the next start to try, and does not stop the others. (4) LOST. Every other open record is recorded as ended, with no exit code. (5) PROOF. `tests/orchestration/test_serve_restart_kill.py` runs a supervisor as a real process, starts a fixture job through its socket, kills the supervisor and the run with SIGKILL while a task is in flight, starts a second supervisor on the same data root, and reads from the cycle records on disk that every task ran exactly once and the job completed.

ALTERNATIVES. Running a job again whenever its record has no exit code was rejected, because a run that outlived its supervisor would then run twice at once. Trusting a live process id alone on Linux was rejected, because after a reboot that number can belong to any program, and the job would then never run again. Refusing to start the supervisor when one job record cannot be read was rejected, because one damaged record would then stop every other job.

CONSEQUENCE. A supervisor restarted by its service manager after a crash, or after the machine restarts, carries on with the jobs it was running. HOW TO REVERSE: revert round 6's code commit, delete this section and the feature file's D7 paragraph.

## DECISION F200 D8 — the service manager's unit stops only the supervisor and restarts it on failure, and the container entrypoint hands the container's stop signal straight to the supervisor and demands a data root (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. The amended Task slicing of `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F200.md` names a systemd unit `scripts/serve/remedy-serve.service` and a container entrypoint `scripts/serve/container-entrypoint.sh`. Measured at `13687cae5`: `run_supervisor` in `packages/orchestration/serve_daemon.py` runs in the foreground, ends on SIGTERM or SIGINT and leaves every run it started running, each in its own session, and DECISION F200 D7 adopts such a run when the supervisor starts again; `pyproject.toml` installs the command as the console script `remedy`; and `tests/orchestration/test_env_registry.py` requires every `REMEDY_*` name a shell script expands to be registered in `packages/orchestration/config.py`.

CHOSEN. (1) THE UNIT is a user unit, so it runs as the operator and reads the operator's own data root: `Type=simple`, `ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/remedy serve start`, `Restart=on-failure`, and `KillMode=process`, so that a stop or a restart sends SIGTERM to the supervisor alone and the runs it started go on, as they do when the supervisor runs in a terminal, to be adopted by the next start. Its comments say how to install it, how to keep it running with nobody logged in, how to read its log, where to change the executable's path and how to pin a data root. (2) THE ENTRYPOINT runs the supervisor with `exec`, so the supervisor itself receives the container's stop signal; it refuses with exit code 2 when `REMEDY_DATA_DIR` is unset or empty, because a container's own file system is thrown away with the container; it creates that directory; it passes its own arguments after `serve start`; and `REMEDY_BIN`, registered as an env-only key, names another `remedy` executable. Its comments ask for an init process, `docker run --init`, because only an init process collects the helper processes a run leaves behind. (3) PROOF. `tests/orchestration/test_serve_artifacts.py` reads the unit's settings and runs the entrypoint against a stand-in executable, which records its process id, its data root and its arguments.

ALTERNATIVES. A system-wide unit running as root was rejected, because the supervisor's socket and token are private to the account that owns the data root. Systemd's default, stopping every process of the service, was rejected, because a restart would then kill the runs the restart exists to keep. A container entrypoint that falls back to a default data root was rejected, because work written there disappears with the container.

CONSEQUENCE. An operator can run the supervisor under the user service manager or in a container with the files the repository ships. HOW TO REVERSE: revert round 7's artifact commit, delete this section and the feature file's D8 paragraph.

## DECISION F200 D9 — the acceptance audit's three gaps are each closed by a test, and no product code changes (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. SLOW MODE's hardening stage (operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap) had a fresh auditor, given only the feature file and the repository, name and prove by mutation a test for every statement under F200's Acceptance and Goal & Done headings. Its report, `.agent/f200_acceptance_audit.md`, audited twenty claims at `c820db28a`: seventeen had a proving test at once, among them claims 2 and 3, proven through the real command line, and claim 11, the SIGKILL restart with two real processes, and three were gaps: a STOP request stopping a supervised run (claim 12), the container's init process (claim 17), and client mode's four commands (claim 18). In the reviewer's dry tree on that commit, the tests written for the three gaps passed with no product change, and each turned red under a mutation of the code or text it guards.

CHOSEN. (1) STOP, R-1134. `tests/orchestration/test_serve_stop_file.py` runs one fixture job through `run_cycles` twice, once as a plain process and once started by a real supervisor through `job.run`, and stops each with the real `remedy job stop` command, run direct in the first case and through the supervisor in the second; both ends must read the same: the conductor's status `stopped` in the job's record, the same tasks completed, the same exit codes and the same printed answer once ids are replaced. The fixture stands in for `remedy job run` the way the restart kill test's does, because a real run needs a model provider; what the test proves is that a run the supervisor starts sees the stop request the command line writes through the supervisor. (2) INIT, R-1135. The expectation is kept by telling the operator, so the test requires the entrypoint's header comment and the built-state page to name `docker run --init`. (3) FOUR COMMANDS, R-1136. `tests/cli/test_serve_client_scope.py` reads every module under `apps/` and `packages/` as a syntax tree and requires the commands handed to `forward_effect` to be exactly the four of DECISION F200 D4, each a literal, and the modules that reach the client bridge to be exactly the three that handle them.

ALTERNATIVES. Running a real `remedy job run` in the STOP test was rejected, because it needs a model provider and the restart kill test already set the fixture precedent. Leaving the init-process expectation as an untested comment was rejected, because the hardening stage closes every gap it can. A guard that imports every command module to see what it sends was rejected, because importing runs code, while a syntax tree only reads it.

CONSEQUENCE. Every acceptance statement of F200 now has a test that turns red when the statement stops being true; the audit is repeated for the three statements before the closure. HOW TO REVERSE: delete the three tests and this section, and reopen R-1134, R-1135 and R-1136.

## DECISION F200 D10 — The closure's self-use item SU-043 changed nothing, so no change of it is landed; it is consumed by F200 at the STATUS flip, and its defect is a recurrence of R-1117 (2026-10-01)

CONTEXT. Closure precondition 6 (`docs/roadmap/STATUS_closure_protocol.md`) has every closure run exactly one self-use item to its approval gate. F200's round 10 found the queue empty, generated `SU-043`, "Narrow the excused handler at apps/cli/commands/dev.py:133", and ran it as job `0be4beca71234163` through the `self_use` role, for 4 provider calls and $0.80.
