## DECISION F290 D1 — F290 takes all seven open findings as seven slices, and R-1127 is closed by the interpreter's own audit events rather than by a child test run (2026-10-01)

THE PROBLEM: F290 is the rolling findings paydown registered thin; its first round reads the open set and writes the slice list (operator amendment amend0911-feedback rule B). At the claim base `31542dbfd` the open set is `['R-1117', 'R-1125', 'R-1127', 'R-1128', 'R-1129', 'R-1133', 'R-1137']`, every id registered before the claim date and every one owned by F290. R-1127's remaining gap, as DECISION F294 D10 narrowed it, is that `test_a_root_is_made_without_numbering_the_base_directory` replaces Python's listing and process functions by attribute, so a function the allocator bound to a name of its own before the test ran escapes it; D10 named a check from outside the test process as one possible repair.

CHOSEN: (1) THE SLICES, one per finding, each repair as its own finding text states it: T001 R-1128, the preview end-to-end test draws its nonce with `secrets.token_hex(8)`; T002 R-1127, the audit-event test below; T003 R-1125, a test that every tier row of the README counts the STATUS lines under that tier, with the row corrected where it is wrong; T004 R-1133, a test that every page under `docs/system/` and `docs/guides/` is linked from `docs/README.md`; T005 R-1129, the cockpit's task-edit refusal reads `detail` before `current_version`; T006 R-1117, the apply step refuses a reviewer's pass for a task that changed no file; T007 R-1137, the suite's CPU time measured per test module and either cut or recorded by a decision. Every slice fits one round, so nothing is carried at the claim. (2) R-1127: a new test in `tests/test_data_root_isolation.py` installs one audit hook per test process with `sys.addaudithook`, armed only while it asks the allocator for two roots, and requires the events seen to be exactly two `os.mkdir`. The interpreter raises its audit events inside the C functions themselves, so a listing reached through a name bound at import time, through `glob`, `os.walk`, a started process or a `ctypes` call is seen however the allocator reached it. MEASURED in the reviewer's dry tree on `31542dbfd`: the new test was red under three mutations of the allocator in `tests/conftest.py` — numbering by `scandir` bound to a name at the module's import, `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` per root, and a C library `system` call through `ctypes` — and green restored, while the existing test stayed green under the first and the third. On Python 3.10.12, an aliased `scandir`, `os.listdir`, `glob.glob`, `os.walk`, `subprocess.run`, `os.system` and a `ctypes` call each raised its own event in a probe. (3) THE ORDER: R-1128 and R-1127 in the claim round; R-1125 and R-1133 together, both under `tests/docs/`; R-1129; R-1117; R-1137 last among the repairs, so its measurement reads the suite the other repairs leave; then the amend0930b-slow-cap hardening stage; then closure.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: in this round, nothing in the product. One test stops failing at random, and one test sees a way of listing a directory that the test beside it cannot.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) for R-1127, a child pytest run that records the directories it lists, REJECTED because every child pytest run pays the suite's whole start-up again, which is the cost R-1137 already counts, while the audit hook costs one function call per event in the test process and records nothing while disarmed; (b) removing the old test as redundant, REJECTED because it names the routes one by one and its failure message says which kind of call was made.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete `test_allocating_a_root_raises_no_audit_event_but_one_mkdir` and its two helpers, and rewrite the slice list in `docs/roadmap/features/T2_F290.md`.

## DECISION F290 D2 — a job task that changed no file is blocked by the job's completion gate whatever its reviewer answered, and the test builders that named a file without writing it now write it (2026-10-06)

THE PROBLEM: R-1117. `validate_job_task_result` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`, the gate every job task passes before it is applied, checks the run's final status, its tests, its reviewer's verdict and findings, a mutated target and the staging path, and never whether the task changed a file. A real builder that changes nothing in its first round makes the loop show the reviewer `(no changes — builder confirmed code already correct)` (R-1138), the reviewer passes, and the task is recorded `applied_to_job_workspace`. SU-039 at F044's closure, SU-042 at F292's and SU-043 at F200's each ended that way.

CHOSEN: (1) The gate adds the reason `no_file_changed` when `result.staged_files` is empty, so such a task is blocked as `completion_gate_failed: no_file_changed` and its job blocks, as for every other reason of that gate. `staged_files` holds only files whose content changed: a job-owned worktree compares the tree at the task's start with the tree at its end, and a copy compares staging with the original. A single run outside a job is unchanged and may still end `builder_no_changes`. `describe_self_use_run_defects` still names such a run, now through the task's own error. (2) `test_builder_no_changes_with_reviewer_pass` in `tests/orchestration/test_job_task_runner.py`, which pinned the old answer, becomes `test_builder_no_changes_with_reviewer_pass_blocks` and asserts the new one, and `test_a_job_task_that_changed_no_file_blocks_the_job` drives `run_job` with a builder that writes nothing. (3) Tests in four other files drove jobs with builders that named `docs/README.md` or `one.txt` in their answer and wrote nothing, because the loop writes a fake builder's files only for a `FakeProvider` instance, so they passed only through the hole this decision closes. Each such builder becomes a `FakeProvider` subclass, the loop writes the file it names, and no assertion changes: `_CountingProvider` in `test_predictive_budget.py`, `_VetoingBuilder` and `_SelfVetoingBuilder` in `test_task_veto_runner.py`, `_InjectingBuilder` in `test_task_injection_runner.py`, and the copy-mode `_Simple` of `test_a_non_git_target_commits_nothing` in `test_job_worktree_integration.py`. MEASURED by the reviewer of F290's fourth session in a dry tree on `32cdc1402`: with the new check removed, `tests/orchestration/test_job_task_runner.py` read `2 failed, 213 passed`, the two tests of (2), and restored, `215 passed`; with the gate in place and the four files of (3) at their base, those four files read `7 failed, 126 passed`, the seven tests of the builders named above.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: a job whose task changes no file now stops at that task instead of recording it as done, even when the model says the work was already there. The person sees the task blocked with the reason `no_file_changed`.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) a new task status for "already satisfied" that is not passed and lets the job go on, REJECTED for this round because every reader of a task's status would have to learn it, and nothing measures whether the claim is true; (b) only correcting the sentence the reviewer is shown, REJECTED as the whole repair because R-1117 asks for the outcome to hold whatever the reviewer answers, and registered as R-1138 instead; (c) giving the builder a repair round, as R-0999 does for a failing reviewer, REJECTED because the reviewer passed and a repair round is the reviewer's to order.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete the `no_file_changed` check and its comment from `validate_job_task_result`, restore `test_builder_no_changes_with_reviewer_pass`, delete `test_a_job_task_that_changed_no_file_blocks_the_job`, and delete operator question Q4. The builders of (3) may stay as they are, since they now write the file they name.

## DECISION F290 D3 — the CPU cost F200's serve tests added to the suite is the price of F200 and no cut is made; the rest of the rise between F292's and F200's closures is left to F290's own closure reading (2026-10-06)

THE PROBLEM: R-1137. F200's closure suite used 981.70 CPU seconds against F292's 863.01, 13.8 percent more, above the 10 percent limit of `scripts/closure_suite_cost.py`. The finding asks for the CPU time per test module measured, the modules that grew named, and their cost cut without losing an assertion, or recorded by a decision as the price of F200.

THE MEASUREMENT, committed as `.agent/authored/f290-r5-cpu.txt`: the eleven test modules that differ between the two closure trees, nine F200 added and two it changed, measured one at a time and serially at `fdf873b6c`, read 39.18 CPU seconds together, including one interpreter and pytest start per module. `tests/cli/test_serve_client_parity.py` is about half of it, 19.12 seconds; its two slowest calls each run one real job twice, once directly and once through a running supervisor, and compare what each prints, returns and writes.

CHOSEN: (1) No cut. Each heavy test starts the real supervisor or the real job whose behaviour it asserts, and a cheaper stand-in would assert less. (2) The cost of those eleven modules is recorded here as the price of F200. (3) The rest of the 118.69-second rise, about 80 seconds, is not attributed. F290's closure suite is the next reading, and `scripts/closure_suite_cost.py` compares it with F200's 981.70, so a further rise of more than 10 percent registers a new finding by itself.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) measure every test module at both closure trees, REJECTED because that is two full suites and amend0917-throughput allows one per feature, in the closure; (b) measure only the 202 unchanged modules that name a production module F200 changed, at both trees, REJECTED because that is still two serial runs over about a quarter of the suite, a test pass amend0930-test-load does not allow outside a round's own verification; (c) share one supervisor across the parity tests, REJECTED because each test's assertion is about a fresh data root, and a shared supervisor would carry one test's state into the next.

HOW TO REVERSE: delete this section and the `Done: R-1137` paragraph of `.agent/live_review.md`; R-1137 is then open again and owned by the next paydown.

## DECISION F290 D4 — The closure's self-use item SU-044 lands: the live-UI probe of `remedy dev status` catches the two errors its import can meet, and two tests pin it through the command line (2026-10-06)

THE PROBLEM: F290's closure consumes one self-use item (docs/roadmap/STATUS_closure_protocol.md precondition 6). The queue held none, and the generator's tier 4 supplied `SU-044`: the handler at line 140 of `apps/cli/commands/dev.py`, around the live-UI probe of `remedy dev status`, caught `(ImportError, Exception)`, that is every exception, under an excused `# noqa: BLE001` mark. Round 7 ran the item to its approval gate (job `b30005533dd74be8`, the `self_use` role on `claude-cli`, 6 provider calls, $1.89, reviewer verdict pass, no run defect) and never applied it; the job's change, saved in `.agent/selfuse_f290/job_diff.txt`, narrows the handler to `(ImportError, AttributeError)` and lowers `MAX_EXCUSED` in `tests/test_ble001_ratchet.py` from 286 to 285. No test covered the handler.

CHOSEN: the job's two-line change lands as the job wrote it, before the closure's one full suite, so that suite runs on the tree that ships, as DECISIONs F293 D14 and F294 D11 landed its two siblings. The two types are the ones the probe's import can meet: a module or name that no longer resolves, and a module-level attribute lookup that fails while `ui_server` is first imported. Two new tests in `TestDevStatusCommandSchema` of `tests/regression/test_named_bugs.py`, beside the four for `SU-040` and `SU-041`, drive `remedy dev status --json` through `apps.cli.main.main` with the first import of `packages.orchestration.ui_server` made to raise: for each of the two errors, the command still answers `ok` with `live_ui_ok` false, `reviewer_loop_ok` true and the live-UI blocker listed; and a `RuntimeError` is no longer read as a failed check, so the command exits 1 with the error's name in its JSON envelope. The import is made to fail by a meta-path finder, not by a replaced attribute, because `from m import n` turns an `AttributeError` of a loaded module into an `ImportError`, so only a failing first import can show the probe an `AttributeError`. The reviewer's mutations in its dry tree on `3a5aba4e9`, each run as `python3 -B -m pytest tests/regression/test_named_bugs.py tests/test_ble001_ratchet.py -q -n auto -p no:cacheprovider -k "DevStatus or ratchet or excused or marks"`: the handler widened back to `(ImportError, Exception)` with its mark (the defect test and the ratchet red); `ImportError` dropped; `AttributeError` dropped; `RuntimeError` added; and `MAX_EXCUSED` left at 286 (the ratchet red). Each turned the test it guards red; restored, 22 passed.

WHAT THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOURALLY, STATED PLAINLY: `remedy dev status` still reports a live-UI module that cannot be loaded as a failed check when the load fails in one of the two expected ways. A defect of any other kind now stops the command with its own name, where before it was hidden as a failed check.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) keeping only `ImportError`, REJECTED because a module-level attribute lookup in `ui_server` or in a module it imports raises `AttributeError` at the probe's import, which is the failure the check exists to report; (b) narrowing the two sibling handlers at lines 126 and 133 in the same change, REJECTED because the item names one mark, and the generator offers each mark as an item of its own.

HOW TO REVERSE: restore the handler's `except (ImportError, Exception):` line with its `# noqa: BLE001` mark, set `MAX_EXCUSED` back to 286, and delete the two tests and the helper named above.

## DECISION F295 D1 — F295 runs in four slices, T001 to T004 in the feature file's order, one round each; the claim's measurement is `.agent/f295_inventory.md`, and one Acceptance line is added for the order-file detection rule (2026-10-06)

A run with the fake builder and reviewer and `--json --no-ui --yes`, its stdin an open pipe nobody wrote to, ended with `stopped_before_apply` true and exit 0 without blocking, and no test pins that it never reads stdin. `.agent/f295_inventory.md` records every command and its reading.

Each slice's own spellings, such as the order file's header format, the digest section's name and version and the decision fields, are ruled by a DECISION in the round that lands that slice, per operator amendment amend0917-throughput rule 3. One Acceptance line is added now, because the measurement shows one gap the existing lines do not name: an order such as `fix the heading in README.md` is text that ends in `.md`, and it must stay text.

ALTERNATIVES: T002 before T001, REJECTED because T004's gate test starts from an order file, and T001 is the smallest slice with production code, so it proves the round shape first. T001 and T002 in one round, REJECTED because SLOW MODE prefers smaller rounds.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete the section `## Slice order (written at the claim, 2026-10-06)` and the Acceptance line that begins "An order argument that holds whitespace" from `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F295.md`, and this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D2 — an order file is one path ending in `.md`; its optional header sits between two `---` lines and names `project`, `contract`, `max-cost-usd` and any number of `constraint` lines; a flag wins over the header; and an order file without a cost cap is refused before any step (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T001 of `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F295.md` orders `remedy do <order.md>` to read the order from a Markdown file with an optional header, to let a command-line flag win over the header, and to refuse a missing, empty or unreadable file, and a file that carries no cost cap, before any step. DECISION F259 D2 named the argument "text or a `.md` path" without a rule for telling the two apart, and DECISION F295 D1 added the Acceptance line that keeps `fix the heading in README.md` a text order. The claim's measurement (`.agent/f295_inventory.md`) shows that `remedy do order.md` plans the text `order.md` today.

CHOSEN: (1) THE RULE. The argument of `remedy do` names an order file when, with its outer whitespace stripped, it is not empty, holds no whitespace, and ends in `.md` in any letter case. Every other argument is order text, exactly as before. A path is read relative to the working directory of the command. (2) THE FILE. It is read as UTF-8, a leading byte-order mark allowed. When its first line is exactly `---`, the lines up to the next line that is exactly `---` are its header, and everything after that line is the order; otherwise the whole file is the order. In the header a blank line is ignored and every other line is `key: value` with a non-empty value. The keys are `project`, `contract` and `max-cost-usd`, each at most once and each meaning what the flag of the same name means, and `constraint`, as often as needed, each one a sentence the plan must honour. (3) THE CONSTRAINTS. They reach the planner as part of the order: the order the plan step reads is the file's order text followed by a blank line, the line `Constraints the plan must honour:` and one `- <constraint>` line each, in the file's order. (4) PRECEDENCE. `--project`, `--contract` and `--max-cost-usd` each win over the header key of the same name; the header's value is used only when the flag is absent, and every value then passes the same checks a flag's value passes. (5) THE REFUSALS, each exit 2 before any step, each message naming the path and ending "Nothing was run.": `order_file_not_found` for a path that does not exist; `order_file_unreadable` for a path that cannot be read as a UTF-8 file, a directory among them; `order_file_invalid_header` for a header that is not closed, a line without `key: value`, an unknown key, an empty value or a repeated single key, naming the line; `order_file_empty` for an order text that is empty once stripped; and `order_file_no_cost_cap` for an order file whose header sets no `max-cost-usd` while no `--max-cost-usd` is given, naming that rule. (6) THE CODE. One new module, `packages/orchestration/order_file.py`, reads and checks the file and knows nothing of the command line; `_cmd_do` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` calls it first, before every other check, and carries the result into the existing flow. The format is written down for a client on the contract page T004 writes.

ALTERNATIVES: A separate `--order-file` flag, REJECTED because DECISION F259 D2 decided the positional `<order>` that is "text or a `.md` path". Reading any argument that names an existing `.md` file, REJECTED because a missing file must be refused rather than silently planned as text, which is the defect the measurement found. YAML for the header, REJECTED because the four keys need no nesting and a YAML reader would be a new dependency. A refusal for an order TEXT without a cost cap, REJECTED because the feature file binds the cap to an order read from a file, the unattended case, and a person at a terminal keeps today's behaviour.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `packages/orchestration/order_file.py`, its line in `tests/orchestration/import_reachability_allowlist.txt`, the order-file block at the top of `_cmd_do`, the two test files `tests/orchestration/test_order_file.py` and `tests/cli/test_do_order_file.py`, restore the `goal` argument's help text in `apps/cli/command_catalog.py`, and delete this paragraph. The record files this round appended to keep their entries, because they record that the decision was made.

## DECISION F295 D3 — a mission started from an order file records the file's absolute path and the sha256 of the bytes Remedy read, beside the order text it acted on (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: Finding R-1141. `MissionOrder` keeps `text`, `source_path` and `source_sha256` (DECISION F260 D1: "text, or file path + sha256"), and the plan step of `remedy do` writes only the text. DECISION F295 D2 made `remedy do <order.md>` read an order file, so a mission now can come from a file, and its record says nothing about that.

CHOSEN: `read_order_file` in `packages/orchestration/order_file.py` returns, besides what DECISION F295 D2 rules, the file's path resolved to an absolute path and the lowercase hex sha256 of the exact bytes it read, a byte-order mark included, as `OrderFile.source_path` and `OrderFile.source_sha256` — spelled as `MissionOrder` spells them, one spelling per concept. `_cmd_do` passes both to the walk as two new `DoContext` fields, `order_source_path` and `order_source_sha256`, empty for an order given as text, and the plan step writes `MissionOrder(text=ctx.order, source_path=ctx.order_source_path, source_sha256=ctx.order_source_sha256)`. The `text` stays the order Remedy acted on, which for an order file is the file's order text followed by its constraints, so a reader who hashes the file and compares the digest learns whether the file has changed since; the text alone could not tell them.

ALTERNATIVES: The path as the user typed it, REJECTED because a relative path names nothing once the working directory is gone. The digest of the decoded text, REJECTED because the digest exists to be checked against the file on disk, and only the bytes are on disk. Recording the source on the job as well, through `JobPlan.job_file_sha256`, REJECTED for this round because the finding names the mission's record, and a mission's jobs each point at their mission.

HOW TO REVERSE: Remove the two `OrderFile` fields, the two `DoContext` fields and their passing in `_cmd_do` and `_cmd_do_order`, restore `MissionOrder(text=ctx.order)` in the plan step, delete the tests the F295 R4 block names for R-1141, and delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D4 — the digest is a `client` object in every `remedy status --json` answer, version 1, covering every project on the data root whatever the scope; this round lands its frame — projects, missions, jobs, the jobs that wait for apply and the supervisor — and the next lands decisions, costs and evidence (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T002 of `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F295.md` orders `remedy status --json` to gain one versioned section for a machine client, read from the records alone and cheap enough to read once a minute. The claim's measurement (`.agent/f295_inventory.md`) shows `remedy status --json` answering only the current project's jobs grouped by state, a count of open decisions, the runtime and pending stops. The records the section needs exist: the project registry, each project's missions with their job links and order, every job's record, the job-apply audit records under the data root's `job_apply_records` directory, which hold `"status": "applied"` once an apply landed, and the supervisor's unix socket, which `socket_answers` in `packages/orchestration/serve_daemon.py` probes. A decision's question and default are carried differently by each decision type, which is why the section lands in two rounds.

CHOSEN: (1) THE KEY. Every successful `remedy status --json` answer carries `client`, an object, beside the keys it already has, which keep their meaning and their project scope; the text output is unchanged. (2) VERSION 1 OF THE FRAME. `client` holds `version` (the integer 1); `read_at`, the UTC time of the read in ISO 8601, the one value that comes from the clock and not from a record; `supervisor`, an object whose `answers` is true when a process accepts a connection on the supervisor's socket under the data root; `projects`, one object per registered project sorted by slug, each with `project_id`, `slug` and `missions`, the project's missions newest first, each with `mission_id`, `status`, `goal`, `job_ids` in the mission's order, `order_source_path` and `order_source_sha256` (empty for an order given as text, DECISION F295 D3); `jobs`, one object per job on the data root sorted by job id, each with `job_id`, `project_id`, `mission_id` (null when no mission links it), `title`, `state` (the job's state word) and `waits_for_apply`; `awaiting_apply`, the ids of the jobs whose `waits_for_apply` is true, sorted; and `degraded` with `skipped_files`, false and empty unless a job or mission file could not be read. (3) WAITING FOR APPLY. A job waits for apply when its state is `completed` and no job-apply record of it reads `"status": "applied"`; a new public reader in `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py`, `job_apply_landed(job_id)`, answers the second half, because that module owns the records. (4) WHERE. One new module, `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py`, builds the object with `build_client_digest(now=None)` from the records alone and never writes; `_cmd_status` in `apps/cli/commands/status_cmd.py` adds it to its JSON answer. (5) THE NEXT ROUND adds, under the same version, every open decision across jobs with its question, its documented default and its age, each job's measured cost with its basis and its evidence references, and each project's cost of the day.

ALTERNATIVES: A new command such as `remedy digest`, REJECTED because the feature file names `remedy status --json`. Nesting each project's jobs under the project, REJECTED because a job whose project is not registered would then have nowhere to go; the flat list names every job once with its project. Scoping the section to the current project as the rest of the answer is, REJECTED because the client is one runner watching every project, and the feature file says every registered project. `waits_for_apply` read from the `do` walk's own result, REJECTED because only the apply record survives the process that ran the walk.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py`, its line in `tests/orchestration/import_reachability_allowlist.txt`, `job_apply_landed` in `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py`, the `client` key in `_cmd_status`, the tests the F295 R5 block names, and this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D5 — the digest lists every open decision of every job with its question, its documented default, its options, its bundled questions and its age; costs and evidence follow in the next round, still under version 1 (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F295 D4 (5) left the digest's open decisions, costs and evidence to a second round. A decision's question and default are carried differently by each type, measured at `7936f8104` in `list_decisions` of `packages/orchestration/decision_queue.py`: a task decision's payload holds `question`, `options` and `safe_default`; the task-plan approval's payload holds `options` (`approve`, `reject`) and, when the plan has open questions, `clarifications`, each with `id`, `question` and `default_answer`, and the approval itself has no default because it is the approval gate; every other type states its question only in `safe_summary`, and some carry `options` (a stop reason's `extend` and `abandon`). `remedy status` already counts open decisions with `list_decisions(job, load_run_events(resolve_data_root(), job.job_id))`. SLOW MODE prefers the smaller round, so this round lands the decisions alone.

CHOSEN: `client` gains `decisions`, a list of every decision whose `status` is `open` across every job on the data root, sorted by job id and then decision id, each an object with exactly: `job_id`; `project_id` (the job's); `decision_id`; `type`; `severity`; `question` — the payload's `question` for a task decision, the decision's `safe_summary` for every other type; `default` — the payload's `safe_default` for a task decision when it is not empty, and null otherwise, null meaning that no default is documented; `options` — the payload's `options` as a list of strings, or an empty list; `clarifications` — for a task-plan approval the payload's `clarifications`, each as `{"id", "question", "default"}` with `default` taken from `default_answer` (null when empty), and an empty list for every other type; `created_at` — the decision's own, possibly empty; and `age_seconds` — the whole seconds from `created_at` to `read_at`, a `created_at` without an offset read as UTC, and null when `created_at` is empty or not ISO 8601. A job whose decisions cannot be read makes `degraded` true and adds `decisions of job <job_id>` to `skipped_files`; the rest of the digest is still answered. The builder reads, never writes; one new private helper in `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py` maps one `HumanDecision` to its entry.

ALTERNATIVES: Inventing a default for the plan approval, such as `approve`, REJECTED because the approval is the gate a machine order must not pass on its own (the feature file's Do-not-touch), so no default is documented and null says so. One entry per bundled question instead of one per decision, REJECTED because `list_decisions` bundles them on purpose, its F034 comment reading "One plan, one human touchpoint — never one decision per question", and one `decision resolve` answers them all. Reading only the jobs that are not terminal, REJECTED because a completed job can still hold an open decision and the count `remedy status` already prints reads every job of its scope.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete the `decisions` key and its helper from `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py`, the tests the F295 R6 block names, and this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D6 — the digest's decision read catches the four exception classes a damaged record raises, named in one tuple, and lets every other error through (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: R-1142's repair clause, drafted at the end of F295's first session, names `except (OSError, ValueError):`. Measured at `13a7e9088`, `load_run_events` in `packages/orchestration/timeline.py` skips a run-log line only on `json.JSONDecodeError` and then sorts the events with `e.get("timestamp", "")`: a line that is JSON but not an object raises `AttributeError` there, and two events whose timestamps are a number and a string raise `TypeError` (R-1143). Both are damaged records, not defects of the digest, and with the drafted pair either one would end `remedy status --json` with a traceback, which DECISION F295 D5 rules out by naming only that job's decisions as skipped.

CHOSEN: One module constant in `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py`, `_DECISION_READ_ERRORS = (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError, TypeError)`, with a comment naming the record fault behind each class; the per-job decision read catches exactly that tuple and carries no `noqa` mark, so the count of excused blind handlers that `tests/test_ble001_ratchet.py` freezes returns to 285. Every other exception propagates. Tests in `tests/orchestration/test_client_digest.py`: the existing unreadable-job test's stand-in raises `OSError` instead of `RuntimeError`; one parametrized test writes each damaged run log for one job and finds that job named in `skipped_files` while the other job's decision is listed; and one test proves that a `RuntimeError` from the read propagates instead of being reported as degradation.

ALTERNATIVES: The drafted `(OSError, ValueError)`, REJECTED for the two measured faults above. Repairing `load_run_events` itself in this round, REJECTED: the reader serves 30 files under `packages/` and `apps/`, so its contract change is a round of its own, and it is registered as R-1143 for the findings paydown F297; the digest must survive whatever the reader raises on a record it cannot read either way. Catching every exception under a reasoned `noqa` mark, REJECTED because the ratchet is frozen and its own message says to narrow the handler.

HOW TO REVERSE: Replace the tuple with `(OSError, ValueError)`, delete the parametrized test and the propagation test the F295 R7 block names, and delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D7 — each job carries its measured cost with its exactness basis and references to its evidence, each project its ledger cost of the UTC day, through the readers the job digest and the cockpit already own; T002 closes (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F295 D4 (5) left each job's cost and evidence references and each project's cost of the day to a later round. Measured at `6a8055359`: `_cost_section` in `packages/orchestration/job_digest.py` turns a job's persisted budget actuals into DECISION F040 D4's exactness basis — `absent` when no cost was measured, `lower_bound` when a provider call went unpriced, `actual` otherwise — but carries the figure only as a rendered string such as `$1.2500`; `decode_persisted_budget_actuals` in `packages/orchestration/budget_guard.py` yields the figure as a number and raises only `BudgetCounterError`, a `ValueError`, on a damaged record. `project_summary` in `packages/orchestration/project_cockpit.py` already answers a project's `cost_today` from the token ledger with `query_cost` over the UTC day, as `day`, `value_usd`, `basis` and `calls`, and `query_cost` raises `OSError` or `sqlite3.Error` on a ledger it cannot open or read. A job's evidence lives in `job_evidence_dir`, which holds the post-mortem and the run manifest its record names; the result diff its record names lives in `job_dir`; the record lists its runs in `run_refs`. Measured in the reviewer's dry run: a synthetic data root of 200 jobs with 400 open decisions, 50 run-log events per job and three ledgers of 100 calls read in a median of 0.066 seconds over five reads.

CHOSEN: (1) REFACTOR FIRST, behaviour unchanged: `job_digest.py` gains the public `cost_exactness_basis(measured_cost_usd, unpriced_call_count)`, which `_cost_section` now calls, and `project_cockpit.py` gains the public `project_cost_of_day(project_id, moment)`, which `project_summary` now calls. (2) Each entry of `jobs` gains `cost`, `{"value_usd", "basis"}` — the decoded `measured_cost_usd` as a number or null and `cost_exactness_basis` of it — and `evidence`, `{"evidence_dir", "run_ids", "postmortem_path", "run_manifest_path", "result_diff_path", "result_diff_sha256"}`: absolute paths, each null unless it is on disk (the directory a directory, each file a file), `run_ids` the record's `run_refs`, and the digest of the result diff as recorded or null. (3) Each entry of `projects` gains `cost_today`, exactly what `project_cost_of_day` answers for the UTC day of `read_at`. (4) A job whose actuals raise `BudgetCounterError` reads `cost` null and adds `cost of job <job_id>` to `skipped_files`; a project whose ledger raises `OSError` or `sqlite3.Error` reads `cost_today` null and adds `cost of the day of project <project_id>`; both make `degraded` true. (5) The version stays 1, and with this round T002 is complete.

ALTERNATIVES: Carrying the job digest's rendered string, REJECTED because a program would have to parse `>= $0.5000` back into a number. Summing each project's jobs' costs for its cost of the day, REJECTED because a job's actuals are cumulative and carry no day, while the ledger records every call with its UTC time and is what the cockpit already shows. Adding each job's cost cap beside its cost, REJECTED for this round: the feature file asks for the measured cost and its basis, and the client set the cap itself in the order file. Evidence paths relative to the data root, REJECTED because the runner reads files on the same machine and an absolute path needs no second rule.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `_job_cost`, `_job_evidence`, `_existing_file`, `_LEDGER_READ_ERRORS`, the `cost`, `evidence` and `cost_today` keys and their imports from `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py`, the tests the F295 R8 block names, and this paragraph; the two extracted readers may stay, since they change no behaviour.

## DECISION F295 D8 — T003 lands in two rounds: first the proof that an unattended run never reads stdin, with every child it starts reading end-of-file; then every decision kind answerable with `--json` (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T003 asks for two things of different size. Measured at `977e6e5e5`: the only reads of stdin in `apps/` and `packages/` are `input()` in `apps/cli/cost_preview_confirm.py`, which refuses a stdin that is not a terminal before it would ask unless `--yes` is given, and `input()` in `apps/cli/commands/chat_cmd.py`, which no machine-client command reaches; `remedy do` reads none. The builder's and the reviewer's child processes inherit Remedy's stdin (R-1145). On the other side, `decision resolve` answers the plan approval, a task decision, a proposal, a re-plan proposal and a stop reason, while a budget stop's `extend` and `abandon`, a patch intent and a hunk decision are answered by other commands or by none; that part needs its own measurement round. SLOW MODE prefers the smaller round.

CHOSEN: (1) This round: R-1145's repair, `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` on the two spawns, and four tests that each start a real process whose stdin is a pipe nobody writes to and nobody closes and that wait on it with a timeout, never through `communicate()`, which would close the pipe: `remedy do <order> --json --no-ui --yes --no-llm` with the fake providers and a cost cap finishes with exit 0 and `stopped_before_apply` true; the F114 confirmation for an estimate that always asks proceeds with `--yes` and refuses with exit 2 and `confirmation_required` without it; and a child started through `run_guarded` and through `run_streamed_command` reads end-of-file at once. (2) The next round measures, for every decision kind `list_decisions` raises, which command answers it under `--json` and whether the answer is recorded as the cockpit's door records it, and closes what is missing; the budget raise and the hunk decision are named in the feature file and are its first items.

ALTERNATIVES: One round for all of T003, REJECTED under SLOW MODE: the decision kinds need a measurement this round does not have. An in-process test that replaces `sys.stdin`, REJECTED as the only proof: it cannot see a child process inheriting the real file descriptor, which is how R-1145 was found. Closing Remedy's own stdin at start-up, REJECTED: an interactive operator's prompts would lose their terminal.

HOW TO REVERSE: Remove the two `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` arguments and the four tests the F295 R9 block names, and delete this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D9 — `remedy job resume` and the loop's resume refuse a job its budget stopped until its budget decision is answered, exit 3 with `budget_decision_open` and the decision's id; the answer itself, the run manifest of a `remedy do` job and the resume's providers follow in rounds of their own (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: Finding R-1147. Measured at `5a3ba7cd4` with `.remedy-wt/f295-r10/probe_preview.py`, on a scratch data root with the fake providers: a job planned by `remedy do <order> --plan-only` and run by `remedy job run <job> --deadline 2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00` records the stop block with `source` `budget` and a request id `budget_<hash>`, `remedy decision list <job> --json` lists the decision `budget:<that request id>`, and `remedy job resume <job> --dry-run --json` answers `"would_run": true`. The job's `status` stays `planned` (R-1148), so a guard keyed on the `stopped` state would miss it. `decide_checkpoint_resume` in `packages/orchestration/checkpoints.py` is the one guard function that both `_cmd_job_resume` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py` and `resume_milestone_job` in `packages/orchestration/orchestrator_loop.py` call. `list_decisions` in `packages/orchestration/decision_queue.py` lists the budget decision whenever the job's `stop_source` contains `budget`, and names it `budget:<request id>`, or `budget_exhausted` when the stop event carried no request id.

CHOSEN: (1) `packages/orchestration/decision_queue.py` gains the public `budget_decision_id(request_id: str) -> str`, which returns `budget:<request_id>` for a non-empty id and `budget_exhausted` otherwise, and `list_decisions` names the budget decision through it; no behaviour changes. (2) `decide_checkpoint_resume` gains a fourth guard, run after the all-green check, so that a pending stop request, a drifted worktree, the plan gate and an all-green job each still decide first: a job whose `stop_source` is exactly `budget` is refused, `RESUME_REFUSED` with the reason `budget_stopped` and a detail naming the stop reason and the decision id `budget_decision_id(job.stop_request_id)`. (3) `_cmd_job_resume` renders that reason as the refusal `budget_decision_open` with exit code 3 and the payload key `decision_id`; its message says that the job was stopped by its budget, names the stop reason and the decision id, says that the job does not resume until that decision is answered, and names `remedy decision list <job> --json`. Nothing is consumed and nothing runs. (4) The `--dry-run` preview gains `budget_stop`, an object `{"stopped", "decision_id"}` whose `decision_id` is the empty string when `stopped` is false; `would_run` is false while `stopped` is true; and the text preview gains one line before its `would run` line, `  budget stop:   ` followed by `OPEN — decision <id>, resume would refuse` or by `none`. (5) The rounds that follow, in this order: R-1148, so that a budget stop of a `remedy do` job is durable; R-1146, the answer to the budget decision under `--json`; the rest of R-1147, `remedy job resume` running the job's own providers; then the hunk decision, and T004.

ALTERNATIVES: Keying the guard on the `stopped` state, REJECTED because a `remedy do` job its budget stopped reads `planned` today (R-1148). Asking `list_decisions` whether an open `token_budget` decision exists, REJECTED for this round: it also reads memory cards, proposals and the run log on every call, and it keys the budget decision on the same `stop_source` field. Refusing every stopped job, REJECTED because an operator's stop has its own resume rule, rule 1 of the same function. Running the guard before the all-green check, REJECTED because a job whose tasks all completed has nothing left to spend, and its resume is a no-op.

HOW TO REVERSE: Remove the fourth guard and its docstring lines from `decide_checkpoint_resume`, the `budget_stopped` branch from `_cmd_job_resume`, the `budget_stop` key, its text line and its term in `would_run` from the preview, the tests the F295 R10 block names, and this paragraph; `budget_decision_id` may stay, since it changes no behaviour.

## DECISION F295 D10 — a job `remedy do` plans records, as its `job_file_sha256`, the sha256 of the order text it was planned from, so its run manifest is written and a budget stop of it ends `stopped`; the other job origins that record none are R-1149 (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: Finding R-1148. The job-input check of the run manifest in `packages/orchestration/run_manifest.py` requires `job_file_sha256` as 64 lowercase hex, under its comment "F6: REQUIRED facts, not optional decoration — an empty value is not a valid definition". Only the job-file parser in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` sets it; the three `JobPlan` constructions of `plan_order_job` in `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py` — for an LLM task plan, for an LLM task plan that failed, and for the deterministic plan — set none. Measured in the reviewer's dry tree at `9233a90bc`, with each of the three given the sha256 of `mission.encode("utf-8")`: `remedy do <order> --json --no-ui --yes --no-llm --max-cost-usd 1` with the fakes writes `run_manifest.json` with an empty manifest error, and `remedy status --json` names that file as the job's `run_manifest_path`; a job planned with `--plan-only` and run with `--deadline 2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00` reads `status` `stopped` beside the stop block with `source` `budget`, and `remedy job resume <job> --dry-run --json` answers `"would_run": false`; and the fifteen test files nearest the path, listed in `.remedy-wt/f295-r11/dry_targets.txt`, read `520 passed`.

CHOSEN: (1) `plan_order_job` computes once, from the order text it plans — its `mission`, which is the `order` argument — the lowercase hex sha256 of that text's UTF-8 bytes, and passes it to each of its three `JobPlan` constructions as `job_file_sha256`. For an order file that text is the file's order text with its constraints, the text Remedy acted on; the file's own bytes stay recorded on the mission (DECISION F295 D3). For one job of a mission with several jobs it is the goal of the milestone outline the job was planned from. (2) A one-line comment directly above the computation says why: the run manifest requires the digest of the job's defining input, and a job planned from an order is defined by that order text. (3) Nothing else changes: not the mission record, not the job record's other fields, and not the manifest's rule.

ALTERNATIVES: The digest of the order file's bytes, REJECTED: a job of a mission with several jobs is planned from a milestone outline's goal and not from the file, so the rule must name the input of the job itself, and the file's digest is already on the mission. Accepting an empty digest in the manifest, REJECTED: the manifest's own rule calls the field a required fact. A digest over the job's tasks, REJECTED: the tasks are derived from the order, and a change to how a task plan is normalised would change the job's identity.

HOW TO REVERSE: Remove the computation, its comment and the three `job_file_sha256=` arguments from `plan_order_job`, the tests the F295 R11 block names, and this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D11 — a budget decision is answered `extend` by `remedy decision resolve <job> <decision> --reason extend --answer <limit>=<value>`: the raised limits are written to the job, the answer is recorded on the job, and the decision and the resume guard read the stop as answered until the job stops again; `abandon` is ruled and landed by the next round (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: Finding R-1146. Measured at `6aec8d959`: `_cmd_decision_resolve` in `apps/cli/commands/decision.py` has no branch for a budget decision and answers `decision_not_resolvable`, while `run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`, the `remedy job run` command in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` and `remedy job budget <job> set` each refuse new limits for a stopped job and send the caller to that decision. A budget stop's request id is a digest of the job id, the episode id and the stop reason (the `_StopSignal` built in `run_job`), so a job that stops a second time for the same limit in the same episode carries the same request id again, while every stop that is finalized writes a new `stopped_at`. A stop reason names its limit after its last colon, as `budget_exhausted:deadline` or `predicted_budget_exhausted:max_cost_usd`, in the field names of `JobBudgets`; `min_free_disk_bytes` is the one floor among them and is set in configuration, never per job. `--answer` already exists on `decision resolve`, for the plan approval's bundled questions only. The cockpit's `_answerable_by_decision_resolve` in `packages/orchestration/decision_inbox.py` mirrors the HTTP write door, which answers no budget decision; that door is F253's under the feature file's Do-not-touch.

CHOSEN: (1) THE COMMAND. `remedy decision resolve <job> <decision> --reason extend --answer <limit>=<value>`, `--answer` repeatable, where `<decision>` is the id `remedy decision list` prints for the budget stop, `budget:<request id>` or `budget_exhausted`; `<limit>` is one of `max_total_tokens`, `max_provider_calls`, `max_wall_clock_minutes`, `max_cost_usd` and `deadline`; and `<value>` is parsed exactly as the `remedy job run` flag of the same name parses it. The help text of `--answer` names both of its uses. (2) THE RULES, each a refusal before anything is written and each exiting 1, the code every other branch of `_cmd_decision_resolve` gives its refusals: the decision must be the job's open budget decision (`decision_not_found`); a decision answered since the job last stopped is `decision_already_answered`; `--reason` must be `extend` (`invalid_argument`, naming `extend`); at least one `--answer` is given (`missing_argument`); every `--answer` is `<limit>=<value>` with a limit named above and a value that parses (`invalid_budget`, the token `remedy job run` already gives a bad limit); the limit the stop reason names is among the answered ones, unless the reason names none (`budget_limit_not_raised`); and every answered ceiling is strictly greater than the job's current value for it when it has one, a deadline strictly later than both its current value and the time of the answer (`budget_limit_not_raised`). A stop by `min_free_disk_bytes` is refused as `budget_limit_not_raisable`. (3) THE EFFECT. The job's `budgets` become its current budgets with the answered limits replaced, validated by `JobBudgets`; one record is appended to the list `job.metadata["budget_decision_answers"]` — `decision_id`, `request_id`, `option` `extend`, `raised` (each answered limit with its new value as the job's `budgets` store it), `answered_at` (UTC, ISO 8601) and `actor` `cli` — and the command then saves the job. Its state and its stop record are not changed: it stays `stopped` and keeps its pending work. The JSON answer carries `decision_id`, `job_id`, `outcome` `extended`, `raised`, `budgets` and `next_command` `remedy job run <job> --json`. (4) ANSWERED UNTIL THE NEXT STOP. A budget stop counts as answered when the job holds such a record whose `answered_at` is not earlier than the job's `stopped_at`, both read as times; a stop finalized after the answer is open again, under the same request id or another. `packages/orchestration/decision_queue.py` gains two public readers, `budget_stop_answer(job)`, that record or None, and `open_budget_decision_id(job)`, the decision id while the job's `stop_source` is `budget` and its stop is not answered and the empty string otherwise; `list_decisions` leaves the budget decision out while `budget_stop_answer` finds a record; and the resume guard of DECISION F295 D9 and its preview key on `open_budget_decision_id` instead of on `stop_source` alone. (5) WHERE. One new module, `packages/orchestration/budget_decision.py`, holds `answer_budget_decision(job, decision_id, option, answers, *, now)`, which applies the rules and the effect to the job it is given without saving it, and returns `{"outcome": "refused", "code", "detail"}`, whose `code` is the refusal's token from (2), or `{"outcome": "extended", "raised", "budgets", "record"}`, as `answer_replan_proposal` in `packages/orchestration/veto_proposal.py` answers its decision; `packages/orchestration/budget_resolution.py` gains the public `parse_budget_limit(name, raw)`, built on the parsers `resolve_job_budgets` already uses; and `_cmd_decision_resolve` gains one branch for a budget decision id and admits `--answer` for it. (6) THE COCKPIT. Its write door answers no budget decision, and `_answerable_by_decision_resolve` keeps reading one as not answerable; widening that door is F253's. (7) `abandon` is ruled and landed by the next round.

ALTERNATIVES: Five flags such as `--max-cost-usd` on `decision resolve`, REJECTED: `--answer` exists for the answers a decision needs, and five flags on the command for every decision kind would apply to one kind. Clearing the job's stop record on `extend`, REJECTED: that record names the stop's post-mortem and its manifest, and an operator's stop keeps its record after a later run too. Keying the answer on the request id alone, REJECTED for the reason the context measures. Moving the job to `planned`, REJECTED: `stopped` already means that the job keeps its pending work and resumes at its first pending task.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `packages/orchestration/budget_decision.py` and its line in `tests/orchestration/import_reachability_allowlist.txt`; delete `parse_budget_limit`, `budget_stop_answer`, `open_budget_decision_id` and the skip in `list_decisions`; delete the budget branch and the `--answer` admission in `_cmd_decision_resolve` and the `--answer` help sentence; return the guard of DECISION F295 D9 and its preview to `stop_source`; take `invalid_budget`, `budget_limit_not_raised` and `budget_limit_not_raisable` out of `_PINNED_TOKENS` in `tests/cli/test_decision_cmd.py`; delete the tests the F295 R12 block names, and this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D12 — a budget decision answered `abandon` cancels the job: its state becomes `cancelled`, the answer is recorded as `extend`'s is, and a cancelled job never runs again through `remedy job run`, `remedy job resume`, the loop's resume or `run_job` itself; and a test pins D11's rule on a deadline earlier than the current one (R-1150) (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: The second half of finding R-1146, and R-1150. The budget decision's option `abandon` reads, in `list_decisions` of `packages/orchestration/decision_queue.py`, "The job stops with the artifacts it has, and nothing further is spent against" the exhausted limit. `RunState.CANCELLED` is one of `JOB_TERMINAL_STATES` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`, "the states a job NEVER runs again from", which `packages/orchestration/data_reclaim.py` reads to free a job's workspace. Read at `e44057b21`: no code sets a job to `cancelled`, and neither `run_job`, nor `_cmd_job_run` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py`, nor `decide_checkpoint_resume` in `packages/orchestration/checkpoints.py` refuses a job in that state. `_cmd_job_run` already refuses a job that cannot be continued with `job_not_resumable` and exit 1 (R-0913), and the catalog entry `job.run` declares no exit code above the floor, while `job.resume` declares 3. Measured at `e44057b21` in the reviewer's mutation that R-1150 records, the check that an answered deadline is later than the job's current one is not pinned by any test.

CHOSEN: (1) `remedy decision resolve <job> <decision> --reason abandon` answers the open budget decision; `--answer` beside it is refused as `option_not_applicable`, the token the command already gives an option that does not apply, exit 1. `answer_budget_decision` checks the decision id and the answered state first, as for `extend`. (2) THE EFFECT: the job's state becomes `cancelled`; its budgets, tasks and stop record are unchanged; one record is appended to `job.metadata["budget_decision_answers"]` with `option` `abandon` and `raised` `{}`, its other keys as D11 (3) rules; the command saves the job and answers `decision_id`, `job_id`, `outcome` `abandoned` and `state` `cancelled`. (3) A CANCELLED JOB NEVER RUNS AGAIN, whatever cancelled it: `run_job` returns a job in the `cancelled` state at once, after loading it and before any stop check, configuration, budget or provider is touched, with `error` beginning `job_cancelled:`, and does not persist it; `_cmd_job_run` refuses such a job with `job_not_resumable`, exit 1, beside the R-0913 refusal and before anything runs or is forwarded; and `decide_checkpoint_resume` refuses it after its all-green check and before its budget guard, `RESUME_REFUSED` with the reason `job_cancelled`, which `_cmd_job_resume` renders as `job_not_resumable` with exit 3 and which the loop's resume reports as not run. The `--dry-run` preview's `state` reads `cancelled` for such a job that is not all green, and its `would_run` is then false. (4) R-1150: the unit tests gain a refusal case with a stop by `max_cost_usd`, a current deadline later than the test's `now`, and the answers `max_cost_usd` raised and `deadline` later than `now` but earlier than the current deadline, refused as `budget_limit_not_raised`; and the round 12 case that used `abandon` as the refused option uses an option that is neither `extend` nor `abandon`.

ALTERNATIVES: Leaving the job `stopped` with the answer recorded, REJECTED: `stopped` means that the job keeps its pending work and resumes, the opposite of the answer. A new state `abandoned`, REJECTED: `cancelled` already exists, is terminal, and is the state `data_reclaim` frees. Refusing only a job whose budget answer was `abandon`, REJECTED: a cancelled job must not run whatever cancelled it. A new token `job_cancelled` for the command-line refusals, REJECTED: `job_not_resumable` is the spelling the command line already gives a job that cannot be continued, and an existing spelling wins (R-1023); `run_job`'s own `error` names the cause.

HOW TO REVERSE: Remove `abandon` from `answer_budget_decision` and its output in `_cmd_decision_resolve`; remove the cancelled-job refusals from `run_job`, `_cmd_job_run` and `decide_checkpoint_resume`, the `job_cancelled` branch of `_cmd_job_resume` and the preview's `cancelled` state; delete the tests the F295 R13 block names, and this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D13 — `remedy job resume` runs a job the ping-pong engine has run through `remedy job run`'s own handler, with the job's persisted builder, reviewer and limits; and under `--json` its progress line goes to stderr, so stdout carries one envelope (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: The second half of finding R-1147. Read at `c2b9a817f`: once its guards pass, `_cmd_job_resume` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py` hands every job to `_cmd_job_run_cycles`, whose single pass, `_cmd_run_next_task_local`, builds with `OllamaBuilder` whatever the job's record names, and whose multi-cycle path does the same. `run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`, which `_cmd_job_run` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` calls for `remedy job run`, resolves the builder and the reviewer from the job's persisted `execution_config` and runs from the first pending task; it writes that `execution_config` the first time it runs a job, and every job `remedy do` runs goes through it. The orchestrator loop's `execute_dispatched_job` in `packages/orchestration/orchestrator_loop.py` runs the jobs it dispatches through the cycle executor. `_cmd_job_resume` also prints its line `no checkpoint found — continuing from persisted job state`, or `resuming from checkpoint ...`, to stdout before handing off, whether or not `--json` was given, so a client reading stdout as one JSON envelope reads a line of prose first.

CHOSEN: (1) When the guards of `decide_checkpoint_resume` let a job through and it is not all green, `_cmd_job_resume` hands a job whose record carries an `execution_config` to `_cmd_job_run` with the job's full id and `json_output` and nothing else, so the job runs exactly as `remedy job run <job>` runs it — through the serve supervisor when one answers, otherwise through `run_job` — with its persisted roles and budgets, and the answer is that command's answer. A job without an `execution_config` keeps `_cmd_job_run_cycles`, unchanged. (2) `--cycles` and `--unattended` do not apply to such a job: when either is given, one line on stderr says so, and the run goes ahead, as the single pass's existing note on `--unattended` does. (3) Under `--json` the progress line goes to stderr; without `--json` it stays on stdout, byte for byte. (4) With this round, DECISIONs F295 D9, D11 and D12 and this one together answer R-1147: a job its budget stopped is held until its decision is answered, and a resumed job runs through its own providers.

ALTERNATIVES: Routing every job through `_cmd_job_run`, REJECTED: a job no ping-pong run ever touched has no persisted roles, and the cycle executor is the engine the orchestrator loop runs its dispatched jobs through. Giving `run_job` a resume mode of its own, REJECTED: `run_job` already continues from the first pending task, so `remedy job run` already is the resume of such a job. Refusing `--cycles` or `--unattended` for such a job, REJECTED: a client that always passes them would break on a job it cannot classify; the note says what happened.

HOW TO REVERSE: Remove the branch that hands a job with an `execution_config` to `_cmd_job_run` and its stderr note, return the progress line to stdout under `--json`, delete the tests the F295 R14 block names, and this paragraph.

## DECISION F295 D14 — a client reads a job's hunk ids and the hunk decision recorded for them with `remedy patch hunks <job> --json`, which answers what the cockpit's own two reads answer; every other kind of decision is already answered under `--json`, and T003 closes (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T003's last part, as DECISION F295 D8 (2) orders it. Read at `741ba4013`. Of the kinds of decision `list_decisions` in `packages/orchestration/decision_queue.py` raises, `remedy decision resolve <job> <decision> --reason <option> --json` answers the plan approval, with its bundled questions through `--answer`, a task decision, a proposal, a replan proposal a veto files, a stop reason and a budget decision (DECISIONs F295 D11 and D12). The patch approval names `remedy patch approve` and `remedy patch reject`, and both answer under `--json` (DECISION F283 D9). A test failure and a memory review are notices: the next action each names is a command that reads, and `decision resolve` refuses both as `decision_not_resolvable`, exit 1. The hunk decision of F033 is not in that list, because an operator decides over a diff when they choose to and no run raises it: `remedy patch approve-hunks <job> --json` records it through `record_hunk_decision_from_view` in `packages/orchestration/hunk_decision_record.py`, the function the cockpit's write door calls in `_dispatch_approve_hunks` in `packages/orchestration/ui_server.py`. The door's other answers go through the functions the command line calls as well: `consume_plan_approval` for the plan approval, `answer_task_decision` with its default source `human` for a task decision, and `answer_replan_proposal` for a replan proposal, whose actor names the door. What a program cannot do through the command line is READ the hunk ids it must answer with: no command shows a job's diff view, and `docs/guides/hunk-approval-user-guide-v1.md` sends its reader to the cockpit's diff viewer or to the cockpit's HTTP routes, which the feature file's Goal rules out for a machine client.

CHOSEN: (1) THE COMMAND. `remedy patch hunks <job> [--task-run <task-id>] [--json]`, the catalog entry `patch.hunks`, `read_only`, with `--json`; `--task-run` names a task run exactly as `remedy patch approve-hunks` takes it. Under `--json` it answers `job_id`, the job's full id; `view`, the envelope `build_diff_view` in `packages/orchestration/diff_view_source.py` builds for the job's evidence directory, resolved as `patch approve-hunks` resolves it, which is what the cockpit's `GET /api/jobs/<job>/diff` and its task-run twin answer; and `decision`, what `recorded_hunk_decision` reads for the attempt that view shows, keyed as `patch approve-hunks` keys the decision it records, which is what the cockpit's hunk-decisions routes answer: `attempt_key`, `decided_at` and one row per recorded hunk with `id`, `state` and `reason`, or an empty key, an empty time and no row when the view shows no attempt. (2) A diff that is not there is not a refusal: the view's `available` is false, its `reason` names why, and the command exits 0, as the cockpit answers such a view with 200. An unknown job is refused as every other `remedy patch` command refuses it. (3) Without `--json` it prints `Diff: <source> (<scope>)`, one line for a diff that is not available and one for a diff that is truncated, each file's path, one line per hunk with its id, its state — `pending` when nothing is recorded for it — and its header, and last `Decision: <attempt key>, recorded <time>` or `Decision: none recorded`. (4) It writes nothing. (5) `docs/guides/hunk-approval-user-guide-v1.md` names it first where hunk ids come from. (6) No answer of any kind of decision changes. T004's contract page lists which command answers each kind, and T003 closes with this round.

ALTERNATIVES: A hunk decision card in `list_decisions`, REJECTED: a hunk decision is the operator's choice over a diff and not a question a run raises, and a card for every diff would stand open on every job that has one. The hunk ids in `remedy patch show`, REJECTED: that command shows one patch intent, and a hunk belongs to a diff. One function that the command and the cockpit both call for the read, REJECTED for this round: the cockpit's read is a few lines over the same two public functions the command calls, and two tests compare the command's answer with the cockpit's own read over the same job, so the two cannot drift apart unseen. `remedy decision resolve` answering a patch approval as well, REJECTED: `remedy patch approve` and `remedy patch reject` already answer it under `--json`, and a second door for one answer is a second thing to keep equal.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `_cmd_show_hunks` and its `patch.hunks` handler from `apps/cli/commands/patch.py`; the `patch.hunks` entry and `_TASK_RUN_SHOW_OPT` from `apps/cli/command_catalog.py`; the class `TestTheHunksCommandIsTheReadSide` and the `DIFF_REASON_UNKNOWN_TASK_RUN` import from `tests/cli/test_patch_cmd.py`; `hunks` from the patch subcommands `tests/test_command_catalog.py` pins, with the count it pins lowered by one; the `patch.hunks` row from `_ARGV_TAIL` in `tests/cli/test_job_refusal_envelope.py`; the command line and the paragraph about it from `docs/guides/hunk-approval-user-guide-v1.md`; and this paragraph. The round's records in `.agent/` stay, because reversing a decision does not delete the record that it was made.

## DECISION F295 D15 — `remedy change proof` lists the job's applies through `remedy job apply` under `job_applies`, as their records state them and never as verified, and says so in its next action when the job has no patch intent (R-1152) (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: Finding R-1152. Read at `89ad24d76`: `build_proof_chain` in `packages/orchestration/proof_chain.py` builds each change from a patch intent and classifies it under the truth rule that a change is verified only with its approval, its apply, its proof and a linked test; a job that `remedy do` runs and `remedy job apply` lands creates no patch intent, so its proof reads no change and the next action "No changes to verify." `remedy job apply` writes one record per apply under `job_apply_records/<job>/<apply id>.json` in the data root, the answer `export_job_apply_json` in `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py` builds; `load_job_apply_record` reads one record and no command calls it, and `job_apply_landed` reads them for the digest's `waits_for_apply` (DECISION F295 D4). A record also carries `post_test_summary`, text a test command printed, which the proof's export may not repeat: `TestRedaction` in `tests/orchestration/test_proof_chain.py` keeps command output out of it. Read callers of `build_proof_chain`: `apps/cli/commands/change.py`, `packages/orchestration/file_provenance.py`, `packages/orchestration/mission_readiness.py`, `packages/orchestration/run_report.py`, `packages/orchestration/self_dogfood_execution.py` and `packages/orchestration/ui_server.py`; each reads the changes or the overall status, which this decision leaves as they are.

CHOSEN: (1) `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py` gains `JOB_APPLY_PROOF_FIELDS` — `job_apply_id`, `status`, `approved`, `dry_run`, `finished_at`, `files_applied`, `commit_sha`, `pushed` and `post_test_passed` — and `list_job_apply_records(job_id, data_dir=None)`, every record of the job reduced to those fields, ordered by `finished_at` and then by `job_apply_id`; a missing directory is no record, and a file that cannot be read, does not parse or is not an object is skipped, as `job_apply_landed` skips it; `data_dir` names the data root, a path or a string, and None reads the one the process resolves. (2) `ProofChain` gains `job_applies`, a tuple of those records, empty by default; `build_proof_chain` fills it from the `data_dir` it is given, keeping under `--path` only the records whose `files_applied` holds that path. (3) The changes, their classification and `overall_status` do not change: a job apply is listed and never called verified. (4) When the proof holds no change and at least one listed record reads `"status": "applied"`, the next action is the label "The job's apply is listed under job applies; it has no patch intent to verify.", no command, the reason "remedy job apply records no patch intent." and `available` true; otherwise it is what it was. (5) `export_proof_chain_json` adds the key `job_applies`, one object per record; the text answer adds, after the changes, `Job applies (<count>):` and one line per record, `  <apply id>: <status>, <count> file(s), finished <time>`. (6) T004's gate test reads the apply it approved in this list.

ALTERNATIVES: Classifying a job apply as a change under the truth rule, REJECTED: it has no patch intent to link an approval, a proof or a test to, so it could only ever read unverified or be called verified without its links, and the second is the overclaim the rule exists to prevent. A new command that reads apply records, REJECTED: the design and the feature file name `remedy change proof` as the client's last read, and a second read would leave that one answering "No changes to verify." for the same job. Repeating the whole record, REJECTED: it carries a test command's printed summary, which the proof's redaction keeps out.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `JOB_APPLY_PROOF_FIELDS` and `list_job_apply_records` from `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py`; the `job_applies` field, its filling, the replaced next action, its export key and its text lines from `packages/orchestration/proof_chain.py`; the class `TestTheProofListsTheJobsApplies` from `tests/cli/test_change_proof_cli.py`; and this paragraph. The round's records in `.agent/` stay.

## DECISION F295 D16 — T004 lands in two rounds: first the gate test, which reaches its one decision through a deadline that has already passed and fails on any read of stdin; then the contract page and the test that holds the page and the gate test to the same names (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F295 D1 gave T004 one round. Measured at `89ad24d76` with `.remedy-wt/f295-r17/probe.py` and `.remedy-wt/f295-r17/probe2.py` on scratch data roots with the fake providers. `remedy do <order file> --json --no-ui --yes --no-llm` completes its job and leaves no decision open, so the one decision the feature file's gate test answers needs a run that raises one. With `--deadline 2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00` the budget stops the job before any task runs, `remedy do` exits 1, and the digest lists the budget decision `budget:<request id>` beside a contract remainder decision; answered `extend` with a later deadline, `remedy job run <job> --json` completes the job, `remedy job apply <job> --approve --json` lands it, and since DECISION F295 D15 `remedy change proof <job> --json` lists that apply. With `--no-llm` the plan of tasks is deterministic and asks for no approval: `plan_order_job` in `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py` marks a plan pending only on the planner's own path. `tests/cli/in_process_cli.py` gives the command line an empty stdin, which a read answers with end of file instead of failing. SLOW MODE prefers the smaller round.

CHOSEN: (1) This round: `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py` holds one test that drives the path of the feature file's T004 through `apps.cli.grouped.main` in the test process, each command in a scratch git repository with the environment a child process would have and a scratch data root: an order file whose header carries `max-cost-usd: 1`; `remedy do <file> --json --no-ui --yes --no-llm` with the fake builder and reviewer and a deadline that has passed, exit 1; `remedy status --json`, whose digest names the mission with the file's path, its job stopped with its cost basis and its run manifest, and the open budget decision; `remedy decision resolve <job> <decision> --reason extend --answer deadline=<later> --json`, whose budgets keep the file's cap; `remedy job run <job> --json`, after which the job is completed and waits for its apply; `remedy job apply <job> --approve --json`, whose files exist in the repository; `remedy change proof <job> --json`, which lists that apply and calls nothing verified; and a last digest in which the job no longer waits. (2) The test's stdin fails the test on any read, so the whole path is proved to ask nothing on stdin. (3) The next round: `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md`, registered in `docs/README.md`, naming every command, flag, JSON key, exit code and file the gate test uses, in the order read, propose, approve, apply, with what Remedy never does on a machine order and `remedy job evidence <job>` as the step before `remedy patch hunks` for a job `remedy do` ran; and a test in the same file that fails when the page names a flag or key the gate test does not use, or the gate test uses one the page does not name.

ALTERNATIVES: Answering the contract remainder decision instead, REJECTED: answering it `no` moves nothing and `yes` starts a second mission, while the rest of the path depends on the budget decision's answer. Running each command as a child process, REJECTED: slower, and the round 9 tests already prove that a child reads end of file on a pipe nobody writes to; in the test process a read fails the test at once. Omitting `--yes` to raise a plan approval, REJECTED: the deterministic plan raises none, and the design keeps `--yes`. Landing the page and the gate test in one round, REJECTED under SLOW MODE: the page's test compares names with the gate test, which has to exist first.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py` and this paragraph; DECISION F295 D1's single T004 round then stands again.

## DECISION F295 D17 — the contract page `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md` holds the path's commands, flags, JSON keys and exit codes in four tables that a test keeps equal to what the gate test uses, read from the gate test's syntax tree; the rest of the page names what lies beside the path; T004 closes (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T004's second part, as DECISION F295 D16 (3) orders it. The feature file's Acceptance asks that the page name every command, flag, key, exit code and file the gate test uses, and that a test fail when the page names a flag or key the test does not use or the test uses one the page does not name. The page must also say which command answers each kind of decision (DECISION F295 D14), that a job `remedy do` ran needs `remedy job evidence` before `remedy patch hunks`, and what Remedy never does on a machine order — names the gate test does not use, so an equality over the whole page could not hold. Read at `c4878bd45`: `remedy do` answers a run that did not finish with `ok` false, `error` `step_failed`, `failed_step` and the whole answer beside it, exit 1, in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py`; an order file is refused with exit 2 as `order_file_not_found`, `order_file_unreadable`, `order_file_empty`, `order_file_invalid_header` or `order_file_no_cost_cap`; and `tests/docs/test_docs_consistency.py` refuses a page under `docs/system/` that `docs/README.md` does not link.

CHOSEN: (1) The page, registered in both lists of `docs/README.md`, carries the order file's format with the gate test's order file byte for byte, the path in four steps — propose, read, answer, approve and apply — and under its section "The path, step by step" four tables: Commands, Flags, JSON keys and Exit codes, each row's first cell one backticked name. (2) `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py` reads the gate test's own syntax tree — the test function and its two helpers `_remedy` and `_digest_job` — for the commands it runs, the flags it passes, the JSON keys it reads and the exit codes it compares, and fails for each kind when the page's table and that reading differ in either direction, or when the reading is empty; a second test fails when the page does not carry the gate test's order file byte for byte. (3) Outside that section the page names further commands and answers — the table of decision kinds and the commands that answer them, the hunk decision's three commands, the exit codes 2 and 3, and the four things Remedy never does on a machine order — which the equality does not bind. (4) `docs/system/proof-chain.md` gains the section "Job Applies", which repairs R-1153. (5) With this round T004 closes, and the feature's building rounds end; the SLOW MODE hardening stage follows.

ALTERNATIVES: Equality over every name on the page, REJECTED: the page must also name the commands beside the path, and Acceptance binds the names the gate test uses. Lists of names kept by hand in the test, REJECTED: a list beside the gate test drifts from what the gate test does; the syntax tree is what the test runs. A machine-readable block in the page instead of tables, REJECTED: the page is read by people first, and a table is both.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md` and its two rows in `docs/README.md`; delete from `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py` everything below its comment naming DECISION F295 D17, the module docstring's last paragraph, and the imports only that part uses (`ast`, `re`, `pytest`); delete the section "Job Applies" from `docs/system/proof-chain.md`; and delete this paragraph. The round's records in `.agent/` stay.
