## DECISION F295 D19 — an `extend` of a budget stop answers the contract remainder decision that stop raised with `no`, as the operator's own answer, and names it under `closed_decisions` (R-1155) (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: R-1155, measured at `d0ca96e49`: after a budget stop is answered `extend` and the job runs to its end, the digest still lists the remainder decision "[contract remainder] Mission <id> stopped at its budget ... Start a follow-up mission to meet them?". Read at `ed52f37fa`: `raise_contract_remainder_decision` in `packages/orchestration/mission_contract.py` enqueues at most one OPEN remainder decision per mission, on the first task of the mission's latest linked job, and raises a new one only while none is OPEN; `start_remainder_follow_up_mission` acts only on the answer `yes`; `answer_task_decision` in `packages/orchestration/escalation.py` answers an OPEN record once and records its `answer_source`, whose vocabulary is `human` and `default`, and the records know the two statuses `open` and `answered`; `_decision_answer_entries` in `packages/orchestration/ownership.py` attributes an answer whose source is not `default` to the operator; and the one caller of `answer_budget_decision` is the budget branch of `_cmd_decision_resolve` in `apps/cli/commands/decision.py`, because DECISION F295 D11 (6) leaves the cockpit's write door untouched.

CHOSEN: (1) `answer_contract_remainder_on_extend(job_id, budget_decision_id, *, root, now)` in `packages/orchestration/mission_contract.py` answers every OPEN remainder decision on the jobs of the mission the job belongs to, through `answer_task_decision` with its default source `human`, with the answer `no: <budget decision id> was answered extend, so the job runs on and no follow-up mission is started`; it saves each job it answered on and returns the answered ids in chain order. A job in no mission answers nothing, a linked job that cannot be read (`JobNotFoundError`, `JobStoreError`) is passed over, and every other decision stays as it is. (2) The budget branch calls it after an `extend` is saved, and never after `abandon`, which ends the job and leaves whether to start a follow-up mission exactly the open question. (3) The JSON answer of an `extend` carries `closed_decisions`, the answered ids; the text answer prints one line per id, `  Remainder decision <id> answered no: the job runs on instead of a follow-up mission`. (4) The gate test reads the remainder decision in the digest after the stop, requires `closed_decisions` to name it, and requires that after the run the digest lists no open decision for the job; the contract page names `closed_decisions` in its JSON keys table and says what an `extend` answers. (5) Tests: the class `TestAnExtendAnswersTheRemainder` in `tests/orchestration/test_mission_contract.py`, and `test_an_extend_answers_the_remainder_and_says_so_in_its_text` in `tests/cli/test_do_sequence_cli.py`.

ALTERNATIVES: A third status `withdrawn`, REJECTED: every reader of the two statuses, the late-answer refusals of both doors and the ownership attribution would have to learn it, for a question the operator's own choice already answers. An answer source naming Remedy itself, REJECTED: the operator answered `extend`, so the answer is the operator's. Hiding the decision from the digest while it stays open, REJECTED: `remedy decision list` and the cockpit's inbox would still ask it. Answering it when the job completes, REJECTED: a job extended and then stopped by another cause would keep a question whose premise, the budget stop, ended at the extend.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `answer_contract_remainder_on_extend` from `packages/orchestration/mission_contract.py`; in `apps/cli/commands/decision.py` delete its import, its call with the comment above it, the text loop over `closed` and `closed_decisions=closed,`; delete the tests named in (5); in `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py` delete the docstring's sentence on the remainder decision, the `remainder` reading and the `closed_decisions` assertion, and restore the `token_budget` filter after the run; delete the sentence on the remainder decision and the `closed_decisions` row from `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md`; and delete this paragraph. The round's records in `.agent/` stay.

## DECISION F295 D20 — the closure's one full suite is run again on the shipped tree, because another actor switched the checkout to main during the last 14 seconds of round 24's run; the new transcript replaces `.agent/authored/f295-closure-suite.txt` and records the HEAD reflog read before and after the run (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: Round 24 ran the feature's one full suite, `python3 -m pytest -n auto -q`, in the primary checkout from 08:09:58 to 08:15:32 on `72f160591`, exit 0, `21479 passed, 22 skipped, 1 warning in 330.49s (0:05:30)`. The HEAD reflog shows `checkout: moving from feature/f295-machine-client-contract-v1 to main` at 08:15:18 and `checkout: moving from main to feature/document-claude-abo-binding` at 08:15:20, neither issued by the session. For the run's last 14 seconds the working tree therefore held main's `9a8431ea9`, which lacks this branch's commits, and a test that started a subprocess or read a file in that span read main's bytes. Operator amendment amend0921-operator-feedback rule 1 says the one run belongs to the tree that is actually shipped and that a run whose tree moved is taken again on the right tree; it names an operator merge, an operator commit and a commit made outside the loop, and not a checkout switch.

CHOSEN: (1) Read in the spirit of that rule, round 25 runs the full suite once more, in the primary checkout, on the shipped tree. (2) Its transcript replaces `.agent/authored/f295-closure-suite.txt` at the same path; round 24's transcript stays in git history at `c465f8198`. (3) The transcript gains two lines, `reflog before:` and `reflog after:`, each the first line of `git reflog -n 1 --date=iso` read right before the run starts and right after it ends; the run counts only when the two lines are identical, which means HEAD did not move while it ran. (4) When they differ, the round commits the transcript as read and stops, and the next session asks the operator again before any further run. (5) Round 24's cost line stays in history; the cost script is run once more for the new run, so the transcript carries the cost of the run it reports.

ALTERNATIVES: Accepting round 24's run, REJECTED: its last 14 seconds did not run on the shipped tree, and a green word over partly foreign bytes is what the one-run rule exists to prevent. Running the suite in a separate worktree to escape another actor, REJECTED: DECISION F275 D48 found that a worktree lacks the cockpit's built files, and the integration gate is defined in the primary checkout. Waiting for the operator's answer to Q6 before running, REJECTED: operator amendment amend0917-throughput rule 5 says an operator question never stalls a round; the reflog check is what makes running safe without the answer.

HOW TO REVERSE: Restore `.agent/authored/f295-closure-suite.txt` from `c465f8198` and delete this paragraph; the round's records in `.agent/` stay.

## DECISION F295 D21 — at the Open PR Gate of F295's own pull request, the red node is registered on F295's branch before the one re-run, and the push of that registration is the re-run (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: The first hosted CI run of pull request 311, run 37584220637 on `988c57e1a`, failed one node on Python 3.12, registered as R-1159. Operator amendment amend0929-context-hygiene says the session registers every failing node in the first commit of the feature it is about to claim, and only then re-runs the workflow, at most once; re-running without registering is forbidden. The feature it is about to claim, F287, has no branch yet: the Open PR Gate of AGENTS.md forbids a new branch while that pull request is open and mergeable once green, and a branch cut from `main` now would fork the ledger that F295's round 28 rotated, before F295 is merged. Operator amendment amend0820-gate-autonomy explicitly allows commits on the open pull request's branch to work a red check. The two earlier cases, R-1107 at F042's claim and R-1128 at F292's claim, re-ran first and registered afterwards, each saying that it departed from the rule.

CHOSEN: (1) The registration of R-1159, the booking of round 28's verdict and this paragraph land in one commit on `feature/f295-machine-client-contract-v1`, with the handback in a commit after it, before any re-run. (2) The push of those commits starts a fresh hosted run of the pull request; that run is the one re-run, and no `gh run rerun` is issued as well. (3) A green fresh run lets the Open PR Gate merge the pull request; a red one is never merged, and the session writes an operator question and stops. (4) The two commits change only files under `.agent/`, so the product tree that the closure's one full suite and the evidence job ran on is unchanged; operator amendment amend0921-operator-feedback rule 1 names commits made outside the loop, and these are made inside it. (5) F287's first commit books nothing of this again.

ALTERNATIVES: Re-running first and registering at F287's claim, as R-1107 and R-1128 did, REJECTED: the amendment forbids that order by name. Cutting F287's branch from `main` before the merge to carry the registration, REJECTED: the Open PR Gate, and the ledger fork above. Issuing `gh run rerun --failed` after the push as well, REJECTED: that would be a second re-run.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph; the round's records in `.agent/` stay.

## DECISION F295 D22 — after the second red run of pull request 311, the session stops with operator question Q7, and the next session repairs R-1159 on F295's branch before one more hosted run (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: Hosted CI run 37588432368, the one re-run DECISION F295 D21 ordered, failed the same node as run 37584220637, in a second way (the recurrence of R-1159). ## DECISION F287 D1 — F287 runs in three slices: the `claude-cli` provider resumes, then the relaunch through `run_job` resumes on it, then every other provider says it did not; the hardening stage and closure follow (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: `docs/roadmap/features/T3_F287.md` lists T001 to T003. The claim's measurement, `.agent/f287_inventory.md`, read at `7c91c3b69`: every production provider answers `supports_resume` with false; `ClaudeCliProvider.build` and `.review` accept `resume` and never use it, and none of the five methods beneath them takes it; `build_claude_cli_args` has no resume parameter; the provider never sets `resume_used` or `resume_session_ref`; `run_pingpong` already offers a relaunched task's parked builder and reviewer sessions to round 1 (R-1055, DECISION F285 D2) and already falls back once, with `resume_fallback` recorded, when a resumed call errors (F106 T002c); the provider's working directory is the run's staging path; and `tests/orchestration/test_session_resume.py` pins `ClaudeCliProvider().supports_resume is False`.

CHOSEN: (1) T001 — `build_claude_cli_args` gains a resume parameter that adds the CLI's resume option with the session reference; `ClaudeCliProvider` threads `resume` from `build` and `review` through every call path beneath them (the JSON path, the streamed path and the structured reviewer path), answers `supports_resume` with true, and on a call that resumed sets `resume_used` true and `resume_session_ref` to the session it resumed. A refused resume comes back as an error output, so the loop's existing fallback-once rule takes over; T001 measures whether the loop's transport retry re-sends a refused resume before falling back, and stops it if so. The pin in `tests/orchestration/test_session_resume.py` changes with T001, in the same commit, and the change is named in the handback. Proofs run the provider with its command line replaced by a recorded stand-in at the `_guarded_cli_run` and streamed seams; no real `claude` process is started by any test. (2) T002 — a job parked or stopped mid-task and relaunched through `run_job` on `claude-cli`, with the same stand-in, records round 1's builder and reviewer `resume_used` true and `resume_session_ref` equal to the parked sessions. T002 first measures whether the relaunch runs the provider in the same working directory as the parked run, because the `claude` CLI keeps its sessions per working directory; if it does not, the slice states and repairs that before the end-to-end test is written. (3) T003 — `ClaudeProvider` and `OllamaPingPongProvider` keep `supports_resume` false, and when a relaunch offers them a session the run's evidence records that the offered session was not resumed and why, without failing the relaunch; the operator guide names which providers resume. (4) Then the hardening stage of operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap, then the closure sequence. Each slice is one or more reviewed rounds; none mixes with another.

ALTERNATIVES: Starting with the relaunch path, REJECTED: without a provider that resumes, its end-to-end proof could run through the test provider only, which is what F285 already proved. Giving `ClaudeProvider` (the API) a resume, REJECTED: the API has no server-side session to resume, and the feature asks only that such a provider says so. Calling the real `claude` CLI in a test, REJECTED: tests never spend the operator's subscription; the closure's self-use run is where a real resume is observed.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph and the feature file's slice order section; the slices are then re-planned at the next round.

## DECISION F287 D2 — T001 is two rounds: round 2 threads a validated session reference through every `claude-cli` call path while `supports_resume` stays false; round 3 makes a refused resume fall back without transport retries and turns `supports_resume` on (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F287 D1 (1) orders T001 and asks it to measure whether the loop's transport retry re-sends a refused resume. Measured by reading `_call_with_retry` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_loop.py` at `0dfa2fd36`: a failed call whose error text contains `exited` counts as a non-zero exit, `should_retry` retries it, and only after `MAX_RETRIES` does the output reach the fallback-once branch; `ClaudeCliProvider` reports a non-zero child as `provider_error: _CliNonZeroExit: claude CLI exited <n>: ...`. So a refused resume would be sent again on every retry before the fallback. Separately, the session reference a relaunch offers is read back from run records on disk and would be placed into the child's argument list.

CHOSEN: (1) Round 2: `build_claude_cli_args` gains the keyword `resume_session: str = ""`; when it is non-empty it must fully match `_CLI_SESSION_REF_PATTERN`, `[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z_-]{0,127}`, or the function raises `ValueError`, and otherwise `--resume <ref>` is appended after the `--json-schema` pair and before the write-mode arguments. `ClaudeCliProvider` threads `resume` from `build` and `review` through `_build_impl`, `_review_impl`, `_call`, `_call_streamed` and `_call_reviewer_structured`; an output with an empty `error` from a call given a non-empty `resume` carries `resume_used` true and `resume_session_ref` equal to it, and every other output keeps the defaults. `prepare_call_input`'s options gain the key `resume` only when a resume is given, so a fresh call's fingerprint is byte-identical to today's. `supports_resume` stays false in this round, so no production call passes a resume yet. (2) Round 3: a failed call that was given a resume returns an error beginning `resume_refused:` whose text the retry predicates do not classify as a timeout or a non-zero exit, so the fallback-once branch is reached on the first failure; `supports_resume` turns true; and the pin in `tests/orchestration/test_session_resume.py` changes in the same commit.

ALTERNATIVES: One round for all of T001, REJECTED under SLOW MODE: the argument threading and the retry interplay are two separately provable changes. Skipping the reference check, REJECTED: a record edited to hold `--dangerously-skip-permissions` would otherwise reach the child's argument list. Passing the reference as `--resume=<ref>`, REJECTED: the shape check already rules out a leading dash, and the separate-argument form matches how every other option is passed here.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph; round 3 then re-plans the remainder of T001.

## DECISION F287 D3 — a failed `claude-cli` call that was given a resume answers `resume_refused:` and is never transport-retried; turning `supports_resume` on moves to its own round (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F287 D2 (2) planned round 3 as T001's second half; round 3 became the repair of R-1161, so that half is round 4's. Turning `supports_resume` on for `claude-cli` does more than the relaunch hand-over: in `run_pingpong` it also switches on F106's repair-round resume and F109's prompt dedupe for resumed rounds, which have never run against a provider that resumes. Measured at `c45db0ce5` by reading `_call_with_retry` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_loop.py`: a builder output whose error text holds `exited` or `nonzero` is retried, after a 30 and a 120 second wait; a reviewer output is never retried unless its error begins `provider_error:`; and `ClaudeCliProvider` reports a non-zero child as `provider_error: _CliNonZeroExit: claude CLI exited <n>: ...`.

CHOSEN: (1) Round 4 sorts the import block of `tests/orchestration/test_claude_cli_resume.py` (round 3's red gate), in a commit of its own. (2) In `ClaudeCliProvider._build_impl` and `._review_impl`, the existing `except Exception` branch returns, when the call was given a non-empty `resume`, the error `_resume_refused_error(exc, resume)` instead of `provider_error: ...`; every other field of that output, the exit code and the standard error tail included, is filled exactly as before. `_resume_refused_error` is a module function: for a `ValueError` it returns `resume_refused: <the exception's message>`, and otherwise `resume_refused: the claude CLI did not continue session <ref>`. Its text never carries the exception's class name or message for any other exception, so `is_timeout_error`, `is_nonzero_exit_error` and `is_rate_limit_error` all answer false, `_call_with_retry` returns it at once, and the loop's fallback-once branch runs on the first failure. A call given no resume keeps its `provider_error:` text unchanged. (3) `supports_resume` stays false in round 4. Round 5 turns it on, together with the pin in `tests/orchestration/test_session_resume.py`, a proof through `run_pingpong` with the CLI replaced by a stand-in, and its own DECISION on F106's and F109's behaviour going live.

ALTERNATIVES: Keeping the exception's message in the error, REJECTED: it carries `claude CLI exited <n>` and the child's standard error, and either can match a retry predicate. Teaching `_call_with_retry` about resumes, REJECTED: the fallback-once rule and the retry path are not this feature's to change, and the provider already knows whether it was asked to resume. Turning `supports_resume` on in this round, REJECTED under SLOW MODE: it switches on two dormant mechanisms as well, which deserve a round and a decision of their own.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph; a failed resumed call then reports `provider_error:` again and is retried before the fallback.

## DECISION F287 D4 — `claude-cli` answers `supports_resume` with true, so F106's repair-round resume and F109's resumed-prompt dedupe go live for it beside the relaunch hand-over (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: After rounds 2 and 4, `ClaudeCliProvider` carries a checked session reference on every call path, records `resume_used` only on a call that succeeded, and answers a failed resumed call with `resume_refused:` so the loop's fallback-once branch runs at once (DECISIONS F287 D2 and D3). `run_pingpong` reads `supports_resume` at three places: a repair round's builder call resumes the session the previous round reported (F106 T002a), the reviewer's primary call does the same (F106 T002b-i), and a relaunched task's first calls resume the parked sessions (R-1055, DECISION F285 D2). When a repair round resumes, the builder's prompt carries only the changed regions of the repair diff (F106 T002b-ii) and drops the segments the resumed session provably already received (F109), unless the run's semantic-dedupe switch is off. No production provider has resumed until now, so none of this has run outside the test provider. The feature file's "Do not touch" list keeps "the prompt, which stays at full context on a resumed call"; the loop's own comment at the R-1055 hand-over states that the relaunch call keeps the full context, because the repair-round reference stays the prompt gate.

CHOSEN: (1) `ClaudeCliProvider.supports_resume` answers true. (2) The consequences are accepted as the designed behaviour of F106 and F109, which were built and reviewed for exactly this provider: on `claude-cli`, a repair round's builder and reviewer calls continue the previous round's sessions, and the builder's repair prompt shrinks as F106 and F109 define; a refused resume falls back once to a fresh session at full context; a relaunch's first calls continue the parked sessions at full context. (3) The feature file's "Do not touch" line is read as the relaunch call's prompt, which round 5 does not change. (4) The pin `assert ClaudeCliProvider().supports_resume is False` in `tests/orchestration/test_session_resume.py`, its module docstring's sentence that every concrete provider reads false, and round 2's `TestSupportsResumeStaysFalse` change in the same commit as (1). (5) The proof runs `run_pingpong` with `ClaudeCliProvider` instances whose child is replaced by a stand-in at `_guarded_cli_run`: round 2's builder and reviewer calls carry `--resume` with the session round 1 reported and record `resume_used` true; and when the stand-in refuses round 2's resumed builder call, the builder phase sends exactly two calls, the refused one and one fresh one without `--resume`, and round 2's builder output records `resume_fallback` true. (6) Operator question Q8 records this as a reversible ruling (operator amendment amend0911-feedback rule C, kind B).

ALTERNATIVES: Letting `claude-cli` resume only at a relaunch and never in a repair round, REJECTED: it needs a second capability flag in `run_pingpong`, which this feature's "Do not touch" list keeps closed, and it gives up the token saving F106 and F109 were built for, against the operator's first priority. Keeping `supports_resume` false until the operator answers, REJECTED: operator amendment amend0917-throughput rule 5 says a question never stalls a round.

HOW TO REVERSE: Set `supports_resume` back to false and restore the two pins; this also stops the relaunch hand-over from resuming on `claude-cli`, so keeping the relaunch while dropping the repair rounds needs the capability split rejected above.

## DECISION F287 D5 — T002 needs no production change: a relaunch in the job's worktree runs `claude-cli` in the parked run's directory and resumes the parked session; a relaunch in copy mode runs in a new directory, the CLI refuses the resume, and the run falls back once (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F287 D1 (2) orders T002 to measure, before writing its end-to-end test, whether a relaunch runs the provider in the working directory the `claude` CLI keeps the parked session under. Measured by the planner and reviewer at `9213a3c76`, in disposable worktrees under `.remedy-wt/`, with `run_job` building the `claude-cli` providers itself and the child replaced at `_guarded_cli_run`, recording every call's working directory and `--resume` value: on a target that is a git repository, the job runs in its own worktree `<target>/.remedy-wt/job-<id>`, and a job paused or stopped during task 1's first builder call is relaunched in that same directory, its first builder call carrying `--resume` with the parked session, and the run record reading `resume_used` true and `resume_session_ref` equal to it (`probe_cwd_git.py`, and `probe_cwd_stop_model.py` for the stop); on a target that is not a git repository, each run gets its own `/tmp/remedy-pingpong-<run id>`, so the relaunch runs in a different directory (`probe_cwd.py`). The `claude` CLI looks a session up under the directory it runs in, so in copy mode the resume is refused; DECISION F287 D3 then falls back once, at full context, with no transport retry. The measurement also found R-1162, which is not this feature's to repair.

CHOSEN: (1) No production change in T002. (2) Copy mode keeps offering the parked session: the refused call costs one short child process and no tokens, the evidence records `resume_fallback` true, and skipping the offer would need the parked run's directory in the run record, which the "Do not touch" list keeps closed. (3) T002's proof is a stand-in that behaves as the CLI does: it remembers the directory each session was created in and refuses a `--resume` from any other directory. With it, three tests run `run_job` on `claude-cli` with a model configured: a job paused during task 1's builder call, and a job stopped there, are relaunched on a git target and complete, the relaunch's first builder call runs in the parked call's directory and carries the parked session, and the run record reads `resume_used` true with that session; and the same pause on a target that is not a git repository relaunches, the resume is refused, the round records `resume_fallback` true, and the job completes. (4) The operator guide's paragraph on which providers resume, T003's, states the copy-mode limit.

ALTERNATIVES: Recording the parked run's directory and skipping the offer when it differs, REJECTED for now: it touches the relaunch hand-over F285 built, for a saving of one short failed process. Proving T002 with a stand-in that never refuses, REJECTED: it would hide the copy-mode limit the measurement found.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph; T002 is then re-planned.

## DECISION F287 D7 — T003: a relaunch that offers a parked session to a provider that cannot resume names the role and the reason in the run record under `resume_declined`, and the operator guide names which providers resume (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F287 D1 (3) orders T003: `ClaudeProvider` and `OllamaPingPongProvider` keep `supports_resume` false, and when a relaunch offers them a session the run's evidence records that the offered session was not resumed and why, without failing the relaunch. Read at `476d86449`: `run_pingpong` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_loop.py` passes a relaunch's parked session to round 1's call of a role only when that role's provider answers `supports_resume` true, and otherwise drops the offer without a trace, so the record shows `resumed_from_run_id` naming the parked run and `resume_used` false with no reason; such an offer reaches the Anthropic API or the Ollama provider, for example, when a job parked on `claude-cli` is relaunched on one of them; `export_pingpong_json` writes the run record `result.json`; and `docs/system/session-resume-v1.md` still says that no adapter resumes in production.

CHOSEN: (1) `PingPongResult` gains `resume_declined: dict[str, str]`, empty by default, mapping a role to the reason its offered parked session was not resumed. (2) A module function `resume_declined_reasons(resume_sessions, *, builder, reviewer)` in `pingpong_loop.py` returns, for each of the roles `builder` and `reviewer` that `resume_sessions` offers a non-empty session and whose provider does not answer `supports_resume` true, the provider's `resume_unsupported_reason` when it has a non-empty one, and otherwise `the <provider name> provider cannot resume a session`. `run_pingpong` sets `result.resume_declined` from it once, right after both providers are resolved, and changes nothing else: no call, prompt, retry or fallback differs. (3) `export_pingpong_json` writes `"resume_declined"` beside `"resumed_from_run_id"`, an empty object for every run that was offered nothing. (4) `ClaudeProvider` and `OllamaPingPongProvider` each gain a read-only property `resume_unsupported_reason`, beside `supports_resume`: `the Anthropic API keeps no conversation between calls` and `an Ollama chat call keeps no conversation between calls`. The `PingPongProvider` protocol is unchanged; the loop reads the property with `getattr`. (5) `docs/system/session-resume-v1.md` is brought to the built state: `claude-cli` resumes in repair rounds and at a relaunch, a refused resume falls back once, a relaunch in copy mode always falls back because the CLI keeps a session under the directory it ran in (DECISION F287 D5 (4)), and the two other production providers never resume and are named under `resume_declined`.

ALTERNATIVES: A per-round key on each role's block, REJECTED: a reviewer parse retry replaces the reviewer's output after the call, so a key set on the output can be lost, and the offer is a fact of the run, made once. Adding the reason to the `PingPongProvider` protocol, REJECTED: every provider and test double would have to grow it, for a value only two classes need. Failing or warning the relaunch, REJECTED: the feature's Acceptance says such a provider never fails the relaunch.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the field, the function, the export key and the two properties; the loop then drops an unusable offer silently again, as it did before T003.

## DECISION F116 D1 — F116 runs in three slices: a pure burn detector, then the job runner acts on its trips at the safe point, then the watchdog's burn tripwire becomes its caller; the hardening stage and closure follow (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: `docs/roadmap/features/T3_F116.md` lists T001 to T003. The claim's measurement, `.agent/f116_inventory.md`, read at `e80b95467`: the watchdog's `evaluate_burn_anomaly` is the only burn check in the product; it compares the mean of the last `window` measured iterations of a mission's ledger against the mean of the earlier ones, in tokens, reads no clock and no timestamp, is inert below `min_samples + window` measured entries, and is called once, by `evaluate_ledger`; `tests/orchestration/test_watchdog.py` names it or its trip kind on 20 lines that are not a `def` line. The job runner evaluates every budget at one safe point, `_stop_check` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`, through `safe_points.should_stop`, which reads the operator stop before the budget. The F103 ledger's per-call rows of one task run all carry that task run's single timestamp, and a provider attempt records no time of its own. No module defines an expectation band, because F074 is not built. The notion of an unattended run exists on `remedy job resume --unattended` (the cycle loop in `long_run_executor.py`) and in the mission loop, and not in `pingpong_job.py`. Neither `packages/orchestration/burn_detector.py` nor `tests/orchestration/test_burn_detector.py` exists.

CHOSEN: (1) T001 — `packages/orchestration/burn_detector.py` holds the one definition of "expected spend": a pure function over a list of spend samples that returns the rate, the expectation, its basis label (`class_default` from configuration while F074's bands do not exist, or `trailing_baseline` from the run's own earlier samples), the multiplier and whether it tripped, with a minimum-spend floor below which nothing trips and a window that spans at least one whole task run. Its trailing-baseline basis must be able to express the watchdog's present contract exactly — window, minimum samples, multiplier, unmeasured samples contributing nothing — so that T003 can delete the watchdog's private arithmetic without changing a verdict. Table tests in `tests/orchestration/test_burn_detector.py`: a spike trips with the right numbers, steady expensive work does not, tiny spend never does. T001 fixes the sample shape, the units and the configuration keys in a DECISION that lands in the same round as the patch (operator amendment amend0917-throughput rule 3). (2) T002 — the job runner calls the detector at its existing safe point, never from a thread. Attended, a trip is a warning in what `remedy job show` prints and in the job's report, plus one run-log event; unattended, it is additionally a pause decision that carries the arithmetic (window, rate, expectation, basis) and the options resume and abandon, one open trip decision per job whose evidence a re-trip updates. T002 first measures two things and decides each in a DECISION with its patch: which job runs count as unattended, given that `pingpong_job.py` has no such notion today, and whether the samples come from the job's F103 ledger rows, which exist only when the job's repository resolves to a registered project, or from the run's own per-task tally. The optional throttle of parallel width is built only if T002's measurement finds a width to throttle. (3) T003 — the watchdog's burn tripwire calls the detector and `evaluate_burn_anomaly`'s own arithmetic is DELETED, not wrapped (the feature file's Orchestrator brief); `tests/orchestration/test_watchdog.py` stays green; `docs/system/autonomy-watchdog-v1.md` and the operator documentation say where the one definition lives. (4) Then the hardening stage of operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap, then the closure sequence. Each slice is one or more reviewed rounds; none mixes with another.

ALTERNATIVES: Unifying the watchdog first, REJECTED: there is nothing to unify into until the detector exists. A background thread that samples spend, REJECTED by the feature file: the check runs at the cadence of the other run-level checks. Inventing class expectation bands now, REJECTED: they are F074's, and configuration defaults stand in until then, as the feature file says. Touching notification channels, budget limits or calibration, REJECTED: the feature file's Do-not-touch list.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph and the feature file's slice order section; the slices are then re-planned at the next round.

## DECISION F116 D2 — T001: `burn_detector.evaluate_burn_rate` is a pure function over spend samples with two bases, `trailing_baseline` per sample and `class_default` per hour; the trailing basis reproduces the watchdog's tripwire exactly, and its configuration keys land with their reader in T002 (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F116 D1 (1) gives T001 the one definition of "expected spend" and requires its trailing-baseline basis to express the watchdog's present contract exactly. `.agent/f116_inventory.md` measured that contract at `e80b95467`: `evaluate_burn_anomaly` keeps the measured entries in ledger order, skips an unmeasured one without shrinking the window, returns nothing while fewer than `min_samples + window` are measured, and trips when the mean of the last `window` exceeds `multiplier` times the mean of the earlier ones. It also measured that the F103 ledger gives every call of one task run the same timestamp, so a per-hour rate can be read only across whole task runs.

CHOSEN: (1) A new module `packages/orchestration/burn_detector.py`, importing only the standard library, reading no clock, no file and no configuration. Public names: `BASIS_CLASS_DEFAULT = "class_default"`, `BASIS_TRAILING_BASELINE = "trailing_baseline"`, `RATE_UNIT_PER_SAMPLE = "per_sample"`, `RATE_UNIT_PER_HOUR = "per_hour"`; the frozen dataclasses `BurnSample(amount: float | None, at: datetime | None = None, label: int = 0)`, `BurnThresholds(window: int = 3, min_samples: int = 5, multiplier: float = 3.0, min_spend: float = 0.0, expected_per_hour: float | None = None)` and `BurnReading(tripped, basis, rate_unit, rate, expectation, multiplier, window_samples, baseline_samples, window_spend, since_label)` with `to_json()` returning exactly those ten keys; and `evaluate_burn_rate(samples, thresholds) -> BurnReading | None`. A sample's `amount` is its spend in whatever unit the caller measures, `at` is when that spend was recorded, and `label` is an attribution carried into the reading and never used as an index. (2) A sample is MEASURED when its `amount` is an `int` or a `float`, not a `bool`, finite and not negative; every other sample is skipped and does not shrink the window. `window < 1` returns None. (3) When `expected_per_hour` is None the basis is `trailing_baseline`, rate unit `per_sample`: None while fewer than `min_samples + window` samples are measured or while the baseline would be empty; otherwise `recent` is the last `window` measured samples, `baseline` the measured ones before them, `rate` the mean of `recent`, `expectation` the mean of `baseline`, `baseline_samples` the length of `baseline`. (4) When `expected_per_hour` is set the basis is `class_default`, rate unit `per_hour`: None while fewer than `window + 1` samples are measured; `recent` is the last `window` measured samples and the ANCHOR the measured sample just before them; None unless the anchor and every sample of `recent` carry a timezone-aware `at`; the span is `recent[-1].at - anchor.at` in hours, None unless it is positive; `rate` is the sum of `recent` divided by the span, `expectation` is `expected_per_hour`, `baseline_samples` is 0, and `min_samples` is not used. (5) In both bases `window_spend` is the sum of `recent`, `since_label` is the label of `recent[0]`, `window_samples` is the length of `recent`, and the reading TRIPS when `window_spend > min_spend` and `rate > multiplier * expectation`; a reading that does not trip is still returned, so a caller can show the numbers. (6) Tests in `tests/orchestration/test_burn_detector.py` cover a spike that trips with its arithmetic, steady expensive work that does not, tiny spend below the floor that does not while the same samples trip with no floor, thin data, unmeasured samples, the per-hour basis tripping and not tripping and its inert cases, the ten JSON keys, the absence of any clock read, and a table of ledgers on which the trailing basis and the watchdog's `evaluate_burn_anomaly` agree on whether they trip and on every number. (7) `tests/test_no_orphan_modules.py` lists the module in `ALLOWED_UNWIRED` with the reason "F116 T001's burn detector; T002 wires it into the job runner's safe point (DECISION F116 D2)", and that guard itself reds once T002 imports the module and the entry is still there, so T002 must delete it. (8) The configuration keys for the multiplier, the floor and the per-hour expectation land in T002 with the code that reads them, not here (operator amendment amend0917-throughput rule 3); this amends the sentence of DECISION F116 D1 (1) that put them in T001.

ALTERNATIVES: Making the trailing basis per hour as well, REJECTED: the watchdog's tests read iterations without timestamps, and its contract is per iteration, so a per-hour trailing basis would change its verdicts. Returning None when the reading does not trip, as the watchdog does, REJECTED: T002 has to show the numbers of an attended run that did not trip. Treating a negative or non-finite amount as a measurement, REJECTED: it would drag a baseline or a rate to a value no provider reported. Reading configuration inside the detector, REJECTED: the watchdog already resolves its thresholds once at the edge and hands them down, and the detector follows that shape.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `packages/orchestration/burn_detector.py`, `tests/orchestration/test_burn_detector.py` and the `ALLOWED_UNWIRED` entry.

## DECISION F116 D3 — T002, first part: a job's burn is measured in tokens per provider call by a `JobBurnMonitor` in `packages/orchestration/job_burn.py`, configured by five `job_burn.*` keys; wiring it into `run_job` is the next round (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F116 D1 (2) leaves two measurements to T002: where a job's samples come from and which job runs count as unattended. The reviewer measured the first at `21cdd3537`. `run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` already tallies every counted provider call in its `_on_provider_call` hook, adding the call's `input_tokens` plus `output_tokens` to `_accumulated_tokens`, and every run-level check reads that tally at `_stop_check`; the F103 ledger is written for a job only when its repository resolves to a registered project, and it gives all calls of one task run one timestamp. A provider call reports tokens wherever it reports usage, and a cost only where the provider reports one. The second measurement, which runs are unattended, belongs to the round that adds the pause and is not decided here.

CHOSEN: (1) A job's samples come from the run's own per-call tally, not from the ledger: one sample per counted provider call, its amount that call's `input_tokens` plus `output_tokens`, the same sum `_accumulated_tokens` adds, so the alarm and the token budget read one basis. Its unit is tokens; a reading of a job is recorded with `"unit": "tokens"` beside the detector's ten keys. Cost in dollars is not the alarm's unit, because a call reports tokens far more often than it reports a price, and an alarm that falls silent on every unpriced call protects nothing on those runs. (2) A new module `packages/orchestration/job_burn.py` holds what the job runner needs and nothing else: `JOB_BURN_UNIT = "tokens"`; `job_burn_thresholds_from_config(config=None) -> BurnThresholds`, which reads the five keys below through `get_config()` imported inside the function when no config is given, and maps a key that reads None to the `BurnThresholds` default; `job_burn_record(reading) -> dict`, the reading's `to_json()` plus `"unit": JOB_BURN_UNIT`; and the class `JobBurnMonitor(thresholds)`, whose `record_call(usage_actuals, *, at)` appends one `BurnSample` labelled with the call's 1-based position among the calls it has recorded, and whose `reading()` returns `evaluate_burn_rate` over every sample recorded so far. `record_call` reads no clock; its caller passes `at`. A call is unmeasured, amount None, when `usage_actuals` is not a dict or when `input_tokens` or `output_tokens` is present and is not an `int`, or is a `bool`; a missing one counts 0. (3) Five keys in `packages/orchestration/config.py`, after the `watchdog.burn_*` keys: `job_burn.window` (`REMEDY_JOB_BURN_WINDOW`, whole number, 3), `job_burn.min_samples` (`REMEDY_JOB_BURN_MIN_SAMPLES`, whole number, 5), `job_burn.multiplier` (`REMEDY_JOB_BURN_MULTIPLIER`, number, 3.0), `job_burn.min_spend_tokens` (`REMEDY_JOB_BURN_MIN_SPEND_TOKENS`, whole number, 20000) and `job_burn.expected_tokens_per_hour` (`REMEDY_JOB_BURN_EXPECTED_TOKENS_PER_HOUR`, number, no default). With no hourly expectation set, the basis is the run's own trailing baseline, which is what the feature file asks for until F074 supplies class bands; the floor of 20000 tokens across a window of three calls is what keeps tiny runs from ever tripping. `docs/guides/environment.md` is regenerated from the registry in the same commit. (4) `burn_detector.py` gains its first production importer, so its `ALLOWED_UNWIRED` entry in `tests/test_no_orphan_modules.py` is deleted, and `job_burn.py` takes one with the reason "F116 T002's job burn monitor; the next round wires it into run_job's safe point (DECISION F116 D3)". (5) The next round wires the monitor into `run_job`: `_on_provider_call` records each counted call with the time it ran, `_stop_check` evaluates once no stop fired, a tripped reading is persisted on the job and shown by `remedy job budget`, and that round deletes the `job_burn.py` entry.

ALTERNATIVES: Reading samples from the F103 ledger, REJECTED: it is written only for registered projects and cannot place two calls of one task run apart in time. Measuring dollars, REJECTED for the reason in (1); a later feature may add a dollar reading beside the token one. Reusing the `watchdog.burn_*` keys for jobs, REJECTED: a mission iteration and a provider call differ in size by an order of magnitude, so one multiplier and one floor cannot fit both, while the definition of "expected" stays the one function both callers share. Putting the monitor inside `pingpong_job.py`, REJECTED: that module is over 5000 lines, and a monitor with its own tests is easier to prove in its own file.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `packages/orchestration/job_burn.py`, its tests and the five keys, regenerate `docs/guides/environment.md`, and restore the `burn_detector.py` entry in `ALLOWED_UNWIRED`.

## DECISION F116 D4 — T002, wiring: `run_job` records every counted provider call in a `JobBurnMonitor`, reads it at every safe point where no stop fired, keeps the newest trip on the job as `burn_reading`, and `remedy job budget` shows it (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F116 D3 (5) orders the monitor wired into `run_job` in this round. The reviewer read `run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` at `901526c7e`: `_on_provider_call` returns early for an attempt whose provider is named `fake` and otherwise counts the call into `_accumulated_provider_calls`; `_stop_check` runs the operator stop and the reactive budget first and, when neither fires, the predictive check and then the pause read; it is called before the first task, before each task, before every provider call and transport retry through the loop's `stop_check`, and after each applied task. `JobPlan` already persists one computed record of this kind, `budget_prediction`, through `_export_job` and the loader, and `remedy job budget` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py` shows it as `recorded_prediction`. A configuration value Remedy cannot parse raises `ValueError` from the resolver, measured with `REMEDY_JOB_BURN_WINDOW=abc`; reading a configuration file from disk can also raise `OSError`, which was not measured.

CHOSEN: (1) `run_job` builds ONE `JobBurnMonitor` per run, from `job_burn_thresholds_from_config()`, directly after the predictive configuration is resolved. When building it raises `ValueError` or `OSError`, the run logs one error with the traceback, keeps no monitor, and continues: an alarm that cannot be configured must never stop a healthy job. (2) `_on_provider_call` records every call it COUNTS — after the `fake` early return, exactly where `_accumulated_provider_calls` grows — with that call's `usage_actuals` and `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` as `at`. The test provider named `fake` is therefore never sampled, as it is never counted by the budget. (3) `_stop_check`, in the branch where neither the operator stop nor the reactive budget fired, first takes the monitor's reading. When the reading trips and its record, `job_burn_record(reading)`, differs from `job.burn_reading`, it sets `job.burn_reading` to that record and persists the job with `_persist_job`; a reading that does not trip changes nothing, so the newest trip of the job stays on it as evidence. This round only records the trip; it stops nothing and pauses nothing. (4) `JobPlan` gains `burn_reading: dict | None = None`, written by `_export_job` directly after `budget_prediction` and loaded as `data.get("burn_reading")`. (5) `remedy job budget <job_id>` shows it whatever limits the job has: `--json` adds the key `burn_reading`, the persisted record or null; the text output, when a record exists, prints `  recorded burn alarm:` and below it the lines `    rate:` and `    window:` that name the rate with its unit and whether it is per call or per hour, the expectation and its basis, the window's calls, the call it starts at, the tokens it spent and the multiplier. `docs/system/job-budget-enforcement-v0.md` says what the command now shows, and its "Deliberately not built" section no longer says that burn-rate anomaly detection exists nowhere in the code. The tests read the registry through the resolver: the five keys' registered defaults handed to `job_burn_thresholds_from_config` give window 3, minimum 5, multiplier 3.0, floor 20000.0 and no hourly expectation. (6) This amends DECISION F116 D3 (2): a key that reads None maps to the registered default of that key, which for the floor is 20000 tokens, and not to the `BurnThresholds` default of 0. (7) `job_burn.py` now has a production importer, so its `ALLOWED_UNWIRED` entry in `tests/test_no_orphan_modules.py` is deleted, and the two modules join `tests/orchestration/import_reachability_allowlist.txt` because `run_job` reaches them; its module docstring and the comments that say nothing calls it yet are corrected.

ALTERNATIVES: Evaluating only at the after-task safe point, REJECTED: a single task can spend for hours, and the loop already calls `_stop_check` before every provider call, which is the cadence the feature file names. Persisting the samples so a relaunch keeps its baseline, REJECTED for now: the monitor's samples are the run's own, like `_accumulated_tokens` before the record that persists it, and a relaunch that starts a new baseline judges only what it has measured itself. Writing the reading on every safe point, REJECTED: a write per provider call to record that nothing happened costs disk and says nothing a person needs.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the monitor and its two calls in `run_job`, the `burn_reading` field and its two wire lines, the `burn_reading` output of `remedy job budget` and its documentation, and restore the `job_burn.py` entry in `ALLOWED_UNWIRED`.

## DECISION F116 D5 — T002, unattended: a job whose plan was approved unattended is paused at the safe point that reads a new trip, with one `[burn_alarm]` decision carrying the arithmetic and the options resume and abandon; an attended job keeps running (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F116 D1 (2) leaves T002 to decide which job runs count as unattended. The reviewer measured it at `8effa367a`. `run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` has no notion of an unattended run. A job's plan approval is audited: `job_plan.auto_approve_task_plan` writes `_approval_audit` with `mode` equal to `AUTO_APPROVAL_MODE`, `"auto_yes"`, and its callers are `remedy do run --yes` in `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py`, which then calls `run_job`, and the mission loop in `packages/orchestration/orchestrator_loop.py`, whose dispatched jobs run through the cycle executor rather than `run_job` and are watched by the mission watchdog. A job pause already exists for `run_job`: `pause_control.request_pause` writes a request that the pause read at the end of `_stop_check` turns into a park before the next provider call, and `remedy job unpause` releases it. The mission watchdog's own trip action, `act_on_trips` in `packages/orchestration/watchdog.py`, is the precedent: it pauses the mission and raises one decision per trip class, deduplicated by a marker at the start of its question, with an empty safe default so that no unattended automation can answer it. `escalation.open_task_decisions` returns the stored records themselves, so a record it returns can be updated in place.

CHOSEN: (1) A job run counts as UNATTENDED when its `task_plan` is a dict whose `_approval_audit` is a dict whose `mode` equals `job_plan.AUTO_APPROVAL_MODE`; every other job run is attended. `job_burn.py` gains `job_approved_unattended(job) -> bool`, importing `AUTO_APPROVAL_MODE` inside the function so the module stays light. (2) `job_burn.py` gains `BURN_DECISION_MARKER = "[burn_alarm]"`, `BURN_PAUSE_SOURCE = "burn_alarm"` and `job_burn_sentence(record) -> str`, one plain sentence built from a `job_burn_record` and used only for a tripped one: for the per-sample basis, "The last {window_samples} provider calls spent {rate:.1f} tokens each on average, more than {multiplier:g} times the {expectation:.1f} tokens per call this job spent before them (from call {since_label} on).", and for the per-hour basis, "The last {window_samples} provider calls spent {rate:.1f} tokens per hour, more than {multiplier:g} times the {expectation:.1f} tokens per hour set in configuration (from call {since_label} on)." A person reads it in the decision and in the pause reason, so it names no internal basis label. (3) In `_stop_check`'s burn branch, after a NEW tripped record is set and persisted, and only when `job_approved_unattended(job)` holds: first `pause_control.request_pause(job.job_id, reason="burn_alarm: " + sentence, source=BURN_PAUSE_SOURCE, control_root_path=_control)`, and when that raises `pause_control.PauseControlError` the safe point returns the error signal `_pause_park_signal` already builds for that error, so the job blocks rather than burns on; then the decision: when an open decision's question starts with `BURN_DECISION_MARKER`, its `question` and `impact` are replaced with the new evidence, otherwise `escalation.enqueue_task_decision` adds one on the first task in plan order whose status is pending or running, else the job's first task, with the question `BURN_DECISION_MARKER + " " + sentence`, the options `resume` and `abandon`, an empty `safe_default`, and the impact "job <job_id> is paused until this is answered; continue it with `remedy job unpause <job_id>`"; then the job is persisted. The pause read further down the same `_stop_check` parks the job before its next provider call. An attended job is not paused: its trip stays the recorded warning D4 gives it. (4) The job's report and the documentation of the whole alarm follow with T003 in the next round; this round adds the pause and the decision only.

ALTERNATIVES: Treating every `run_job` run as unattended, REJECTED: a person who started `remedy job run` themselves is watching, and the feature file asks only for a warning then. A new decision type with its own resolve route, like the budget decision of DECISION F295 D11, REJECTED for this feature: the job pause and the task decision already exist, the watchdog already pairs them, and a second route would be a second answer to one question. Stopping the job instead of pausing it, REJECTED: the feature file asks for a pause, and a pause keeps the task's place for `remedy job unpause`.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the unattended branch in `_stop_check`, the three names and two functions it adds to `job_burn.py`, and their tests.

## DECISION F116 D6 — a failed burn pause request blocks the job even when the halt happens inside a task; T003, first half: the watchdog's burn tripwire becomes a caller of the burn detector, its own arithmetic is deleted, and its trip carries the basis label (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: (1) DECISION F116 D5 (3) says that when `pause_control.request_pause` raises, the safe point returns the error signal so that the job blocks rather than burns on. The round 5 worker measured that this holds at the pre-task safe point but not inside a task: the in-task halt branch of `run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` re-reads the pause with `_pause_park_signal`, a failed request has written nothing to re-read, and the halt then fell through to an ordinary stop with the job left running. The worker added six lines that block the job in that case, and the round 5 gate proved them with a test that turns red when they are removed. (2) DECISION F116 D1 (3) gives T003 the watchdog's unification. The reviewer measured it at `cf6b6868a`: `evaluate_burn_anomaly` in `packages/orchestration/watchdog.py` computes its own baseline and window means, its own minimum and its own strict comparison; its only production caller is `evaluate_ledger`; `tests/orchestration/test_watchdog.py` compares a burn trip's whole `numbers` dictionary with a literal once, in `test_burn_fires_when_the_window_beats_the_multiple`; and `evaluate_burn_rate` in `packages/orchestration/burn_detector.py` on the trailing basis computes the same verdict and the same numbers, which the two agreement tables of `tests/orchestration/test_burn_detector.py` prove for every case they hold. One difference exists: the watchdog's `measured_tokens` can return a negative total, which the watchdog counts, while the detector's `_is_measured` refuses a negative amount and treats it as not measured.

CHOSEN: (1) The six lines in `run_job`'s in-task halt branch stand as landed in `e1734aab3`: when the halt reason is a pause-control error and the fresh pause read returns nothing, the job is blocked through `_block_for_pause_error` with the halt's own reason. This widens DECISION F116 D5 (3) to every pause-control error that reaches that branch, which is the rule `_pause_park_signal`'s docstring already states: a pause-control error at any safe point blocks the job. (2) `evaluate_burn_anomaly` keeps its name, signature and return type, and its body becomes a translation only: each entry becomes `BurnSample(amount=measured_tokens(entry), label=_iteration(entry))`, the thresholds become `BurnThresholds(window=window, min_samples=min_samples, multiplier=multiplier)`, the reading comes from `evaluate_burn_rate`, and the function returns None when the reading is None or did not trip. Every line that computes a mean, compares a count with the minimum or compares the window with the multiple is DELETED from `watchdog.py`, as the feature file's Orchestrator brief requires; `watchdog.py` imports `BurnSample`, `BurnThresholds` and `evaluate_burn_rate` at module level. (3) The trip is built from the reading: `what` keeps its present sentence with `reading.window_samples`, `reading.rate`, `reading.expectation` and `reading.baseline_samples` in place of the local values; `since_iteration` is `reading.since_label`; `numbers` holds `window_mean` from `reading.rate`, `baseline_mean` from `reading.expectation`, `multiplier` from `reading.multiplier`, `baseline_samples` from `reading.baseline_samples`, and a new fifth key, `basis`, from `reading.basis`, which reads `trailing_baseline`, so the watchdog's rates carry their basis label as the feature file's Acceptance asks. The literal in `test_burn_fires_when_the_window_beats_the_multiple` gains that key; no other assertion of `tests/orchestration/test_watchdog.py` changes. (4) A ledger entry whose measured total is negative is no longer counted by the watchdog: the detector's definition of a measurement is the one definition, and a negative token total is not a measurement any provider reports. A new test in `tests/orchestration/test_watchdog.py` holds it. (5) `docs/system/autonomy-watchdog-v1.md` names `basis` among the trip's numbers, says that the `burn_anomaly` arithmetic is the burn detector's trailing basis, states the negative-total rule, and replaces the deliberate absence that said class-expectation detection is a later feature's with one that says the watchdog uses the trailing basis only. The module docstring of `burn_detector.py` and that of `tests/orchestration/test_burn_detector.py` say the watchdog calls the detector, in the present tense. (6) The job's report, what a person sees of a recorded trip outside `remedy job budget`, and the page that documents the whole alarm follow as T003's second half in the next round.

ALTERNATIVES: Keeping `evaluate_burn_anomaly`'s arithmetic and calling the detector beside it to compare, REJECTED: that is the wrapping the Orchestrator brief forbids, and two computations of one verdict can disagree. Deleting `evaluate_burn_anomaly` and having `evaluate_ledger` call the detector directly, REJECTED: the watchdog's tests and the detector's agreement tables call it by name, and the translation from ledger entries to samples and from a reading to a trip has to live somewhere; this function is that place. Keeping negative totals counted by giving the detector a flag, REJECTED: a flag would be a second definition of a measurement inside the one detector. Reverting the six in-task lines and leaving a failed pause request to stop the job, REJECTED: a stopped job is a different outcome from the one D5 (3) promised, and only a blocked job keeps a person in charge of what happens next.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph; restore `evaluate_burn_anomaly`'s body and the import block of `watchdog.py`, the two module docstrings, `tests/orchestration/test_watchdog.py` and `docs/system/autonomy-watchdog-v1.md` from `cf6b6868a`; delete the six in-task lines and the test that proves them. The round's bookkeeping files are deliberately left out: reversing a decision does not delete the record that it was made.

## DECISION F116 D7 — T003, second half, first part: `remedy job show` and the report section show a recorded burn alarm as its plain sentence, read through one tolerant reader; no parallel-width throttle is built, because a job has no parallel width (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F116 D1 (2) promises that an attended trip is a warning in what `remedy job show` prints and in the job's report, plus one run-log event, and leaves the optional parallel-width throttle to a measurement. The reviewer measured at `f807fe53c`. `remedy job show <id>` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py` prints `_export_job(job)` as JSON on stdout, which already carries `burn_reading` since DECISION F116 D4 (4), and prints its human blocks on stderr — the intake block, then the blocked-task findings block — so a person reading the text sees no burn alarm at all. The `report` section of `remedy job show --full`, `_report_section`, builds a progress payload whose key set `tests/cli/test_job_report.py` pins by set equality in `PROGRESS_KEYS`, and a progress view whose lines name the stop reason. `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` names no parallel width, no worker pool and no concurrency: `run_job` dispatches one task at a time, and each task makes one provider call at a time. A persisted `burn_reading` is read back with `data.get("burn_reading")`, so a torn or hand-edited job file can hand a view any value.

CHOSEN: (1) `packages/orchestration/job_burn.py` gains `recorded_burn_sentence(record) -> str | None`: None unless `record` is a dict whose `tripped` is True, and otherwise `job_burn_sentence(record)`, with `KeyError`, `TypeError` and `ValueError` from a record missing a field or holding a value of the wrong type read as None. Every view a person reads takes the sentence from this one reader, so no view raises on a damaged record. (2) `remedy job show <id>` prints, on stderr after the blocked-task findings block and only when that reader returns a sentence, a block headed `--- Burn alarm ---` with the sentence and the line `remedy job budget <id> shows the numbers.`; its JSON on stdout does not change. (3) The `report` section's data gains the key `burn_alarm`, after `latest_stop_reason`, holding the sentence or None, and its progress view prints `  Burn alarm: <sentence>` after the stop line when there is one; `PROGRESS_KEYS` gains the key. The F053 run report's markdown is not changed: its sections are pinned as one structure for final and interim reports, and the progress view above it already names the alarm. (4) No parallel-width throttle is built: there is no width to narrow. `job_burn.py`'s module docstring says so as a deliberate absence. (5) The run-log event of a new trip and the page that documents the whole alarm are the next round's.

ALTERNATIVES: Adding a burn key to `remedy job show`'s JSON, REJECTED: `burn_reading` is already there, and a second copy of one record is a second thing to keep in step. Calling `job_burn_sentence` directly from the views, REJECTED: it indexes the record and raises on a damaged one, and a read command that raises on a damaged job file is worse than one that stays silent about the alarm. Adding a section to the run report's markdown, REJECTED for this feature: its section structure is shared by the final and interim reports and pinned by their tests, and the progress view already carries the sentence. Building a throttle with nothing to throttle, REJECTED: code that cannot act is a promise it cannot keep.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `recorded_burn_sentence` and the deliberate-absence paragraph in `packages/orchestration/job_burn.py`, `_print_burn_alarm` and its call in `apps/cli/commands/job.py`, the `burn_alarm` key and line in `_report_section` and the import above them, the tests this round added in `tests/orchestration/test_job_burn.py`, `tests/cli/test_job_show.py` and `tests/cli/test_job_report.py`, and the `burn_alarm` entry of `PROGRESS_KEYS`. The round's bookkeeping files are deliberately left out: reversing a decision does not delete the record that it was made.

## DECISION F116 D8 — T003, second half, last part: a new trip writes one `job_burn_tripped` run-log event, and one page documents the whole alarm; with it the three building slices are complete (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F116 D1 (2) promises one run-log event for an attended trip, and D1 (3) the documentation of where the one definition lives. The reviewer measured at `9d83716dd`. `run_job` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` writes its task events through a task log that `_open_task_log` opens when the first task starts, so it is None at the pre-task safe point, while `append_run_event` in `packages/orchestration/timeline.py` writes one event to the job's run log at any time, as `_teach_task_lesson` already does; a field beyond the named ones lands in the event's `metadata`. `tests/orchestration/test_event_names.py` requires every written event name to be declared in `EVENT_NAMES` in `packages/orchestration/event_names.py`, and `tests/ui_contracts/test_humanize_catalog.py` requires the names emitted under `packages/` and `apps/` to equal the keys of `apps/ui/src/api/humanizeCatalog.ts`, and finds an emission only where the callee is named `append_run_event`, `log` or `emit_important_event`, so a call through an alias is invisible to it. No page under `docs/` describes the alarm as a whole: `docs/system/job-budget-enforcement-v0.md` describes `remedy job budget` and `docs/system/autonomy-watchdog-v1.md` the watchdog.

CHOSEN: (1) In `_stop_check`'s burn branch, directly after a NEW tripped record is set and persisted and before the unattended pause, `run_job` writes one event `job_burn_tripped` with `append_run_event`, called by that bare name, whose metadata is the record's keys plus `unattended`, the value `job_approved_unattended` returns; that value is computed once and the unattended branch reads it. A failure of the classes `_TASK_LOG_ERRORS` names is logged as one error with the traceback and the run continues, because a ledger write must never stop a healthy job. (2) `job_burn_tripped` joins `EVENT_NAMES` and `humanizeCatalog.ts`, each in its alphabetical place, the catalog line reading "The job's recent provider calls cost far more than expected, so its burn alarm tripped." (3) A new page, `docs/system/cost-anomaly-alarm-v1.md`, says where the one definition of expected spend lives and who calls it, what a reading compares and its two bases, how a job's samples and settings are taken, what a trip does attended and unattended, where a person sees it, and the deliberate absences; `docs/README.md` lists it in its quick-find table and in its system table. (4) T001, T002 and T003 are then built; the hardening stage of operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap comes next.

ALTERNATIVES: Writing the event through the task log, REJECTED: it does not exist at the pre-task safe point, where a trip can be read. Writing an event at every reading, REJECTED: a line per provider call that says nothing happened is noise in the timeline a person reads. Folding the page into the budget page, REJECTED: the alarm is not a budget limit and also serves the watchdog, so a reader looking for it there would find half of it.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the event write in `_stop_check` with its error log, the `job_burn_tripped` entries in `event_names.py` and `humanizeCatalog.ts`, the three tests this round added to `tests/orchestration/test_job_burn.py`, `docs/system/cost-anomaly-alarm-v1.md` and its two rows in `docs/README.md`. The round's bookkeeping files are deliberately left out: reversing a decision does not delete the record that it was made.

## DECISION F116 D9 — hardening repair round 1: the burn decision names `remedy job run` as what continues a burn-paused job, `remedy job budget` shows a recorded burn alarm on a job with no budgets, and the first trip's whole decision is pinned (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: The amend0930b-slow-cap acceptance audit of F116, run at `ddcedb336` and saved as `.agent/f116_acceptance_audit.md`, proved 21 of 24 claims at once and found two gaps, recorded as R-1173 and R-1174; the reviewer measured a third defect from the auditor's minor note, R-1175. DECISION F116 D5 (3) wrote the burn decision's impact as "job <job_id> is paused until this is answered; continue it with `remedy job unpause <job_id>`". Measured at `ddcedb336`: the park that follows the trip consumes the pause request, so `unpause_job_command` finds nothing to lift and answers `parked` with `remedy job run <job_id>` as its next step, and answering the decision only records the answer. `_cmd_job_budget` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py` returns before it reads the burn reading when the job has no budgets.

CHOSEN: (1) The impact reads "job <job_id> is paused; `remedy job run <job_id>` continues it, and answering this question only records your choice"; this amends the impact sentence of D5 (3), and `docs/system/cost-anomaly-alarm-v1.md` says the same. (2) The `recorded burn alarm` lines of `remedy job budget` move into one helper, `_print_recorded_burn_alarm`, which the limited path calls where the lines were and the no-budget path calls after its "no budgets configured." line; the no-budget JSON gains `burn_reading`, the persisted record or null, beside `budgets`. This makes D4 (5)'s "whatever limits the job has" true for a job with none, and the page says so. (3) `test_an_unattended_trip_pauses_the_job_before_the_next_call` asserts the whole question and the whole impact of the first decision; the re-trip test asserts the same impact through one helper; three tests of `TestJobBudgetCliRendersBurnReading` cover a job without budgets with a trip, in text and JSON, and without one. (4) The audit is repeated for claims 9b and 23 and for the impact once this round passes.

ALTERNATIVES: Wiring the decision's answers to the pause, so that `resume` relaunches and `abandon` stops the job, REJECTED for this feature: D5 rejected a second resolve route beside the existing job pause, and a relaunch started from a decision answer would be a new way to start a run, which belongs to a feature that owns decision routes. Making `remedy job unpause` relaunch a parked job, REJECTED: it would change the meaning of an existing command for every pause source, which this feature's Do-not-touch spirit and scope do not reach. Saying in the budget page that the burn alarm needs a limit, REJECTED: the alarm is not a money-limit feature, and a person who set no limit is exactly the one an alarm protects.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph; restore the impact sentence in `_stop_check` of `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`, `_cmd_job_budget` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py`, the two tests of `tests/orchestration/test_job_burn.py`, the three tests and helper added to `tests/orchestration/test_job_budgets.py` and the two sentences of `docs/system/cost-anomaly-alarm-v1.md` from `ddcedb336`. The round's bookkeeping files are deliberately left out: reversing a decision does not delete the record that it was made.
