## DECISION F298 D1 — F298 runs in the feature file's seven slices, T001 to T007 in order, the contract as data first; the claim's measurement is `.agent/f298_inventory.md`, and T007's digest bound is 65,536 bytes (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F298.md` lists T001 to T007 and asks the first round to repeat every measurement and to fix T007's size bound. The claim's measurement, `.agent/f298_inventory.md`, was taken on `main` at `77493e0f9` with the fake providers on scratch repositories and a scratch data root, and every "Measured" sentence of the feature file reproduced: in a folder that is no repository the order fails its init step; in repository `a` an order whose header names `project: b` files the job under project b and runs it in `a`; a full fake run leaves `C001` unmet and `remedy job apply <job> --approve --commit-with-history --push --json` answers `"ok": true`, `"status": "blocked"` and a `blocked_reason` beginning `push_refused:`, exits 0 and moves neither `a` nor its upstream; after `remedy mission abandon` the completed job still reads `waits_for_apply` true; an order of two jobs answers `waiting_job_ids` and a `next` sentence telling a person to commit and then run; two starts of one order file make two missions; the contract templates are the four the file names; `remedy init` leaves `remedy.toml` and `.remedy/config.toml` untracked; the order header's one cap is `max-cost-usd`; a job's `total_tokens` is input plus output with cache tokens excluded (read in `pingpong_job.py`, since the fake provider reports no tokens); `final_job_review.json` reads `PASS` with no acceptance criteria while `test_passed` and `test_command` are null. Two readings are new: 1,000 added completed jobs grew the scratch digest from 7,249 to 514,249 bytes, and the operator's own data root gives a `client` object of 8,622,726 bytes over 11,652 jobs, 1,122 of them waiting for an apply, with 13,480 open decisions.

CHOSEN: (1) The slices run in the feature file's order, one at a time, each one or more reviewed rounds and none mixed with another. (2) T001 first: one module holds the contract as data — operations with their flags and answer fields, the digest's and the answers' keys, the job states and mission status words, the refusal tokens, the exit codes, the contract templates, the budget kinds and the document's version — one command prints it with `--json`, `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md` is rendered from it, and a test fails when the code returns a key the document does not name or the document names one the code does not return. T001's first round reads where each of those already lives in the code and fixes in a DECISION, in the same round as its patch, which are read from the code and which are declared, so that nothing is typed twice. Every later slice that adds a key, a token or a word adds it to the document in the same round. (3) T002, T003 and T004 next, in that order: the part F253 cannot start without, with T004's second gate test driving what T002 and T003 make true. (4) T005, T006 and T007 after them. (5) T007's bound, which the feature file asks this round to fix: with 1,000 settled jobs on a scratch data root the default digest stays under 65,536 bytes and names how many jobs it left out. T007's own round decides what "still needs something" means, because on the operator's data root 1,122 completed jobs wait for an apply and 13,480 decisions are open, and a default that lists all of those stays several megabytes. (6) If the soft limit forces a split, what remains of T005 to T007 moves to a feature placed directly behind this one and before F253 (the feature file's Orchestrator brief, and operator amendment amend0906-split-placement). (7) Then the hardening stage of operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap, then the closure sequence.

ALTERNATIVES: The behaviour slices first and the document last, REJECTED: each slice would add keys and tokens to a page written by hand, which is the drift the feature exists to end. T003 before T002, REJECTED: an order that changes the wrong repository is the larger harm, and the feature file's order already puts it first. A size bound taken from the operator's data root, REJECTED: that root is the operator's own and changes daily, while the Acceptance line names a scratch root with 1,000 settled jobs.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph and the feature file's slice order section; the slices are then re-planned at the next round.

## DECISION F298 D2 — T001's first part: the machine client interface is a dict read from the code by `apps/cli/client_interface.py` and printed by `remedy client interface`; the product says "interface" because the vocabulary reserves "contract" (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T001 of `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F298.md` asks for one document, generated from the code, that names every operation a client uses with its fields, the keys the digest and the answers return, the job states and mission status words, the refusal tokens, the exit codes, the contract templates, the budget kinds and its own version, printed by one command with `--json`, rendered as `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md`, and held equal to the code by a test. Read at `0deb416e6`: the command catalog `apps/cli/command_catalog.py` already holds every command's arguments (`ArgDef`: name, help, required, option, flag, repeatable) and the exit codes its handler can reach, which `tests/cli/test_exit_codes.py` holds to a static reading of the handler; `apps/cli/exit_codes.py` holds each code's meaning; `RunState` in `packages/core/models.py` holds every job state a digest job can carry; `MISSION_STATUSES` in `packages/orchestration/mission_state.py` the mission status words; `list_contract_templates` the templates; `JobBudgets` the budget kinds; `apps/cli/json_envelope.py` the envelope. `docs/system/vocabulary.md` makes "contract" a binding word that names a mission's acceptance criteria and nothing else, and `tests/docs/test_vocabulary.py` refuses a catalog description that uses it otherwise; the reviewer's dry run measured exactly that refusal for a command first named `client contract`.

CHOSEN: (1) `apps/cli/client_interface.py` holds `build_client_interface()`, which returns `interface_version` (`1.1`), `envelope`, `operations`, `exit_codes`, `job_states`, `mission_statuses`, `contract_templates` and `budget_kinds`, each read at call time from the place named above; it reads only. The one declared list is `CLIENT_OPERATION_IDS`, the catalog commands a client uses: `do.run`, `status.run`, `decision.resolve`, `job.run`, `job.resume`, `job.apply`, `change.proof`, `job.evidence`, `patch.hunks`, `patch.approve-hunks`, `patch.approve`, `patch.reject`, `mission.abandon` and `client.interface`. An operation the catalog lacks raises `KeyError` rather than leaving a silent gap. Each operation is spelled `remedy <group> <subcommand>`, a form the parser always accepts. (2) `remedy client interface`, in a new advanced group `client` owned by F298 and reached from the golden path, prints that dict as the envelope's payload with `--json`, and a short summary otherwise. (3) The module lives under `apps/cli/` because it reads the catalog; F253's HTTP call imports it from there. (4) The product, its code and its command say "machine client interface"; the feature file's word "contract" for this document is not used on any catalog surface. The page keeps its file name until the round that renders it decides its title. (5) The keys of the answers and of the digest, the refusal tokens and the rendered page are T001's next rounds; each adds to the same dict.

ALTERNATIVES: Naming the command `client contract`, REJECTED: the vocabulary test refuses it, and the vocabulary reserved the word after an earlier group that used it for another concept was deleted. Building the document in `packages/orchestration/`, REJECTED: it would read the command catalog across the boundary for every field, while `apps/cli/` already owns the catalog and the exit codes. Spelling a default subcommand short (`remedy do` instead of `remedy do run`), REJECTED: it would need the parser's private default table, and the full form is always accepted.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `apps/cli/client_interface.py`, `apps/cli/commands/client_cmd.py` and `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, the `client` group and the `client.interface` entry in `apps/cli/command_catalog.py`, `client_cmd` in `apps/cli/commands/__init__.py`, the two lines of `tests/orchestration/import_reachability_allowlist.txt`, the `client` group in `tests/cli/test_cli_ux.py` with its count, the section "The interface as data" of `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md`, and the clause added to that page's row in `docs/README.md`.

## DECISION F298 D3 — T001's second part: the digest's keys are one declared tree in the interface, held to the digest's code by its syntax tree and to a real run's digest by a live test (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T001's Acceptance line asks for a test that fails when the code returns a key the document does not name, or the document names one the code does not return. The digest a client reads, the `client` object of `remedy status --json`, is built by `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py` from dict literals, plus `cost_today`, the dict literal `project_cost_of_day` in `packages/orchestration/project_cockpit.py` returns. Measured at `d9697d902` on the round 1 scratch data root: every key of that object is a fixed name, and no level is a map keyed by data. A key's place cannot be read from the syntax tree, because the literals are built in helpers and joined at run time; its name can.

CHOSEN: (1) `DIGEST_KEY_TREE` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` names the digest's keys as a tree: each key maps to the tree of the object under it, or of every element of the list under it; the interface carries it under `digest`, and the text output names its top-level keys. (2) `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py` holds it from two sides. The names in the tree equal the string keys of every dict literal in `client_digest.py` and in `project_cost_of_day`, read from their syntax trees, so a key the code writes and the tree omits, or a key the tree names and the code does not write, is red. A real run with the fake providers and a deadline that has passed, the first step of F295's gate test, leaves a digest with a mission, a project's day, a job's evidence and an open budget decision; every key path that digest returns must be a path of the tree, so a key in the wrong place is red too. (3) The helpers of F295's gate test are imported from `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py`, not copied. (4) T005, T006 and T007 change the digest; each round that does extends the tree, and these tests force it.

ALTERNATIVES: Generating the tree from a recorded run and committing it as a data file, REJECTED: a key that only a rare state reaches, such as a plan approval's clarifications, would drop out of the document without anything going red. Reading the tree's shape from the syntax tree alone, REJECTED: the shape is joined at run time and no static reading can place a key.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `DIGEST_KEY_TREE` and the `digest` key from `apps/cli/client_interface.py`, the `Digest` line from `apps/cli/commands/client_cmd.py`, the two digest tests with their helpers and the digest assertions of the vocabulary and text-output tests from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, and the digest sentence from the section "The interface as data" of `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md`.

## DECISION F298 D4 — T001's third part: each operation's refusal tokens are declared in the interface and held to a static reading of its handler, with dynamic sites verified by hand (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: T001 asks the document to name every refusal token a client meets. A refusal envelope's token is the first argument, or the `error` keyword, of `fail`, `emit_error` or `build_error`. The catalog's exit codes are already held this way: declared per command and asserted against a static reading of the handler in `tests/cli/test_exit_codes.py`, whose module walk follows same-module calls by bare name and `apps.cli` imports, including imports inside a function. The reviewer's prototype at `da6ace684`, `.remedy-wt/f298-r4/token_proto.py`, read the fourteen operations that way and found 81 literal tokens, counted per operation, and five sites whose token is not a literal, at four places: `exc.error` in `_cmd_do` (an `OrderFileError`), `exc.code` in `_consume_plan_approval` (a `PlanEditRefused`), the `error` parameter `forward_effect` passes through, reached by `job run` and `job resume`, and `result.code` in `_cmd_approve_hunks` (a `HunkApprovalRefusal`). `remedy status` and `remedy job apply` reach no token at all; the apply's blocked answer is the `"ok": true` the claim measured.

CHOSEN: (1) `OPERATION_REFUSAL_TOKENS` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` names, per operation, its tokens sorted; each operation of the interface carries them as `refusal_tokens`. (2) `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py` reads each operation's handler with `_module_info` from `tests/cli/test_exit_codes.py`, collects the literal tokens it reaches, and folds in `UNRESOLVED_TOKEN_SITES`, which names each dynamic site with the tokens a reader verified by hand and why; a dynamic site missing from it fails with its location, and the result must equal the declaration. (3) The hand-verified sets that come from code are held to it too: the `OrderFileError` tokens equal the literals `order_file.py` raises, read from its syntax tree, and the hunk refusal codes equal the `REFUSAL_` and `HUNK_RECORD_REFUSAL_` constants of `hunk_approval.py` and `hunk_decision_record.py`. (4) The `PlanEditRefused` site names no token: `consume_plan_approval` raises it only as `approval_closed`, which the line before it answers as `no_pending_plan_approval`. (5) T003 gives `remedy job apply` its refusal tokens; that round extends the declaration, and this test forces it.

ALTERNATIVES: Reading the tokens at run time inside the product, REJECTED: the product would parse its own source on every call, and the catalog's exit codes set the precedent of a declaration held by a test. A second copy of the exit-code walk, REJECTED: the module walk is imported, so both readings follow the code the same way. Listing every token any `apps/cli` module can answer, REJECTED: it would name tokens no client operation can meet.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `OPERATION_REFUSAL_TOKENS` and the `refusal_tokens` key from `apps/cli/client_interface.py`, the token reader, `UNRESOLVED_TOKEN_SITES` and its three tests with the `refusal_tokens` assertion from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, and the token sentences from the section "The interface as data" of `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md`.

## DECISION F298 D5 — T001's fourth part: the top-level answer keys of the path's six operations are declared in the interface and held to a static reading of each handler and to a real run of the path (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T001 asks the document to name every key the answers return, and its Acceptance line asks for a test that fails when the code returns a key the document does not name, or the document names one the code does not return. Read at `c4521aee1`: every answer is printed by `emit_ok`, or by `fail`, `emit_error` or `build_error` with keywords beyond the envelope's own, and a handler names its keys as keywords, as a dict literal it spreads with `**`, or as a spread of a builder's return. The reviewer's prototype at `c4521aee1`, `.remedy-wt/f298-r5/answer_proto.py`, read the fourteen operations through the same module walk as DECISION F298 D4: the six of the path, `remedy do`, `remedy status`, `remedy decision resolve`, `remedy job run`, `remedy job apply` and `remedy change proof`, leave five sites the reading cannot resolve — the keyword pass-through of the two job id resolvers in `apps/cli/job_id_arg.py`, which no call on these paths uses, and the spreads of `export_job_report`, `export_job_apply_json` and `export_proof_chain_json`, each of which returns one dict literal — while the other eight operations leave eight more. A real run of F295's path returns, for each of the six, only keys that reading names, and `remedy status` writes three keys that only an answer with an unreadable runtime state or with skipped record files carries.

CHOSEN: (1) `OPERATION_ANSWER_KEYS` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` names, for the six operations of the path, every top-level key an answer can carry beside the envelope's four, sorted, whether the command succeeds or refuses; the interface carries it under `answers`. (2) `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py` reads each handler with the walk of D4, now shared by both readings, collects the keywords of every answer call and the keys of every dict literal a handler spreads, with the keys it stores into that dict, and folds in `UNRESOLVED_ANSWER_SITES`, which names each site the reading cannot resolve with the keys a reader verified by hand and why; the result must equal the declaration. (3) The hand-verified sets of the three builders are held to their code: each equals the keys of the dict literal its builder returns, read from its syntax tree, and the job run's set also the keys `_cmd_job_run` stores into the report. (4) A real run of the path, with the preview and the approved apply both read, returns no top-level key the declaration does not name. (5) The keys under these keys, and the answers of the other eight operations, are T001's next parts; each extends the same declaration and these tests force it.

ALTERNATIVES: Declaring each answer's whole key tree in this round, REJECTED: `execution_config` alone carries forty keys, `modes_applied` is keyed by the paths a job changed, and the round would mix two readings in one change. Holding the declaration to the live run alone, REJECTED: a key only a degraded status or a refusal carries would drop out of the document with nothing red. Reading all fourteen operations now, REJECTED: eight more hand-verified sites would double the round in a mode that asks for small ones.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `OPERATION_ANSWER_KEYS` and the `answers` key from `apps/cli/client_interface.py`, `UNRESOLVED_ANSWER_SITES`, the answer reader and its four tests with the `answers` assertion from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, and the `answers` sentences from the section "The interface as data" of `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md`; the shared walk may stay.

## DECISION F298 D6 — T001's fifth part: the top-level answer keys of seven more operations, with three more sites verified by hand and an annotated dict read like a plain one; `job resume` follows alone (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F298 D5 declared the top-level answer keys of the path's six operations and left the other eight for later. Read at `2214c8f0b` with D5's reader: `remedy job evidence`, `patch hunks`, `patch approve-hunks`, `patch approve`, `patch reject`, `mission abandon` and `client interface` leave four sites it cannot resolve. Resolving a name bound to a builder's call inside the reader, REJECTED: the builders live in `packages/`, which the shared module walk does not follow, and a hand-verified set held to the builder's own syntax tree is the D4 and D5 pattern.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete the seven entries from `OPERATION_ANSWER_KEYS`, the three sites and their assertions from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, the seven answers of its live test, and the annotated-binding branch of `_bound_dict_keys`; restore the page's `answers` sentence from `158a20b68`.

## DECISION F298 D7 — T001's sixth part: `job resume`'s top-level answer keys, the union of its shapes, with a keyword-only `dict(...)` read like a literal and four builder sites held to their code (2026-10-07)

CONTEXT: DECISION F298 D6 left `remedy job resume` alone, because its answers come from five builders. ## DECISION F298 D8 — T001's seventh part: the keys under the answers' top-level keys are declared as trees, `remedy do` first, each tree held to the code that builds it and to a real run (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: DECISIONs F298 D5 to D7 named every top-level answer key of the fourteen operations and left the keys under them for later. Measured at `0c3b8a91d` with `.remedy-wt/f298-r8/probe_nested.py`, which replays the live test's run: the answers reach 571 paths below the top level, under 36 top-level keys of eleven operations (`.remedy-wt/f298-r8/count_probe.txt`), built in many functions of `packages/`. Some objects are keyed by data rather than by names: `remedy do`'s `cost.mirror_errors` by job id, `remedy job apply`'s `modes_applied` and `remedy job evidence`'s `files` by path, and the interface's own `answers` by operation. A mission contract criterion's `check` carries a `spec` whose keys are the arguments of the check's `kind`, which F061's check schema validates per kind. `remedy do` answers six objects below its top level: `contract`, read back from the mission's record, whose fields `packages/orchestration/mission_contract.py` fixes in `_CONTRACT_FIELDS`, `_CRITERION_FIELDS` and `_AMENDMENT_FIELDS` and whose `check` is a `DoDCheck`; `cost`, from `do_cost_summary`; `jobs`, from `do_job_task_listing`; `steps`, from `DoStepResult.to_json`; and `landed` and `push`, which the run does not reach and which only `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py` writes, through `ctx.landed.append(...)`, `_do_push_record` and `ctx.push_outcome`.

CHOSEN: (1) `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` names, per operation and top-level key, the tree of the keys under that key, in the form of `DIGEST_KEY_TREE`; a top-level key absent from it carries no keys below it. The key `*` stands for keys that are data and maps to the tree under each of them; a key that maps to None holds an object whose keys the interface does not fix, and only a check's `spec` may. The interface carries it under `answer_trees`. (2) This round declares `remedy do`'s six trees. (3) `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py` holds each to the code that builds it: the contract's levels to the three field constants, to the two `to_json` methods and to `DoDCheck.model_fields`; `cost` and `jobs` to the keys of the dict literals in their builders; `steps` to the dict `to_json` returns; `landed` and `push` to the keys the module appends, updates and stores into those two names, and to the dict `_do_push_record` returns. (4) The live test checks every answer of an operation the trees declare, at every depth, and asserts that `remedy do`'s answer reaches a check's `kind`, a task's `deliverable` and a step's `detail`. (5) The other operations' trees follow in later parts, a few operations at a time; the part that adds the last requires a tree for every top-level key that carries keys below it.

ALTERNATIVES: Replacing the lists of top-level keys with trees, REJECTED: two representations in one round, and the lists are what the handler reading of D5 holds. Declaring every operation's trees in one round, REJECTED: 571 paths in many builders is several rounds of hand-verified sources in a mode that asks for small ones. Naming each `spec` key per check kind, REJECTED for now: F061 owns that schema and validates it per kind, so the interface names the check's own keys and leaves `spec` open, which a later part may close. Holding the trees to the live run alone, REJECTED: `landed` and `push` appear only after a commit and a push, which this run does not make.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `ANSWER_KEY_TREES`, the `answer_trees` key of `build_client_interface` and `answer_trees` from `OPERATION_ANSWER_KEYS["client.interface"]` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py`; delete `_tree_names`, `_opaque_paths`, `_undeclared_paths`, `_expression_keys`, their two tests, the `answer_trees` assertion and site key, and the nested half and reach assertion of the live test from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; restore the page's `answers` sentences from `fa079e7cb`.

## DECISION F298 D12 — T001's eleventh part: the answer trees of the four `remedy patch` commands, two of them declared empty (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: DECISIONs F298 D8 to D11 declared the answer trees of five operations. Read at `d6ff91214`: `remedy patch hunks` answers the diff view `build_diff_view` in `packages/orchestration/diff_view_source.py` binds as `view` and fills, whose `files` come from `parse_unified_diff_to_view` in `packages/orchestration/diff_parser.py`: each file a dict literal appended to `files` with its `stats` inside, each hunk one appended to `hunks_out`, each line one appended to `hunk["lines"]` and given its `intraline` spans, lists of offset pairs, by `_apply_intraline_spans`; and the `decision` `recorded_hunk_decision` in `packages/orchestration/hunk_decision_record.py` returns, or the empty one `_cmd_show_hunks` binds when the view shows no attempt. `remedy patch approve-hunks` answers the recorded decision, whose `hunks` rows carry `_EXPORT_ENTRY_KEYS` of `packages/orchestration/hunk_ledger.py`. `remedy patch approve` and `remedy patch reject` answer a constant, a `bool(...)` and three values of the approval entry, whose `risk` is one of the risk level words of `packages/orchestration/approval_queue.py`, so neither answers a key below its top level.

CHOSEN: (1) `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` declares `patch.hunks`'s `view` and `decision` and `patch.approve-hunks`'s `hunks`, and maps `patch.approve` and `patch.reject` to an empty dict, which the declaration's comment now defines as an operation that answers no keys below its top level, as against an operation absent from the declaration, whose trees a later part names. (2) A test holds each level of the diff view to the code that builds it, the decision to `recorded_hunk_decision`'s dict literals and to the empty decision of `_cmd_show_hunks`, and the recorded rows to `_EXPORT_ENTRY_KEYS`. (3) A second test reads the one answer call of each of the two intent handlers and requires every value to be a constant, a `bool(...)` or the approval entry's `intent_id`, `target_path` or `risk`, and every risk word to be a string. (4) The live test asserts that `remedy patch hunks` reaches a line's `intraline`, a file's `stats` and the decision's `attempt_key`.

ALTERNATIVES: Leaving the two intent commands out of the declaration until a later part, REJECTED: they answer nothing below their top level today, and saying so is what lets the last part require an entry for every operation. Naming the diff view's keys from its own documentation, REJECTED: the code is the source the interface reads, and the parser's docstring is held by nothing.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete the four `patch` entries from `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` and the sentence about an empty dict from its comment in `apps/cli/client_interface.py`; delete the two patch tests and the patch hunks reach assertion of the live test from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; restore the page's `answer_trees` sentence from `ee8c498b4`.

## DECISION F298 D13 — T001's twelfth part: `remedy job evidence`'s answer trees, with the target guard as a second shared tree (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: DECISIONs F298 D8 to D12 declared the answer trees of nine operations. Read at `b18ca3ce5`: `remedy job evidence` answers the dict `export_job_evidence` in `packages/orchestration/job_evidence.py` returns. Its `files` is the map `written`, annotated `dict[str, str]`, from the path of each file written into the bundle to where it was written. Its `manifest` is the dict `_build_job_manifest` returns, with the `bundle_generated_at` the export stores into it afterwards; inside it `task_statuses` and `task_run_ids` are dict comprehensions keyed by task id, each holding a word, and `execution_config` and `target_guard` come from `_export_execution_config` and `_export_target_guard`, which the module imports from `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`, the same exporters `remedy job run`'s answer uses.

CHOSEN: (1) `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` declares `job.evidence`'s `files` as `{"*": {}}`, keys that are paths, and its `manifest`, whose two task maps are `{"*": {}}` and whose `execution_config` and `target_guard` refer to the shared trees. (2) `TARGET_GUARD_KEY_TREE` names the target guard's keys once, and `job.run`'s tree now refers to it too, as D9 did for the execution configuration. (3) A test holds `files` to the annotation of `written`, the manifest to `_build_job_manifest`'s returned dict and the export's stores, each task map to a dict comprehension, and the two shared trees to the expressions the manifest builds them with and to the identity of the imported exporters with `pingpong_job`'s. (4) The live test asserts that the export reaches the manifest's execution configuration and target guard, and names at least one file and one task.

ALTERNATIVES: Naming the bundle's file paths, REJECTED: which files a bundle holds depends on the job and its tasks, so they are data, and the interface already says each value is a path. Keeping the target guard inline in two answers, REJECTED: two declarations of one set of keys can drift.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `job.evidence` from `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` and `TARGET_GUARD_KEY_TREE` from `apps/cli/client_interface.py`, restoring `job.run`'s inline target guard from `8f8c2e181`; delete the job evidence tree test, the target guard identity assertions of the job run tree test and the job evidence reach assertions of the live test from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; restore the page's `answer_trees` sentence from `c07cadbf3`.

## DECISION F298 D14 — T001's thirteenth part: `remedy mission abandon`'s answer trees, a mark for a shape that repeats itself, and the mission contract as a shared tree (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: DECISIONs F298 D8 to D13 declared the answer trees of ten operations. Read at `beb901add`: `remedy mission abandon` answers `version` and `mission`, which `_mission_json` in `apps/cli/commands/mission_cmd.py` builds from `Mission.to_json` in `packages/orchestration/mission_state.py`, adding `job_state` to each job link. The record's `order` is `MissionOrder.to_json`, its `contract` is the mission contract `remedy do` already answers under `contract`, and its `mission_plan` is the plan model's `model_dump()` with the keys two functions store into it: `plan_mission` in `packages/orchestration/mission_compiler.py` stores `_versions` and `_version`, and `mark_milestone_done` in `packages/orchestration/orchestrator_loop.py` stores `_milestones_done`. `_versions` holds each earlier plan body whole, and each of those still holds its own `_versions`, so the shape repeats itself to any depth. A tree in Python can hold itself, but `json.dumps` refuses an object that holds itself, and the tests' tree readers would never end on one.

CHOSEN: (1) `KEY_TREE_REPEAT_MARK`, the string `^`, is a value a tree's key may map to: the object under that key, or each element of the list under it, has the shape of the object that holds the key. `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` uses it only at a mission plan's `_versions`. (2) `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` declares `mission.abandon`'s `mission`, with its job links, its order, its plan with the plan's milestones and their draft jobs, and its contract. (3) `MISSION_CONTRACT_KEY_TREE` names a mission contract's keys once, and `do.run`'s tree now refers to it, as D9 did for the execution configuration and D13 for the target guard. (4) A test holds the mission to `Mission.to_json`, the job links to `MissionJobLink.to_json` and the key `_mission_json` adds, the order to `MissionOrder.to_json`, the plan to the tree the plan model's `model_dump()` writes plus the keys the two writers store, and the writers themselves to exactly those two functions in `packages/` and `apps/`. (5) The live test reads the abandon answer's levels, and builds a plan with a history of two versions from the real one, because a first plan has no earlier version: the tree names it, and a key one earlier version adds is still caught.

ALTERNATIVES: Naming the repeated tree by a name in a list of named trees, REJECTED for now: it adds a part to the document that one key needs; the mark says the same thing in place, and the later part that renders the page can still introduce names if the interface's own trees need them. Declaring a fixed depth of earlier versions, REJECTED: the depth grows with every recompile, so any fixed depth is wrong for some mission. Leaving `_versions` open as None, REJECTED: None admits any key at all, and the earlier versions have a known shape.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `mission.abandon` from `ANSWER_KEY_TREES`, `KEY_TREE_REPEAT_MARK` and `MISSION_CONTRACT_KEY_TREE` from `apps/cli/client_interface.py`, restoring `do.run`'s inline contract from `beb901add`; delete the mission tree test, its three helpers and the abandon assertions of the live test from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, and restore the tree readers there from `beb901add`; restore the page's `answer_trees` sentence from `beb901add`.

## DECISION F298 D15 — T001's fourteenth part: the answer trees of `remedy client interface` itself, whose key trees repeat under every name (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: DECISION F298 D14 introduced `KEY_TREE_REPEAT_MARK` for a shape that repeats itself. Read at `d0087778a`: `remedy client interface` answers the dict `build_client_interface` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` returns. Its `envelope` and every element of its `exit_codes` are dict literals there; each element of `operations` is the dict `_operation_entry` returns, whose `arguments` are the dicts `_argument_entry` returns. Its `digest` is a copy of `DIGEST_KEY_TREE` and its `answer_trees` a copy of `ANSWER_KEY_TREES`: key trees, whose names are the names of another answer, and under each name stands a key tree again, empty, None or the mark. Its `answers` maps each command id to a list of names. Every other top-level key holds a word or a list of words.

CHOSEN: (1) `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` declares `client.interface`'s `envelope`, `operations` with their `arguments`, and `exit_codes` by their keys; `digest` as `{"*": KEY_TREE_REPEAT_MARK}`, names that are data each holding a key tree again; `answer_trees` as command ids, then top-level keys, then such a key tree; and `answers` as `{"*": {}}`. (2) A test holds those trees to the dict literals and the two entry builders, the `digest`, `answers` and `answer_trees` to the exact expressions `build_client_interface` answers them with, every leaf of the declared trees to None or the mark, and every other top-level key to a word or a list of words. (3) The test that says where None and the mark may stand now names the exact set of places the mark stands: a mission plan's `_versions`, the digest's names and the answer trees' names. (4) The live test reads the interface's answer down to an argument's keys, an exit code's meaning, a digest name below a mission, and a plan's versions inside the answer trees.

ALTERNATIVES: Declaring `digest` as `DIGEST_KEY_TREE` itself, REJECTED: it would hold the description of the digest to the digest's key names a second time, while what a client meets under `digest` is a tree of names whose shape the interface states once, here. Declaring both as None, REJECTED: None says the keys are not fixed, while the shape of a key tree is fixed.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `client.interface` from `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` and restore the two comments on the mark and the trees from `d0087778a`; delete the interface tree test and `_tree_leaves` from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, restore the test of where None and the mark stand and the live test from `d0087778a`; restore the page's `answer_trees` sentence from `d0087778a`.

## DECISION F298 D16 — T001's fifteenth part: `remedy decision resolve`'s answer trees, every shape, with the job budgets as a fourth shared tree (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: Read at `a941f79a9`: `_cmd_decision_resolve` in `apps/cli/commands/decision.py` answers in one shape for each kind of decision it resolves and each outcome that changes its keys: a stop reason, a task's question, the plan approval approved, the plan approval rejected, a proposed task, a replan proposal, a budget decision abandoned and a budget decision extended. Over all of them, three keys hold objects. A plan approval's `answers` is a list of records, one per bundled question, built as a dict literal with `id`, `source` and `answer`. An extend's `budgets` is the job's budgets after it, `merged.model_dump(mode='json')` of a `JobBudgets` in `answer_budget_decision` in `packages/orchestration/budget_decision.py`, and its `raised` maps each limit it raised to the new value, keyed by the same names. Every other key holds a word, an id, a path, None or a list of decision ids; `matches` comes only from the refusal of an ambiguous job id, a list of job ids.

CHOSEN: (1) `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` declares `decision.resolve`'s `answers` by its record's keys, and `raised` and `budgets` as `JOB_BUDGETS_KEY_TREE`, which names the job budget kinds once. (2) A test reads every expression the handler answers each key with, over all its shapes, and holds it equal to a table read by hand, `_DECISION_ANSWER_SOURCES`, whose comment says why each key without a tree holds no object; it holds the record keys to the dict literal, the shared tree to the tree `JobBudgets`'s dump writes, and `budgets` and `raised` to the expressions `answer_budget_decision` builds them with. (3) The live test reads the extend's answer down to a raised limit and a budget kind.

ALTERNATIVES: Declaring `raised` as keys that are data, REJECTED: its keys are budget kinds by construction, since each is looked up in the job's budgets, and naming them tells a client more. Running every shape live, REJECTED for this part: every shape but the extend needs a record the gate test's path never makes, and the static reading reaches all of them.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `decision.resolve` from `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` and `JOB_BUDGETS_KEY_TREE` from `apps/cli/client_interface.py`; delete `_DECISION_ANSWER_SOURCES`, the decision tree test and the extend assertions of the live test from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; restore the page's `answer_trees` sentence from `a941f79a9`.

## DECISION F298 D17 — T001's sixteenth part: `remedy job resume`'s answer trees, with `remedy job run`'s report trees shared (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: Read at `bf20bdb92`: `remedy job resume` answers through several paths. `_cmd_job_resume` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py` answers a preview built by `_resume_preview`, whose `stop_request`, `worktree_head` and `budget_stop` are dict literals; it answers a stop or a no-op with words; it hands a job the ping-pong engine already ran to `_cmd_job_run`, which answers that job's report exactly as `remedy job run` does; and it hands every other job to `_cmd_job_run_cycles`, which answers `CycleLoopResult.to_json` in `packages/orchestration/long_run_executor.py`, whose `cycles` are `CycleRecord.to_json` records, or, for a single pass, `_cmd_run_next_task_local`'s answer, whose `failures` are a list of dict literals. `--checkpoint` routes to `_cmd_resume`, which answers `export_dry_run_json` or `export_resume_result_json` in `packages/orchestration/event_replay.py`, with `worktrees`, each `WorktreeResumeOutcome.to_json` in `packages/orchestration/worktree_resume.py`.

CHOSEN: (1) `JOB_REPORT_KEY_TREES` holds the trees that were `job.run`'s, and `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` maps `job.run` to it. (2) `job.resume` declares those same trees, the preview's three objects, the single pass's `failures`, the executor's `cycles` and the replay's `worktrees`. (3) A test holds the hand-off to `_cmd_job_run` and the identity of the shared trees, each preview object to the dict literal it is bound to, `failures` to its list's element, `cycles` to `CycleRecord.to_json` and to the list `CycleLoopResult.to_json` builds from its records, and `worktrees` to `WorktreeResumeOutcome.to_json`, to every expression `_cmd_resume` answers or stores them with, and to the return types of the functions that make the outcomes. (4) The live test reads the preview down to each of its three objects. (5) The proof that every other key of `job.resume`, and of every operation, holds no object is the next part, which takes it as its own item.

ALTERNATIVES: Declaring the hand-off's report keys again under `job.resume`, REJECTED: one report has one set of trees. Proving the other keys hold no object in this part, REJECTED: `job.resume` alone answers through every function the context names, and the slow pace this feature runs at asks for one proof per round.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `job.resume` from `ANSWER_KEY_TREES` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` and restore `job.run`'s inline trees from `bf20bdb92`, deleting `JOB_REPORT_KEY_TREES`; delete the job resume tree test, `_bound_dict_values`, the identity assertion of the job run tree test and the preview assertions of the live test from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; restore the page's `answer_trees` sentence from `bf20bdb92`.

## DECISION F298 D18 — T001's seventeenth part: every operation has an answer tree entry, and `remedy job resume`'s keys without a tree are proved plain; D17 (5) narrowed (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: DECISION F298 D17 (5) named, as this part, the proof that every key without a tree holds no object, "`job.resume`'s, and of every operation". Read at `f27eac67a`: every operation now has an entry in `ANSWER_KEY_TREES`, and no test says so. `remedy job resume` answers its keys without a tree through `_cmd_job_resume`, `_resume_preview`, `_cmd_run_next_task_local` and `_cmd_resume` in `apps/cli/commands/job.py`, as answer-call keywords, a `dict(...)` of keywords and a returned dict literal, and through the dicts `_cmd_job_run_cycles` and `_cmd_resume` answer whole: `CycleLoopResult.to_json`, `export_dry_run_json` and `export_resume_result_json`, whose values read the fields of `CycleLoopResult`, `ResumeDryRun` and `ResumeResult`. The live run reaches only the preview and a refusal among those shapes. Every other operation's keys without a tree were read when its trees were declared, in the contexts of DECISIONs F298 D8 to D17, and the live run reaches each operation's answers.

CHOSEN: (1) A test fails when an operation has no entry in `ANSWER_KEY_TREES`, and the comment there says every operation has one. (2) A test reads every expression those four functions answer under a key `job.resume` gives no tree, holds it equal to a table read by hand, `_RESUME_PLAIN_SOURCES`, holds the dicts they answer whole to `_RESUME_EXPANDED`, and holds every value of the three exports, outside the cycles, to a constant, a `str(...)` or a field whose type is a word, a number, a flag, None or a list of words. (3) D17 (5) is narrowed to `remedy job resume`, for the reason the context gives: its shapes lie off the live run, while each other operation's were read at its declaration and are reached live. Proving every operation's keys without a tree statically is not part of T001; it is not registered as a finding, because no key is known to hold an undeclared object.

ALTERNATIVES: Proving every operation's keys without a tree in this part, REJECTED: it would repeat by hand, for every operation, the reading each declaration already made, and grow this part past one round. Keeping D17 (5) as worded and taking the rest in later rounds, REJECTED: it would start a chain of deferred parts while T001's page part waits.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `_RESUME_PLAIN_SOURCES`, `_RESUME_EXPANDED`, `_plain_hint`, the plain keys test and the entry assertion from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`, and restore the two comments of `apps/cli/client_interface.py` and the page's sentence from `f27eac67a`; D17 (5) then stands as worded and is open.

## DECISION F298 D19 — T001's eighteenth part: whether an argument takes a value and may be repeated is read from the command line's parser, repairing R-1178; the page's rendering follows in its own round (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: Read at `c04575133`: `_argument_entry` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` answers an argument's `takes_value` as `not arg.is_flag` and its `repeatable` as `arg.is_repeatable`, from the catalog. The command line does not build its parser from those two fields alone: `_add_command_args` in `apps/cli/grouped.py` gives some options their own rules by name, so `--json`, `--approve`, `--dry-run`, `--no-ui`, `--stream-evidence` and `--no-stream-evidence` are switches that take no value whatever `is_flag` says, and `--verification-command` collects every occurrence whatever `is_repeatable` says. Measured over the fourteen client operations, twenty arguments answer `takes_value` wrongly and one answers `repeatable` wrongly; that is R-1178. The reviewer found it while preparing T001's last part, the page rendered from the interface, which would have printed the wrong values into the page.

CHOSEN: (1) The interface builds each operation's arguments with `_add_command_args` on a fresh parser and reads `takes_value` as whether the argument's action takes a value and `repeatable` as whether it collects every occurrence; `name`, `help`, `option` and `required` stay the catalog's, and `required` agrees with the parser for every client argument. (2) A test holds both fields of every argument to the actions of the parser `remedy` really runs, reached through `build_parser`, and a second test pins by name the switches and the collected options a client is most likely to build, `--approve` and `--json` first. (3) This repair is its own round, before the page is rendered, so that the first rendering of the page carries the parser's values; the rendering's design is the next round's DECISION, in the same round as its patch.

ALTERNATIVES: Setting `is_flag` and `is_repeatable` right in the catalog for the twenty-one arguments, REJECTED: the parser would still decide by name, so the catalog could drift from it again with no test to see it, while reading the parser's action makes the interface say what the command line does. Rendering the page first and repairing after, REJECTED: the page would carry twenty-one wrong values for a round.

HOW TO REVERSE: Restore `apps/cli/client_interface.py` and `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py` from `c04575133`, which deletes `_parser_actions`, `_command_parser_actions` and the switch test; R-1178 then stands open.

## DECISION F298 D20 — T001's page part: the machine client page's last section is the interface rendered between two markers, held to the code by its bytes and by reading it back; the walk through the path stays written by hand (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T001 asks that `docs/system/machine-client-contract-v1.md` be rendered from the interface and that a test fail when code and document differ. Read at `0c49b3234`: the page holds F295's walk through the path, with its order file, its four steps and four tables (commands, flags, JSON keys and exit codes) that `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py` holds equal to what the gate test uses, the decisions and the commands that answer them, and what Remedy never does; and a last section, "The interface as data", written by hand over eighteen rounds, describing `remedy client interface` in prose. The repository already generates one page, `docs/guides/environment.md`, by a render function in its source module, a write function beside it and a test that the committed bytes equal the rendering.

CHOSEN: (1) `render_client_interface_markdown` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` renders the interface `build_client_interface` returns as the section "The interface": the version, the envelope, every exit code with its meaning, the job states, mission status words, contract templates and budget kinds, and for every operation its command, id, description, a table of its arguments, its exit codes, refusal tokens and answer keys, and the keys under those keys as one bullet per key that holds keys; then the digest the same way. Keys are sorted, lists keep their order, a key whose keys are not fixed and a key that repeats the object holding it are marked in words. (2) The section stands between two markers on the page; `write_client_interface_page` replaces what lies between them and nothing else, and the section replaces the hand-written "The interface as data". (3) The walk through the path, its tables included, stays written by hand beside the rendering: it explains one path for a person, and F295's test already holds its tables to the gate test. (4) Three tests: the committed section equals the rendering of the interface the code builds; reading the committed section back line by line gives that interface again, every name, word, number and tree, so the page can neither name what the code does not return nor leave out what it does; and the writer replaces only the generated section. (5) The page's banner and the docs index say that the last section is generated.

ALTERNATIVES: Rendering the whole page, the walk included, as the environment guide does, REJECTED: the walk's prose and tables would move into strings in Python, which is still writing them by hand, only in a worse place. A command flag such as `remedy client interface --markdown`, REJECTED for now: it adds an argument to an operation the interface itself describes, while the page is written by the repository and read by people, and the write function needs no command. Holding only the bytes to the rendering, REJECTED: a renderer that drops a name would render a page that still equals its own output, so only reading the page back proves it names everything.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `render_client_interface_markdown`, `write_client_interface_page`, their helpers, the three page constants and the `pathlib` import from `apps/cli/client_interface.py` and restore its docstring from `0c49b3234`; delete the three page tests and their helpers from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; restore the page and `docs/README.md` from `0c49b3234`.

## DECISION F298 D21 — F298 closes at T001's scope; T002 to T007 move, word for word, to F304, registered directly after F298 and before F253 (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: Read at `346a7af1a`: F298 stands at 20 rounds in its fifth session, against the soft limit of 25 rounds or 7 sessions (operator amendment amend0827-process-diet rule 6). T001 is built: the interface, its tests and the page rendered from it (DECISIONs F298 D2 to D20). T002 to T007 are open. T001 alone took 20 rounds at the slow pace this session runs at, one proof per round. Five rounds remain before the limit, and the closure of a feature in SLOW MODE needs at least an acceptance audit round, up to three repair rounds, and the closure sequence's integration-gate and evidence rounds (operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap and `docs/roadmap/STATUS_closure_protocol.md`). T002 alone, an order run in its project's repository with refusals and a registering command, would run past the limit with the feature at no self-consistent scope. DECISION F298 D1 (6) names the split this would force: what remains moves to a feature placed directly behind this one and before F253.

CHOSEN: (1) The split-and-close default of operator amendment amend0905-throughput is executed now, at the seam where T001 is complete, and not at round 25 inside T002: F298 closes at T001's scope. (2) F304, "Machine client contract v1.1, part two: what a client can rely on", is registered as Tier 12 with T002 to T007, their Acceptance lines, the Goal & Done and the Do-not-touch copied word for word from F298's file, its STATUS line directly after F298's and before F253's, and `TOTAL_FEATURES`, the README total and the README's Tier 12 count raised by one in the same commit (operator amendment amend0906-split-placement). No open feature file names F298 in its "Depends on" line, so none gains F304. (3) F298's file gains a Built State that records T001, the split, and which Acceptance lines stay with F298: the line that a test fails when code and document differ, and the line that F295's gate test stays green, which F304 carries as well. (4) The next rounds are the hardening stage over F298's remaining statements, then the closure sequence. (5) The ruling changes the order of work the operator sees, so the handback commit records it in `.agent/operator_questions.md` as a ruling made and reversible (operator amendment amend0911-feedback rule C, kind B, and amend0917-throughput rule 5).

ALTERNATIVES: Starting T002 now and splitting at round 25, REJECTED: the limit would fall inside T002, the default could find no self-consistent scope, and the old hard stop with an operator question would remain. Splitting only T005 to T007 off, as D1 (6) first named, REJECTED: T002 to T004 do not fit in five rounds beside the hardening stage and the closure. Closing F298 at T001 with no follow-up feature, REJECTED: F253 cannot start without T002 to T004, and nothing would carry them.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `docs/roadmap/features/T12_F304.md`, F304's STATUS line and the pin's comment lines, lower `TOTAL_FEATURES`, the README total and the README's Tier 12 count by one, and delete the Built State paragraph from F298's file; F298 then continues with T002, and reaches its soft limit inside it.

CONTEXT: Operator amendment amend0930b-slow-cap rule (2) orders an acceptance audit by a fresh worker given only the feature file and the repository. Its one gap: the line that F295's gate test and its path are unchanged has no test that fails when the gate test changes. Of its observations, one says that nothing holds the operations the interface names to the commands and flags the gate test drives, so a client command the interface leaves out goes unseen.

Registering the `**dict(...)` observation, REJECTED: the claim it concerns is proved by the real run.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete `F295_GATE_TEST_SHA256`, the two tests, the `hashlib`, `_DEFAULT_COMMAND` and `_gate_names` imports and the docstring paragraph from `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; R-1179 and R-1180 then stand open.

CONTEXT: The first hosted CI run of pull request 315, run 37716986653 on `ad6081d74`, failed one node on Python 3.12 and none on Python 3.10, registered as R-1182.
