## DECISION F304 D2 — T002's first part: an order that names a project runs in that project's registered repository, and two refusals before any step; registering a repository for a client follows in its own round (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: F298's claim measurement (`.agent/f298_inventory.md`, "Where an order runs"), which DECISION F304 D1 kept: an order file naming `project: b`, started in repository `a`, filed its records under b and did its work in `a`; started in a folder that is no repository, it failed the init step. Read at `4eda924c5`: `_step_init` in `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py` takes its repository from the client's `--repo`, by default the current directory, and selects the named project only for the records; `_cmd_do` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` already uses that repository before any step, for the commit and push refusals and for the budget resolution; `do.run`'s `--repo` defaults to `.` in the catalog, so a typed `--repo .` cannot be told from none; a registered project carries `canonical_repo_path` and `repo_paths`; and `tests/cli/test_do_flags.py` pins `job.repo_path` to the client's own repository after `--project` named another, the defect itself.

CHOSEN: (1) `_cmd_do` resolves the repository right after reading the order file and before every other check, through one helper, `_order_repo`. Without a project, the repository is `--repo` or else the current directory, as before. With a project — from `--project` or else the order file's header — it is the project's `canonical_repo_path` when `--repo` is not given; a project with no registered repository is refused with `project_has_no_repo`, and a `--repo` whose top level is neither the project's canonical repository nor one of its `repo_paths` is refused with `repo_not_in_project`; both exit 2 and name the fix in their message. A selector that names no single project is left to the init step, which fails on it as before (DECISION F268 D16 (4)). (2) `do.run`'s `--repo` defaults to nothing in the catalog, and the handler passes it on as given, so a typed `--repo` is told from none; its help names the new default. (3) The two tokens join `OPERATION_REFUSAL_TOKENS["do.run"]` in the interface, the page's generated section is written again from it, and the page's hand-written order-file section states the rule and the two refusals. (4) `tests/cli/test_do_flags.py`'s pin now reads the named project's repository, and `tests/cli/test_do_project_repo.py` stands the order in repository `a`, in a folder that is no repository, with `--repo` naming `b` and naming `a`, and names a project without a repository. (5) T002's second sentence, one command that registers a repository for a client and leaves its working copy clean, is the next round's.

ALTERNATIVES: Refusing only a `--repo` registered to another project and running in an unregistered one, REJECTED: the order's records would then be filed under one project while its work happens in a repository no project owns, which is the defect this slice removes. Moving the choice into `_step_init`, REJECTED: the commit and push refusals and the budgets read the repository before any step. Refusing a selector that names no project before any step as well, REJECTED for this round: F268's pinned behaviour, an init step that fails with the project's name, is unchanged by the slice and has its own test.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the helper and its call, restore the catalog default `.` and the handler's `or "."`, the two tokens and the page's two sentences, and the old pin; the order then runs where the client stands again.

## DECISION F304 D3 — T002's second part: `remedy project register --repo <path>` registers a repository for a client and writes nothing `git status` shows; R-1183's repair lands first, in its own commit (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T002's last sentence asks for one command that registers a repository for a client and leaves its working copy clean. F298's claim measurement read `remedy init --json` in a clean repository leaving `.remedy/config.toml` and `remedy.toml` untracked. Read at `15dcffc1b`: `remedy init` registers only the repository it stands in and writes those two configuration files; `register_project_repo` in `packages/orchestration/project_registry.py` registers a repository or returns the project that already owns it, and takes the project's slug from the repository's folder name, never from the name it is given; `ensure_ignore_entry` writes Remedy's ignore entries to `.git/info/exclude`, which git does not track; `project.attach` and `project.attach-repo` need a project that already exists; the exit-code taxonomy gives 4 to a machine without a prerequisite "such as a git repository", which `remedy init` answers with `not_a_git_repo`. Every operation of the client interface declares its refusal tokens, its answer keys and an answer-tree entry, and `test_a_real_runs_answers_return_only_keys_the_interface_names` runs each operation once. R-1183 is registered by this round.

CHOSEN: (1) C2 repairs R-1183 alone: `project_has_no_repo` exits 3, `do.run` declares `exit_codes=(0, 1, 2, 3)`, the exit-code guide and the page say so, and the test asserts each refusal's code. (2) C3 adds `project.register`: `remedy project register --repo <path> [--json]` resolves the repository's top level, answers the project that already holds it with `created` false, or registers it as `remedy init` would, without `remedy init`'s two files, with `created` true, and adds the ignore entries `remedy init` adds; it answers `project_id`, `slug`, `repo_path` and `created`, all plain values, and refuses a path that is no git repository with `not_a_git_repo` and exit 4. There is no `--name`: the slug is the folder's name, which the answer carries. (3) The operation joins the interface first, before `do.run`, because a client registers before it orders; its tokens, keys and an empty answer tree join the tables, the real-run test calls it once, the guide lists it with 4, and the page's order-file section names it. (4) `tests/cli/test_project_register.py` proves the answer, an untouched working copy, a second call answering the same project, an order naming the registered project running in its repository, and a path that is no repository.

ALTERNATIVES: A flag on `remedy init` that skips its two files, REJECTED: `remedy init` registers only the folder it stands in, so a client would still change directory into each repository first. A `--name` option, REJECTED: `register_project_repo` ignores the name for the slug, so it would promise what it does not do. Exit 2 or 3 for a path that is no repository, REJECTED: the taxonomy names a missing git repository under 4, and `remedy init` answers the same case with 4.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the catalog entry, the handler, the interface's four entries, the guide's row, the page's sentence and the test file; for R-1183, restore exit 2 and the catalog line.

## DECISION F304 D4 — T003's first part: an approved apply that did not land is refused with one token per cause and exits non-zero; declining a result follows in its own round (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T003 asks that under `--approve --json` an apply that did not land answer `"ok": false` with one fixed error token per cause (the contract refuses the push, no upstream, a dirty tree, a detached `HEAD`, a merge conflict, protected files) and exit non-zero, while the preview without `--approve` keeps exit 0. Read at `ecfb19291`: `_cmd_job_apply` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` answers every apply with `emit_ok` and exit 0, whatever its status. `apply_job` in `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py` writes the cause into `blocked_reason` as a fixed prefix (`job_not_completed:`, `blocked_paths:`, `baseline_check_failed:` and others), and a refusal of the `--commit…` and `--push` flags as `commit_refused:`, `history_merge_refused:` or `push_refused:` followed by one sentence from `checkout_refusals`, `upstream_push_refusals`, `mission_push_refusals` or `_merge_job_branch`, the last of which fills `merge_conflicts` on a conflict; so a dirty tree and a detached `HEAD` share one prefix, and no upstream and the contract share another. `remedy do` calls the same refusal functions and prints their sentences. The tests that drove a blocked approved apply through the command line pinned exit 0, two of them with the comment "a blocked apply exits 0". The interface declared no refusal token for `job.apply`.

CHOSEN: (1) `apply_refusal(result)` in `job_apply.py` returns None for a preview, `--dry-run` included, and for status `applied`, and otherwise `(token, sentence)`, the token one of `APPLY_REFUSAL_TOKENS`: `target_dirty`, `target_detached_head`, `push_no_upstream` (no upstream, or an upstream that is a local branch), `push_refused_by_contract` (an unmet blocking criterion, or a contract that cannot be read), `merge_conflict` and `blocked_paths` (the fence's paths, which the prefix and `files_blocked` name) for the causes the slice names, and `job_not_found`, `job_not_ready`, `target_changed`, `commit_refused`, `history_merge_refused`, `push_refused`, `post_test_failed`, `push_failed` and `apply_failed` for the rest. The token names the first cause met, the one `blocked_reason` holds. The sentence-level causes are read from module constants that the refusal functions now build their sentences from, so the words and their reader cannot drift apart; every sentence is byte-identical to before, and `remedy do`'s output is unchanged. (2) `_cmd_job_apply` answers a refusal with `fail(token, sentence, ...)` carrying every key of `export_job_apply_json` beside the envelope, with exit 3 for `job_not_found` and `job_not_ready`, the taxonomy's "not ready", and exit 1 otherwise; the text answer prints the same summary as before and then exits with the same code. Only status `applied` answers `"ok": true`, so an apply whose files landed but whose post-test, push, cleanup or record failed is refused too. (3) Under `--approve`, flags that clash, a lone `--push` and an empty or two-line `--commit` are refused by `commit_flags_refusal` before the job is read, with `invalid_argument` and exit 2. A preview keeps its answer and exit 0. (4) `job.apply` declares exit codes 0 to 3 in the catalog and the guide, its tokens join the interface, the token reader's hand-verified entry for the handler is held equal to `APPLY_REFUSAL_TOKENS`, the page's step 4 says so, and its generated section is written again. (5) `tests/cli/test_job_apply_refusals.py` drives each cause the slice names through the command line, and a missing job, a clash, two previews and the text answer, and reads every token from a table of results; the pinned tests now read exit 1 or 2 and the token. (6) T003's second sentence, a command that declines a completed job's result, with a declined job and a job of an abandoned mission no longer waiting for its apply, is the next round's.

ALTERNATIVES: New fields on `JobApplyResult` set where each refusal is made, REJECTED for this round: the refusal functions return plain sentences that `remedy do` also prints, so each would change shape, and its callers with it; constants shared by a sentence and its reader give the same guarantee with the sentences unchanged. One token per reason prefix, REJECTED: a dirty tree and a detached `HEAD` share `commit_refused`, and no upstream and the contract share `push_refused`, which the slice asks to tell apart. A non-zero exit in the JSON answer only, REJECTED: an exit code belongs to the command, whatever its output form, as `fail` keeps it everywhere else. Refusing the clash in the preview as well, REJECTED: the slice keeps the preview's exit 0.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `apply_refusal`, its tokens and the constants (writing the sentences out again), restore `_cmd_job_apply`'s `emit_ok` for every apply, the catalog's default exit codes, the guide's row, the interface's empty tuple, the hand-verified entry and the page's sentences, and the tests' exit 0.

## DECISION F304 D5 — T003's second part: `remedy job decline <job> --reason <text>` records the operator's decline on the job, and a declined job or a job of an abandoned mission no longer waits for its apply (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T003's second sentence asks for one command that declines a completed job's result with a reason, recorded as the operator's decision the way the cockpit's door records one, and that a declined job, and a job of an abandoned mission, no longer wait for their apply; its Acceptance line asks that a declined job read `waits_for_apply` false, be absent from `awaiting_apply`, and have its decision in the job's ownership record. F298's claim measurement found no `decline` subcommand, and a completed job of an abandoned mission still waiting. Read at `f831e0a42`: `build_client_digest` in `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py` sets `waits_for_apply` from the job's state and `job_apply_landed` alone. The ownership ledger, `build_ownership_ledger` in `packages/orchestration/ownership.py`, reads every operator act from the record it is kept in, each with its actor's door (`cli`, or the browser's), its time and its words, and renders each through one sentence in `packages/orchestration/ownership_phrases.py`, whose actions `tests/ui_contracts/test_ownership_view_contract.py` holds equal to the cockpit's chip words in `apps/ui/src/api/ownership.ts`. A task decision's answer is kept in the job's own `metadata` and saved with `save_job_plan`, as `remedy decision resolve` does, and the door records `job.stop` with its `source`, `reason` and time.

CHOSEN: (1) `decline_job_result` in `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py`, the module that owns the apply's records, keeps the decline in the job's `metadata` under `result_decline` as `{"reason", "source", "declined_at"}`, written once; `job_result_decline` reads it. (2) The digest's `waits_for_apply` is false for a job carrying a decline, and for a job of a mission whose status is `abandoned`, read from the missions the digest already lists. (3) The ledger reads the decline as the action `result_declined`, with the door its `source` names, its time and its reason; the phrase catalog words it "declined the job's result; it was not applied", the cockpit's chip reads "Declined", and the golden ledger and its sentences carry it. (4) `remedy job decline <job> --reason <text> [--json]` (`job.decline`, handled in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` beside `job.apply`) records a decline with source `cli` and answers `job_id`, `reason`, `source`, `declined_at` and `already_declined`; a blank reason is refused with `missing_argument` and exit 2, a job that is not completed with `job_not_declinable` and exit 3, a job whose result landed with `job_already_applied` and exit 3, and a second decline answers the first unchanged. Nothing is applied, removed or reset. (5) The operation joins the interface after `job.apply`, with its tokens, its answer keys (the shared job-id resolver's `matches` among them) and an empty answer tree; the real-run test declines the job it applied and reads `job_already_applied`; the guide lists exit 3; the page's step 4 says so; its generated section is written again. (6) An apply of a declined job is not refused: the decline is the operator's word that the result is not wanted, and an operator who changes their mind applies it as before. (7) Because this round changes `apps/ui/src`, the closure's one full suite builds `apps/ui` first, so that no live server rebuilds a stale `dist` inside a test (checklist item 33's reading, recorded at F290's closure).

ALTERNATIVES: A run-log event `result_declined`, REJECTED: run-log event names are a published vocabulary (`packages/orchestration/event_names.py`), and the digest would read every job's run log to decide `waits_for_apply`, while the job's own record is read already. A browser door for the decline, REJECTED for this feature: the transport is F253's, and the record shape is the one a door would write. Marking an abandoned mission's completed jobs declined, REJECTED: an abandon is not the operator's word about each result, and the digest reads the mission's status directly. Refusing an apply after a decline, REJECTED: the slice asks that the job stop waiting, not that it be locked.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the catalog entry, the handler and its registration, the interface's entries, the guide's row, the page's sentences, the two digest conditions, the ledger reader and its phrase, the chip word and the golden lines, `decline_job_result`, `job_result_decline` and their tests; a decline already kept on a job then stays in its `metadata`, read by nothing.

## DECISION F304 D6 — T004's first part: one order file is run by one mission at a time; a second start is refused before any step with `order_already_running` and exit 2, naming the running mission, unless `--new-mission` (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T004 asks that a second start of one order file be refused before any step and name the mission that already runs it, unless a flag asks for a new mission; its Acceptance line asks that a second `remedy do` of an order file a running mission records exit 2 before any step. F298's claim measurement read two `--plan-only` starts of one order file both exit 0 and make two missions. Read at `9cf860628`: `_cmd_do` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` reads the order file and refuses an invalid invocation before any step, and `_step_plan` in `packages/orchestration/do_sequence.py` creates the mission and records the order file's resolved path and sha256 on it as its `MissionOrder`. A mission's status is `active`, `paused`, `achieved` or `abandoned`, and nothing moves a mission to `achieved` because its jobs finished, as `set_mission_status` in `packages/orchestration/mission_state.py` states. `--force-mission` asks for a mission of several jobs, not for a second mission, and `mission_for_job` in the same module scans every project's missions.

CHOSEN: (1) `running_mission_for_order_file(source_path)` in `mission_state.py` returns the newest mission whose recorded order file is that resolved path and whose status is neither `achieved` nor `abandoned` (`MISSION_ENDED_STATUSES`), read from every project; an empty path matches nothing, so a text order is never matched. (2) `_cmd_do`, after every other check that comes before the steps, refuses such an order file with `order_already_running`, exit 2 and the running mission's id under `mission_id`; the message names the mission, `remedy mission abandon <mission>` and `--new-mission`. (3) `do.run` gains the flag `--new-mission`, which starts another mission for the same order file. (4) The token joins the interface, the page's order-file section says so, and the generated section is written again. (5) The test that starts one order file twice to show a `--contract` flag winning over the header passes `--new-mission` on its second start; `tests/cli/test_do_order_file.py` proves the refusal, the flag, a restart after an abandon and another order file beside a running mission, and `tests/orchestration/test_mission_state.py` proves the lookup. (6) The second gate test, T004's other part, is the next round's.

ALTERNATIVES: Matching by the file's sha256, REJECTED: an order file edited between starts is still the same order file, and two files with the same bytes are two orders. Refusing only while a job of the mission runs, REJECTED: a mission waits between its jobs, for an answer or an apply, and a second mission started then is the duplicate the slice forbids. Ending a mission when its last job is applied, REJECTED: nothing moves a mission to `achieved` on its own, which `set_mission_status` states as a deliberate absence. Reusing `--force-mission`, REJECTED: it already means a mission of several jobs.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the check in `_cmd_do`, the flag, `running_mission_for_order_file` and `MISSION_ENDED_STATUSES`, the token, the page's sentence and the tests, and drop `--new-mission` from the contract test's second start.

## DECISION F304 D7 — T004's second part: the second gate test drives three paths through the command line alone, and R-1184 is registered and owned by F304 (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T004 asks for a second gate test that drives an order file to `remedy job apply <job> --approve --commit-with-history --push --json` against a local bare upstream and reads the commit, the branch and the push from the answer, drives an order of two jobs to its end as a program would, and starts one order file twice; the Acceptance lines ask that it be green through the command line alone with a stdin that fails the test on any read, and that F295's gate test and its path stay unchanged and green. Measured in the reviewer's dry run on `38a448c18`: in a scratch repository without a test, the planner's one blocking criterion, `C001`, a `pytest` check over `tests`, reads `unmet`, so the push is refused with `push_refused_by_contract`, as DECISION F304 D4 answers it; with one passing test in the repository the merge lands and the push reaches the bare upstream. An order run with `--force-mission` answers two jobs and `waiting_job_ids` naming the second; the second job runs on what the first committed, and `remedy job run <second>` without the client's builder and reviewer ends it `blocked` with `provider_unavailable`, because a job that never started has no builder or reviewer of its own, while its answer read `"ok": true` and exit 0 (R-1184). F295's `_remedy` in `tests/cli/test_machine_client_contract.py`, a file `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py` pins by its digest, runs each command in this process with a stdin that fails the test on any read.

CHOSEN: (1) `tests/cli/test_machine_client_paths.py` imports F295's `_remedy`, `_scratch_repo`, `_digest_job` and `_GIT_IDENTITY` and leaves that file untouched; its repository carries one passing test, so the planner's criterion is met as a client's real repository would meet it. (2) The first path merges a job with `--commit-with-history --push` against a bare upstream and reads `commit_sha`, `merge_commit`, `target_branch`, `pushed`, `push_remote` and `push_ref` from the answer, against the repository and the upstream. (3) The second path runs an order with `--force-mission`, applies and commits the first job with `--commit-auto`, runs the second with the client's own builder and reviewer, applies and commits it, and reads both jobs completed and nothing waiting in the digest. (4) The third path starts one order file twice and reads `order_already_running` with the first mission's id, one mission in the digest, and a second mission with `--new-mission`. (5) The page's status note names the new test. (6) R-1184 is registered and owned by F304, and its repair is the next round's, so this round changes no product code.

ALTERNATIVES: Extending F295's gate test file, REJECTED: its digest is pinned and the Acceptance line keeps it unchanged. A repository without a test, with the push refused, as the first path's end, REJECTED: T004 asks for an apply that commits and pushes, and the refusal is proved by `tests/cli/test_job_apply_refusals.py`. Repairing R-1184 in this round, REJECTED under SLOW MODE: it changes what `remedy job run` answers and needs its own rule for each end state, its own tokens and its own red-proofs.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the test file and the page's sentence; R-1184 stays registered.

## DECISION F304 D8 — R-1184's repair: `remedy job run` refuses a run that ended blocked, failed or stopped by its budget, with its report beside the token and exit 1; every end the client asked for answers as before (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: R-1184 (Medium, owned by F304): `remedy job run` answered `"ok": true` and exit 0 for a job that ended `blocked`. Read at `e430266a5`: `_cmd_job_run` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` answers the report `export_job_report` builds, whatever state `run_job` leaves the job in. `RunState` names `completed`, `paused`, `stopped`, `blocked`, `failed` and the states before a run; `run_job` writes `paused` when an operator pauses the job and when `--tasks` caps it, and `stopped` only through `_finalize_stop`, whose `stop_source` is `budget` for a budget stop and the door's word for an operator's stop. `CLI_EXIT_CODES` gives 0 to a command that did what it was asked, a pending stop request honoured included, and 1 to one that ran and did not. `remedy job resume` hands a job the engine has run to the same handler (DECISION F295 D13). Measured in the reviewer's dry run: a run of a job that does not exist ends `blocked` and answered exit 0 as well, and the tests that pinned exit 0 for a run ending blocked or at its budget include live tests of the veto and the task edit that drive a job to a blocked end on purpose; the live tests of the veto, the injection and the subtree rerun run with `--tasks 0` on purpose.

CHOSEN: (1) After the run, `_cmd_job_run` refuses an end the client did not ask for: a `stopped` job whose `stop_source` is `budget` with `job_stopped_by_budget`, a `blocked` job with `job_blocked` and a `failed` job with `job_failed`; each refusal carries every key of the report beside the envelope and exits 1, the taxonomy's "ran and did not do what was asked". (2) Every other end answers as before: `completed`, `paused` at the operator's request or at `--tasks`, and `stopped` at the operator's request. (3) The text answer prints the report as before, then the refusal's sentence on standard error, with the same exit code. (4) `job.run` and `job.resume` declare the three tokens, the page's step 3 says so, and the generated section is written again. (5) `tests/cli/test_job_run_end_states.py` drives a real run that blocks through the command line, and every end state through the handler with `run_job` standing in for the engine. The pinned tests now read exit 1: the budget-stop test of `tests/cli/test_do_sequence_cli.py` reads the token, the resume test of `tests/orchestration/test_job_worktree_handoff.py` and the signature test of `tests/orchestration/test_f018_authority_integration.py` expect the exit, and `tests/ui_server/test_task_edit_e2e_live.py` and `tests/ui_server/test_task_veto_e2e_live.py` read exit 1 and the blocked sentence for the runs they drive to a blocked end. (6) The handler reads `state`, `stop_source` and `error` with `getattr`, the way it already treats what `run_job` returns, because tests hand it a stand-in that carries only `job_id`; and `report` is bound by an expression that is no dict literal, so the interface's static reading still reaches its hand-verified keys.

ALTERNATIVES: Refusing every end but `completed`, REJECTED: a run capped by `--tasks`, paused or stopped by the operator did what was asked. A token for every end, with exit 0 for the ends asked for, REJECTED: a refusal envelope is `"ok": false`, and an end the client asked for is no refusal. Exit 3 for a blocked end, REJECTED: the job exists and was acted on, while 3 says the command could not act on what it was given.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the three refusals and their tokens, the page's sentence and the new test file, and restore the pinned tests' exit 0; R-1184 then reopens.

## DECISION F304 D9 — the operator confirms Q9 via remedy-answer: the client contract feature's early split stands (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: Operator question Q9 in `.agent/operator_questions.md`, written at F298 round 21 on 2026-10-08, reported that the feature making Remedy's promises to a program true and written down had seven parts, that the first part was finished and tested, that the feature had used twenty of its twenty-five working rounds, and that the session split it: the feature closes with the first part, and the other six parts move unchanged into a new feature placed directly after it and before the feature that serves Remedy over HTTP. Recommendation: keep the split, since the first part is a clean point to close and the new feature carries the rest word for word. The split was already executed as DECISION F298 D (the registration of F304, "Machine client contract v1.1, part two", at commit range around `28196`). The operator answered via remedy-answer, quoted in full: "Ok".

CHOSEN: the standing recommendation stands exactly as written and is now confirmed rather than merely defaulted-to: F298 stays closed at its first part, and F304 keeps T002 to T007 as the carried six parts, placed directly after F298 and before the HTTP feature.

ALTERNATIVES: none — the operator's answer confirms the standing recommendation without amendment.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph; the split would then again await operator confirmation.

## DECISION F304 D10 — T005's first part: each completed job in the digest carries an `approval_card` read from its record alone, with its changed files, its test command and its tasks; the mission's blocking criteria, the recommendation and risk words and the "no check ran" statement follow in their own round (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T005 asks that each completed job in the digest carry the files it changed (a count and a bounded list), each task with its title, its reviewer's verdict, its repair rounds and whether a test command ran and what it answered, the blocking criteria of its mission's contract with status and text, one recommendation word and one risk word derived by rules the contract document states, and that a job on which no check ran say so. F298's claim measurement (`.agent/f298_inventory.md`, "What a client can read") found nothing a client reads that says in one place what changed and which checks ran, and a job record whose `test_passed` was null and `test_command` empty. Read at `7fb75de02`: `build_client_digest` in `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py` gives each job its state, cost and evidence, and `DIGEST_KEY_TREE` in `apps/cli/client_interface.py` is held equal to the dict literals that module writes and to a real run's digest by `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`. A job's `TaskEntry` records `title`, `reviewer_verdict` (empty when no reviewer answered), `repair_rounds_used` and `test_passed`, which `pingpong_loop` leaves null when the job has no test command and sets true or false when it ran one; the job's test command is `execution_config.test_command`. `_reviewed_task_files` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py` is the sorted union of the files of every task manifest whose status is `applied`, in both isolation modes, the set the hand-off coverage check already treats as the reviewed work. Measured in the reviewer's dry run: `remedy do` with the fake providers completes a job whose one task reads verdict `pass` and one repair round, with `test_passed` null, and whose card names `docs/README.md`, the one path its result diff names. T007's bound is 65,536 bytes for the default digest of 1,000 settled jobs (DECISION F298 D1), so the file list is bounded from the start.

CHOSEN: (1) Every job in the digest carries `approval_card`, null unless its state is `completed`. (2) A card holds `changed_file_count`, every path of `_reviewed_task_files` counted; `changed_files`, the first `APPROVAL_CARD_FILE_LIMIT` (20) of those paths, sorted; `test_command`, the job's test command or null; and `tasks`, one entry per task in plan order with `task_id`, `title`, `reviewer_verdict` (null when empty), `repair_rounds_used`, `test_ran` (whether `test_passed` is not null) and `test_passed`. (3) Nothing on the card comes from a model or from a file outside the job's record. (4) The keys join `DIGEST_KEY_TREE`, the page's step 2 says what the card holds, and the generated section is written again. (5) `tests/orchestration/test_client_digest.py` proves the card from records, the bound and the null card of every other state; `tests/cli/test_status_cmd.py` reads a real fake run's card through the command line and holds its files to the job's result diff. (6) T005's second part, the next round's: the blocking criteria of the job's mission contract with status and text, the recommendation and risk words and the rules that derive them, stated in the page, and a card that says when no check ran.

ALTERNATIVES: The job's `root_changed_files` as the changed files, REJECTED: only a worktree-isolated job records them, while the applied manifests exist in both modes and are what the hand-off check holds the root diff to. Reading the result diff's file list, REJECTED: a read of a file outside the record for every completed job on each digest read, and a job without a diff would answer nothing. A card on every job, REJECTED: an approval is asked only of a completed job, and T007 has to keep the digest small. A separate key per task field at the job's top level, REJECTED: a client renders the card as one object. Landing the whole slice in one round, REJECTED under SLOW MODE: the two words need their own rules, tests and red-proofs.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `_approval_card`, `_card_task`, `APPROVAL_CARD_FILE_LIMIT` and the digest's key, the tree's entry, the page's sentence and the tests.

## DECISION F304 D11 — T005's second part, first half: the approval card carries the blocking criteria of the job's mission's contract with id, text and status, and `checks_ran`, false when no test ran and no gate evaluated a blocking criterion; the two words follow in their own round (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T005 asks that each completed job's card carry the blocking criteria of its mission's contract with status and text, and that a job on which no check ran say so; DECISION F304 D10 (6) left both, with the recommendation and risk words, to this part. Read at `61fa89d19`: `build_client_digest` already lists every project's missions and maps each job to its mission; a `Mission` carries its contract body, which `read_mission_contract` in `packages/orchestration/mission_contract.py` reads into a `MissionContract`, raising `ContractError` on a body that breaks a rule. A criterion carries `id`, `text`, `blocking` and `status`, one of `open`, `met` and `unmet`; `open` means no gate has evaluated it yet, as `mission_push_refusals` in `packages/orchestration/job_apply.py` states, and `contract_blockers` names the blocking criteria not `met`. A task's `test_passed` is null exactly when its test command did not run (`pingpong_loop`, DECISION F304 D10). Measured in the reviewer's dry run: `remedy do` with the fake providers in a repository without tests leaves the planner's one blocking criterion `C001`, "The mission goal is met in full: <order>", `unmet`, as `remedy do` answers it under `unmet_blocking_criteria`.

CHOSEN: (1) A completed job's card carries `blocking_criteria`, one entry per blocking criterion of its mission's contract, in contract order, each with `id`, `text` and `status`; empty when the job has no mission or the mission no contract; null when the contract cannot be read, in which case the digest is `degraded` and `skipped_files` names `contract of job <job_id>`, while the rest of the card stands. (2) The card carries `checks_ran`: true when a task's test command ran or a blocking criterion's status is `met` or `unmet`, false otherwise; a criterion that does not block is not on the card and does not count. (3) The digest maps each job to its mission object instead of its id, and reads the contract only for a completed job. (4) The keys join `DIGEST_KEY_TREE`, the page's step 2 says what they hold, and the generated section is written again. (5) `tests/orchestration/test_client_digest.py` proves the criteria and their order, a met and an unmet criterion counting as a check, open criteria and no test saying no check ran, a job without a mission, and an unreadable contract; `tests/cli/test_status_cmd.py` reads a real fake run's criterion through the command line and holds it to `remedy do`'s answer. (6) The recommendation word, the risk word and the rules that derive them, stated in the page, are the next round's.

ALTERNATIVES: Only the blockers `contract_blockers` names, REJECTED: the slice asks for the blocking criteria with their status, and a met criterion is what a client needs to see as well. Counting a criterion that does not block as a check, REJECTED: it is not on the card, so a client could not see why the card says a check ran. Refusing the whole digest, or dropping the card, on an unreadable contract, REJECTED: the digest names a read that failed and nulls only its value, as it does for a cost. All three in one round, REJECTED under SLOW MODE.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `_mission_blocking_criteria`, the card's two keys, the contract read and its degraded name, the tree's two entries, the page's sentence and the tests, and map jobs to mission ids again.

## DECISION F304 D12 — T005's last part: the approval card ends with one recommendation word, `apply`, `review` or `hold`, and one risk word, `low`, `medium` or `high`, each derived from the card's own facts by rules the page states and the interface names (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T005 asks that each completed job's card carry one recommendation word and one risk word, that the rules deriving them from recorded facts stand in the contract document, and that no word come from a model; DECISIONs F304 D10 and D11 put every fact on the card. Read at `049787eb1`: a task's reviewer verdict is one of `pass`, `needs_repair`, `fail` and `blocked`, or empty when no reviewer answered (`validate_reviewer_output` in `packages/orchestration/pingpong_loop.py`); a push is refused while a blocking criterion is `unmet` and not while it is `open` (`mission_push_refusals`); the interface names every word a client meets in its "Words" section, built by `build_client_interface` and read back from the page by `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`; DECISION F304 D1 (2) asks that a word join the interface in the round that adds it. Measured in the reviewer's dry run: the fake run's card reads verdict `pass`, one repair round, no test and `C001` `unmet`.

CHOSEN: (1) `recommendation` is `hold` when a record says no: a test that ran and failed, a reviewer's verdict other than `pass`, or an `unmet` blocking criterion; else `review` when something is unverified: no check ran, a task without a reviewer's verdict, a blocking criterion still `open`, or a contract that cannot be read; else `apply`. (2) `risk` is `high` when no check ran or more files changed than the card names (`APPROVAL_CARD_FILE_LIMIT`, 20); else `medium` when a task took a repair round or more than `APPROVAL_LOW_RISK_FILE_LIMIT` (5) files changed; else `low`. (3) The words are `APPROVAL_RECOMMENDATIONS` and `APPROVAL_RISKS` in `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py`, and `_card_recommendation` and `_card_risk` apply the rules to the card's own entries, so a client can recompute each word from the card. (4) The interface answers `approval_recommendations` and `approval_risks`, its page lists them under "Words", the page's step 2 states both rules with the code's limits, and `tests/orchestration/test_client_digest.py` holds that sentence to the constants. (5) The rule tables prove every clause and both limits; the command-line test reads `hold` and `medium` from the fake run's card. (6) T005 is complete; T006 is next.

ALTERNATIVES: A numeric score, REJECTED: the slice asks for one word each, and a word a client can recompute from stated rules is a promise a score is not. Risk from the recommendation, REJECTED: the two answer different questions, whether to apply and how much an approval stakes, and a held result can still be small. Leaving the words out of the interface and naming them only in the page's prose, REJECTED: DECISION F304 D1 (2) and T001's "every state word" ask that the generated document name them. `decline` as a recommendation, REJECTED: declining is the operator's act, and `hold` already says the records speak against an apply.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the two functions, the three constants and the card's two keys, the interface's two keys, its answer keys, its two "Words" lines and the tests' entries, and the page's rule sentences.

## DECISION F304 D13 — T006's first part: each job in the digest carries `calls` and `tokens` by kind beside its `cost`, and each project's `cost_today` carries `tokens` beside its `calls`, read from the project cost ledgers; the order's cap and the token budget's sentence follow in their own rounds (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T006 asks that each job in the digest and each project's day carry the provider calls and the tokens the records hold, by kind (input, output, cache read, and cache creation where a provider reports it), beside the existing `cost`; that an order's mandatory cap may be any one job budget; and that the document say exactly which tokens the token budget counts. F298's claim measurement found a digest job's `cost` with no token and no call, and a job record with no key naming either. Read at `59687dfe7`: `remedy do` and `remedy job run` mirror every finished job's evidence into the cost ledger of the project its repository resolves to (`mirror_job_run_into_ledger` in `packages/orchestration/job_evidence.py`), one row per provider call keyed by the job's id, with `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cache_read` and `cache_write`, each null when the provider reported none; `query_cost` in `packages/orchestration/token_ledger.py` sums them with nulls kept, and `project_cost_of_day` in `packages/orchestration/project_cockpit.py` reads one UTC day of it into `cost_today`, a shape the cockpit's browser decoder pins by its keys (`tests/ui_contracts/test_project_scope_door.py`). `COST_GROUP_KEYS` is also the choice list of `remedy stats cost --by`. Measured in the reviewer's dry run: a fake `remedy do` leaves 4 ledger rows for its job, every token null, because the fake provider reports no usage.

CHOSEN: (1) `ledger_usage_by_job(project_id=...)` in `token_ledger.py` reads one project's ledger once, grouped by job id, with the same aggregation and nulls as `query_cost`; rows without a job id are left out, and a missing ledger reads empty and is never created. `COST_GROUP_KEYS` is untouched, so `remedy stats cost --by` gains no choice. (2) `build_client_digest` reads every registered project's ledger that way and adds a job's rows found in two ledgers, a figure neither reported staying null. Each job carries `calls`, its rows' count, 0 when no ledger names it, and null when a ledger could not be read, in which case the digest is degraded and names `calls and tokens of the jobs of project <project_id>`; and `tokens`, `input`, `output`, `cache_read` and `cache_creation`, each the ledger's sum or null when no call reported it. (3) `cost_today` gains `tokens` for the same UTC day, read by the digest itself, so `project_cost_of_day` and the cockpit's shape are unchanged. (4) The keys join `DIGEST_KEY_TREE` through one `TOKENS_BY_KIND_KEY_TREE`, the page's step 2 says what they hold, and the generated section is written again. (5) `tests/orchestration/test_client_digest.py` proves the kinds, the sums, the nulls, a job no ledger names, two ledgers and an unreadable ledger; `tests/orchestration/test_token_ledger.py` proves the grouped read; `tests/cli/test_status_cmd.py` reads a real fake run's 4 calls and null tokens through the command line and holds the count to `query_cost`. (6) T006's next part is the order's cap by any one job budget, and its last the page's sentence on which tokens the token budget counts, with the Acceptance line's order capped only by calls or by total tokens.

ALTERNATIVES: The job's budget actuals as the source, REJECTED: they hold one `total_tokens` without cache tokens and no kind, while the slice asks for tokens by kind. One `query_cost` per job, REJECTED: one ledger open per job on every digest read. Adding `job` to `COST_GROUP_KEYS`, REJECTED: it would add a choice to `remedy stats cost --by` that no slice asks for. Changing `project_cost_of_day`, REJECTED: its shape is pinned by the cockpit's decoder, which needs no tokens. Calls and tokens inside `cost`, REJECTED: `cost` comes from the job's budget actuals and is null when they are damaged, while calls and tokens come from the ledger and fail on their own.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `ledger_usage_by_job` and its test, the digest's ledger read, its helpers and its two job keys and one day key, the tree's entries, the page's sentence and the tests.

## DECISION F304 D14 — T006's second part: an order file's mandatory cap may be any one of the four job budgets, from its header or its flag; the refusal keeps its token `order_file_no_cost_cap` and names all four (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T006 asks that an order's mandatory cap may be any one of the job budgets — cost, total tokens, provider calls or wall-clock minutes — and that an order with none be refused as today. Read at `2494ac701`: `ORDER_FILE_HEADER_KEYS` in `packages/orchestration/order_file.py` holds `project`, `contract`, `max-cost-usd` and `constraint`, and `_cmd_do` in `apps/cli/commands/do_cmd.py` refuses an order file when neither `--max-cost-usd` nor the header's `max-cost-usd` is set, with `order_file_no_cost_cap` and exit 2, then hands every budget flag on to the run, where `--max-total-tokens`, `--max-provider-calls` and `--max-wall-clock-minutes` already set the job's budgets and a value that is no number is refused as `invalid_budget`. The client interface's refusal tokens only grow inside a major version. Measured in the reviewer's dry run: a header carrying only one of the three other caps was refused before this change, and after it runs to its end with that budget recorded on the job and `max_cost_usd` null; `max-provider-calls: many` is refused as `invalid_budget` with exit 2 before any mission is filed.

CHOSEN: (1) The header gains the keys `max-total-tokens`, `max-provider-calls` and `max-wall-clock-minutes`, each single-valued and meaning the flag of the same name, collected with `max-cost-usd` as `ORDER_FILE_CAP_KEYS`; `OrderFile` carries the three new values. (2) `_cmd_do` fills each budget flag the client did not give from the header, then refuses an order file only when all four caps are absent; a flag still wins over the header. (3) The refusal keeps the token `order_file_no_cost_cap`, because the interface only grows inside a major version, and its sentence names the four header keys and the four flags; the page says the token keeps its old name. (4) The page's order-file section names the four caps and the rule. (5) `tests/orchestration/test_order_file.py` reads every key and refuses a repeated cap; `tests/cli/test_do_order_file.py` runs an order capped only by each of the three, proves the flag alone and the flag winning, the refusal's sentence, and a cap that is no number. (6) T006's last part, the next round's, states on the page exactly which tokens the token budget counts and proves that an order capped only by provider calls or by total tokens is stopped at its cap.

ALTERNATIVES: A new token `order_file_no_cap` with the old one retired, REJECTED: a removed token is a change of major version, and the handler would declare a token it can no longer reach. Counting `deadline` as a cap, REJECTED: the slice names the four budgets, and a deadline alone does not bound what a run spends. Refusing a header that names two caps, REJECTED: several budgets on one job are what the flags already allow.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the three header keys and `OrderFile` fields, the handler's three fills and its four-cap check, restoring the cost-only check and sentence, the page's sentences and the tests.

## DECISION F304 D15 — T006's last part: the call and token budgets stay as they count today, the page says what they count, and a test provider that reports usage proves that an order capped only by calls or by tokens is stopped at its cap (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T006 asks that the document say exactly which tokens the token budget counts, and its Acceptance line that an order capped only by provider calls or by total tokens is accepted and stopped at its cap, and that the digest name calls and tokens by kind for a job run with a provider that reports them. DECISION F304 D14 made such an order acceptable. Read at `f66e5638c`: `_on_provider_call` in `run_job` (`packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py`) returns before counting anything for an attempt whose provider is `fake`; for every other attempt it adds one call, and the input and output tokens of its `usage_actuals`, leaving `cache_read` and `cache_creation` out, as `_aggregate_usage_actuals` in `pingpong_loop.py` does. `_call_with_retry` hands every attempt, a retry included, to that counter (`TestOnProviderAttemptCallback::test_callback_fires_on_retry` in `tests/orchestration/test_job_budgets.py`). `evaluate_budget` in `budget_guard.py` reaches a cap at `count >= cap`, and the run checks it before each builder and reviewer call. The cost ledger still holds a row for each fake call, which is what the digest's `calls` counts (DECISION F304 D13). Measured in the reviewer's dry run, with a stand-in for `ollama` that is the fake builder and reviewer reporting 10 input, 5 output, 1,000 cache-read and 200 cache-creation tokens per call: `max-provider-calls: 2` and `max-total-tokens: 20` each end `stopped` after two calls with 30 tokens counted, exit 1, `step_failed`; with `max-cost-usd: 1` the job completes after four calls and the digest reads `calls` 4 and tokens 40, 20, 4,000 and 800.

CHOSEN: (1) No production code changes: the call budget counts every builder and reviewer call to a provider other than the fake one, a retry included; the token budget counts the input and output tokens those calls report and never cache tokens; a call that reports no tokens adds none; both are checked before each call, so the last call can carry a run past a token cap. (2) The page's order-file section says so in one paragraph, including that the fake provider's calls count toward neither cap although the digest's `calls` counts them. (3) `tests/cli/test_do_order_file.py` gains `_UsageReportingProvider`, the fake provider reporting fixed usage, which a fixture installs for the provider name `ollama` through `pingpong_loop.create_provider`, the seam the live cockpit tests already replace; no model runs and the model-call tripwire stays. Its tests run an order capped only by calls and one capped only by tokens to their stop after two calls, read the digest's calls and tokens by kind for a completed run and hold its `calls` to the cost ledger and the job's budget actuals, and hold the page's sentences. (4) T006 is complete; T007 is next.

ALTERNATIVES: Counting the fake provider's calls toward the call budget, REJECTED: a fake call spends nothing, and the budget and the cost evidence both treat it as no provider call at all, so the rule would change for every real job to suit a test. A provider name of its own for a fake that reports usage, REJECTED: it would add a choice to `--builder-provider` that no user needs. Counting cache tokens toward the token budget, REJECTED: not asked for, and it would change every running job's budget behind its back; the page states the rule instead. Proving the stop with `run_job` alone, REJECTED: the Acceptance line speaks of an order, so the proof goes through `remedy do`.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, the page's paragraph and section 14 of `tests/cli/test_do_order_file.py` with its import and docstring sentences.

## DECISION F304 D16 — T007's first part: the digest lists every job that still needs something and the 20 ended jobs that ended last, names that window and how many ended jobs it left out, and `remedy status --all-ended-jobs` widens it to every ended job (2026-10-08)

CONTEXT: T007 asks that by default the digest list every job that still needs something and the jobs that ended inside a window, name the window and how many jobs it left out, and that a flag widen it, the first round measuring the operator's own data root; the Acceptance line asks that with 1,000 settled jobs on a scratch data root the default digest stay under a size the first round fixes and name the count it left out, and DECISION F298 D1 fixed that size at 65,536 bytes. Read at `5eabb4059`: `build_client_digest` in `packages/orchestration/client_digest.py` lists every job on the data root; `JOB_TERMINAL_STATES` in `pingpong_job.py` holds `completed`, `failed` and `cancelled`, the states a job never runs again from, while `blocked`, `stopped`, `paused` and `planned` keep pending work; a job's record carries `finished_at`, empty when no finish was recorded, and `created_at`. `remedy status` always exits 0 and its catalog entry takes no value but the scope. Measured, read only, on the operator's own data root at `/home/decodeux/Repos/remedy/.data` (`.remedy-wt/f304-r15/measure-root.txt`): 11,653 jobs, 13,481 open decisions, 1,123 jobs awaiting an apply and a digest of 10,243,731 bytes, of which 5,714,354 are the jobs and 4,418,503 the decisions; 11,476 of the jobs have an open decision, the other 177 are `planned`, and all but a handful are 15 to 32 days old, so no job there has ended in the sense below and the window leaves none of them out (the digest built by this round's code over the same root: 10,239,214 bytes, `left_out` 0). Measured on a scratch root of 1,000 completed jobs whose results were declined, each card naming 25 changed files (`.remedy-wt/f304-r15/size-readings.txt`): every job listed, 1,184,252 bytes; this round's default, 23,932 bytes for 20 jobs of 1,182 bytes each.

CHOSEN: (1) A job has ENDED when its state is terminal (`job_is_terminal`), it does not wait for its apply and none of its decisions is open; a job whose decisions could not be read has not ended. Every other job still needs something and is always listed. (2) The window is a count, `CLIENT_DIGEST_ENDED_JOB_LIMIT` (20): the ended jobs listed are those that ended last, by `finished_at`, or `created_at` when the record holds no finish, the job id breaking a tie; `jobs` stays sorted by job id. (3) The digest gains `job_window`, with `ended_limit`, the limit or null, and `left_out`, how many ended jobs it did not list. (4) `remedy status --all-ended-jobs`, a flag of the JSON answer's digest that the text overview does not read, lists every ended job and reads `ended_limit` null; `build_client_digest` takes it as `every_ended_job`. (5) The key joins `DIGEST_KEY_TREE`, the flag the catalog, the page's step 2 says what `jobs` holds and what has ended, and the generated section is written again. (6) `tests/orchestration/test_client_digest.py` proves the order, the creation fallback, every kind of job that still needs something, the flag and an unreadable job, and holds the page's sentence to the constant; `tests/cli/test_status_cmd.py` proves through the command line that 1,000 settled jobs give a default digest under 65,536 bytes with `left_out` 980, and that the flag lists every one. (7) The template question of T007 is the next round's.

ALTERNATIVES: A window of time, the jobs that ended in the last day, REJECTED: 1,000 jobs that ended within it would all be listed, about 1.2 MB, so no time window keeps the Acceptance line's bound. A time window with a count cap, REJECTED: two limits to name where one bounds the size. A flag taking a number, REJECTED: a value that is no number needs a refusal on a command that always exits 0, and the slice asks only that a flag widen the window. Leaving out old jobs that still need something, REJECTED: the slice lists every one; the operator's own root stays large because its records still hold 13,481 open decisions, which is a matter for those decisions and not for the digest's rule.

HOW TO REVERSE: Delete this paragraph, `CLIENT_DIGEST_ENDED_JOB_LIMIT`, `_job_ended`, `_ended_at`, the selection and `job_window` in `build_client_digest` and its `every_ended_job` argument, the catalog's flag and the handler's argument, the tree's entry, the page's sentences and the tests, and restore the pinned call in `tests/cli/test_client_interface.py`.
